Two complete technical readings produced two reusable deductions. No
publication, external validation, or global resolution of the assigned
conjectures is claimed. All sources are pinned to OpenAI/math commit
`adc7f1241b42e322a6451854ab7e4b4c146bf78a` (commit timestamp
2026-10-06T21:58:50Z in the shared commit record). No nested workers,
untrusted build-script execution, paid services, contacts, or commits
were used.
The root dispatch record identifies this new worker's configuration as
`gpt-6.1-sol`, reasoning effort `max`, with no model fallback.

The strongest result is the extracted Schatten-3 triangle certificate.
The entire dyadic triangular manuscript (October 5, 2026) was read and
its finite matrix, conditional-child, total-energy, telescoping and
density steps reconstructed. The same proof extends its constant 40
to every base q≥2, complex L³ inputs, and arbitrary real child-constant
mean-zero multipliers bounded by one. The q-independent step is a
two-way Jensen rounding of the q-way partition. The complex phase
mechanism also appears in the annular companion's matrix section,
which was subsequently read in full; that part is not a new priority
claim. The q-uniform extension is a deduction of the release mechanism,
with broader novelty unresolved.

Pairwise independence of child coordinates is essential. Uniform
marginals alone permit an exact 2×2 example with local trace −1/8 and
energy gap 3/4−√2<0. This records a concrete obstruction to transferring
the dyadic proof to arbitrary correlated or geometric refinements.

The second result is a generalized capacity decomposition. The entire
diagonal restriction manuscript (September 24, 2026) was read. Its
Lemma 3.2 extends to any positive-density exponent r>1: for n weighted
atoms and a legal geometric test capacity, there are at most
`min(n,2+floor((1+1/(r−1))log₂ n))` disjoint coordinate pieces with

```
Σ_j m(u^j)K(u^j)^{r−1}

```

The bound has no dependence on coefficient dynamic range. If weights
are squared complex coefficients and the oscillatory map is linear,
the output norm power is 2r and the resulting grouping loss is
J^{2r−1}; r=3/2 reproduces the source's log² loss. The capacity oracle's
acquisition cost remains separate from the logarithmic piece count.

the sphere packet propagation Theorem 6.4 and the 3D Kakeya maximal
Theorem 1.1. I read the exact packet interface and targeted portions of
its extremal/time-profile argument. At the pinned version the packet

advertised legal domain; an objection based solely on sphere-only
labels would be incorrect. The complete underlying geometric
propagation and refined quartic packet estimates were not independently
checked. The strict restriction conclusion also supplies no p=3
endpoint and no polynomial bound on its full constant as p↓3, because
packet/Kakeya loss-constant growth is unspecified.

The characteristic-zero source proof survives an independent reconstruction of monodromy, field transfer, formula/ABP conversion, Wronskian/minor multiplicity, and rational bit bounds. This is internal proof review, with no fresh Lean build or external validation. The Lean scope document asserts universal detection but excludes the quantitative construction/dimension statements from its selected theorem.

The strongest new deduction uses **full evaluated matrices**. The source's explicit Volterra tuple at dimension `2nm` hits every nonzero polynomial with an acyclic `m`-state coefficient realization, improving its quadratic first-column dimension to linear full-response dimension. Thus dimension `4ns` suffices for the source's size-`s` formula trees. The proof reconstructs a nonzero bivariate Volterra kernel, bounds a diagonal derivative by rational row-span closure, and recovers its first homogeneous part with invertible Cauchy moments. It uses the source's finite-word faithfulness, but does not use the scalar Moura bound. Root, experiments, analysis and crossfield independently reconstructed the core argument. These internal audits are not external validation; historical novelty remains UNKNOWN.

For arbitrary proper cyclic `m`-state recognizable series, the fixed **m-point scalar grid** `ell T_i`, `ell=1,...,m`, each at dimension `2nm`, hits every nonzero series. The derivative numerator is divisible by the length marker lambda, and after division has lambda-degree at most `m-1`; a nonzero coefficient therefore survives some grid point. Specialization does not use rational row-dependence coefficients. Alternatively, a single nilpotent marker tuple has dimension `2nm(m+1)`, or the grid direct sum has dimension `2nm^2`. Every query is jointly nilpotent and defined under proper-series semantics.

The exact output-only residual learner must retain all matrix entries. Full-width prefix chains and the scalar grid recover a minimal `r<=m` weighted automaton using at most `m(1+nr)` exact queries of dimension at most `2nm(r+1)`, feature length `4n^2m^3`, plus polynomial exact field work. Residual combinations share hidden transitions, so `m` suffices; comparison with an unrelated m-state hypothesis instead needs `2m`. A conservative `2m` learner has at most `2m(1+nr)` queries, dimension at most `4nm(r+1)`, feature length `32n^2m^3`. Individual scalar-seed queries offer a different matrix-size/query-count tradeoff, fully ledgered but not implemented here. All full responses, description sizes, response heights and oracle work are charged. There is no coefficient-bit bound from `n,m` alone.

The independent proof, alias and complete ledger are in `notes/frontier_check_hitting/cycle19/FULL_MATRIX_VOLterra_AND_CYCLIC_ALIAS.md`. This divergence is minimal among laws satisfying those marginal and event-mass constraints. An adaptive assay revealing at most k distinct coordinates from each fresh specimen has identical transcript laws under P0 and P*, even with unlimited specimens. A separate positive regime assumes known product structure and explicit polynomial-size DNF failure modes and composes established product-estimation/weighted-witness methods.

The negative pair is indistinguishable from supplied low-order marginals; the assay reveals at most k distinct coordinates per fresh specimen. The positive product/DNF regime charges measurements and arithmetic and uses known methods.

The adjoint action-compatible transfer is (A_P z)_i=integral pi(g)^(-1)(sum_j P_g(i,j)z_j)dg and has norm at most kappa_m(pi).

Let K_D={A_rho=(rho-I/D)/r_0: rho>=0, Tr(rho)=1}. For fixed D, 0<delta<=1/n and 0<epsilon<delta/(2n), the minimum number of classical Markov states that uniformly approximates all preparations, terminal queries, and words of length at most T is Theta_(D,delta,epsilon)(T^(D-1)). The static positive factorization size is exactly D^2; the quantum realization uses Hilbert-space dimension D; the state-count law corresponds to (D-1)log_2 T+O_(D,delta,epsilon)(1) classical bits.
Interface: The preparation rho=I/D+r_0 A ranges over all density matrices; B ranges over the Hilbert-Schmidt unit ball; controls are arbitrary supplied unitary words; the binary effect is E_B=1/2(I+delta B/r_0). The classical simulator must meet uniform additive error epsilon for all inputs and all word lengths <=T, with arbitrary measurable time/current-unitary stochastic transitions. Only the finite internal state stores history; no persistent seed, correlated external noise or stored continuous state is free.
Proof spine: For independent Haar unitaries, unnormalized conditional means contract by kappa_(m,D). A uniform small-ball bound for every unit traceless-Hermitian conjugation orbit follows by selecting a nontrivial eigenvalue gap and comparing nearby conjugates to complex Grassmannian projection balls. This yields 1-kappa_(m,D)=Theta_D(m^(-1/(D-1))) without claiming equality of repeated powers. A bounded terminal score gives the Omega(T^(D-1)) state lower bound. A projective net and an inflated convex polytope with barycentric stochastic updates give O(T^(D-1)); a regular simplex proves the separate exact D^2 static factorization size.
Costs: Fixed-D asymptotic state count only. The theorem does not bound the size or precision of the transition maps, construction of projective nets/polytope triangulations, barycentric evaluation, sampling, gate compilation or runtime. It is not a general computational quantum speedup and is not uniform jointly in D,T,delta,epsilon.
Failure: No sharp state law is established for the fixed five-gate qubit alphabet in N546. No lower bound follows for an unrestricted floating-point simulator unless all persistent numerical state is charged. The source explicitly does not assert R_T=kappa_(m,D)^T.
Closest comparator: The source identifies Montina 2008/2010 and correlated-noise models as important predecessors; detailed comparison with those full papers and the 2026 finite-memory preprint is incomplete. No priority claim is made. N507 is unreviewed context only, not an imported theorem.
Open verification: Independently audit the Grassmann small-ball and eigenvalue-gap argument, the weak-effect and uniform-score contracts, both asymptotic bounds, and the exact static rank argument. Then complete the prior-art review.

The finite-group exact realization uses the group translates of a circumscribed simplex. These facts limit direct use of the continuous-Haar exponent.

Claim: Let the same smooth unknown drift b and constant symmetric D≻0 govern controlled diffusions on R^d with vanishing boundary flux/integrability, or on a flat torus. Under known smooth controls u_i, strictly positive stationary C² densities p_i and divergence-free currents J_i=(b+u_i)p_i−D∇p_i, set r=p_i/p_j, w=∇log r and δu=u_i−u_j. For every admissible scalar q for which the integrations are justified, the source derives D:E_{p_i}[q(r)wwᵀ]=E_{p_i}[q(r)δu·w]. Thus full rank of the collected symmetric matrix features M_{ij,q}=E_{p_i}[q(r)wwᵀ], in dimension d(d+1)/2, identifies the constant D uniquely.
Interface: All regimes share b and constant state-independent D; intervention fields are known; stationary laws are exact and fully observed for the theorem. The feature-rank condition is a hypothesis to check, not a consequence of having multiple regimes. The test-function class for q and the required boundary/integrability conditions are not fully enumerated in the source.
Proof spine: Use J_i=rJ_j+p_i(δu−Dw). Choose f with f′(r)=q(r)/r, multiply the stationary divergence equation by f(r), cancel the J_j term as a gradient against a divergence-free current, and integrate the remaining divergence by parts. The resulting identity is linear in the symmetric entries of D.
Costs: No finite-sample or numerical acquisition bound. The features require density-ratio gradients and stationary expectations; acquiring or estimating these, waiting for each regime to mix, and calibrating controls are uncharged. An algebraic perturbation bound is conditional on the exact design singular value and feature errors.
Failure: Rank deficiency prevents unique D recovery; two-regime weighted features can be ill-conditioned despite full rank. The exact identity does not supply a statistical estimator for general smooth densities or a physical snapshot-acquisition protocol.
Closest comparator: Fokker–Planck inversion and weak-form/Stein generator identities have established prior work. The source reports a partial literature check and leaves the exact weighted current-cancellation identity priority UNKNOWN.

Claim: Let s_i=∇log p_i and T_i=∇²p_i/p_i for d+1 controlled experiments, and define W(x)=[s_1−s_0,…,s_d−s_0]. For i=1,…,d define h_i=D:(T_i−T_0)−∇·u_i−u_i·s_i+∇·u_0+u_0·s_0. Under the source’s smoothness and exact-law assumptions, if the pairwise matrix features identify constant D and W(x) is invertible almost everywhere, subtracting stationary Fokker–Planck equations identifies b(x)=W(x)^{−T}h(x) almost everywhere. Conversely, for a compatible pair of positive stationary densities on T², known D and controls do not identify general b: adding v(x)=p_0(x)^{−1}S∇(p_1/p_0), for a nonzero constant skew matrix S, preserves both stationary laws but changes their currents.
Interface: The sufficient theorem assumes full-state, exactly known positive stationary densities, common smooth b, constant D, known controls, full rank in the D-feature system and almost-everywhere pointwise rank of W. The counterexample is on the flat two-dimensional torus and retains the same D and controls. Neither statement is a finite-sample result.
Proof spine: Subtract the stationary Fokker–Planck equations to obtain d linear equations in b(x); invert W wherever it has full rank. For the obstruction, p_0v=S∇r has zero divergence, and p_1v=rS∇r also has zero divergence because S is skew and Hessians are symmetric.
Costs: The nonparametric formula uses density scores, second derivatives, pointwise matrix inversion and conditioning. Statistical error, regularization, regions where W is nearly singular, mixing, finite samples and partial observation have no guarantee.
Failure: A singular or poorly conditioned W prevents stable drift recovery. The two-regime gauge refutes unrestricted full-drift identification from those two laws, but it does not refute recovery of D or the d+1 rank-conditional theorem. A radial or latent projection does not satisfy the full-state interface.
Closest comparator: The source cites prior Fokker–Planck algebra and intervention-identifiability work; no complete proof-level priority audit is reported. N498 is a useful projection-loss contrast, not a theorem premise.
Open verification: Independently verify the almost-everywhere uniqueness statement and the two-law gauge for the declared boundary conditions; quantify what changes under partial observation or noisy estimated scores.

Thus an arbitrary nonlinear log p_0 is allowed within this exact-tilt family and the circulation can be nonzero. Fewer than d independent tilt directions cannot guarantee full generator identification in the worst case within the family.

title: Unbounded mixed-state families allow near-perfect marginal broadcasting with maximal EB and commuting error
text:
N552-mixed-family-approximate-broadcasting-maximal-instability | Unbounded mixed-state families allow near-perfect marginal broadcasting with maximal EB and commuting error
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The attached source supplies a self-contained analytic argument and author-internal algebraic/finite checks (112 construction and 44 finite-design checks). The repository intake only preserves and routes the source; it did not run scripts, independently reconstruct the proof, or conduct external or formal review. Historical priority and practical resource-bounded significance remain UNKNOWN. No historic-scale or 9–10/10 breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Let T(ρ,σ)=½‖ρ−σ‖₁. For every finite recipient count m≥2 and ε,η>0, the source constructs finite d,L, a finite family F={ρ_{ψ_x}} on H=⊕_{r=0}^L Sym^{m^r}(C^d), and one fixed positive finite prior (w_x), such that a full-domain permutation-symmetric CPTP map B:H→H^{⊗m} has every one-recipient marginal error at most 1/L≤ε, while every common entanglement-breaking map E:H→H and every family of commuting replacement states diagonal in one common basis have worst-case error at least 1−η. The same lower bounds hold as averages under the fixed prior. For the corresponding classical–quantum state ω_XH=Σ_x w_x|x⟩⟨x|⊗ρ_{ψ_x}, each XH_j marginal can be broadcast within 1/L, yet its trace distance from every state classical on H is at least 1−η, even when the comparator may change its X marginal. Consequently the suprema of EB and commuting reconstruction error are one for every positive broadcasting tolerance at fixed finite m. The proof gives formulas a=(1/L)Σ_{r=1}^L(k_r+1)/(k_r+d), β=min{1,√(Σ_{r=1}^L D_{k_r}/D_{2k_r})}, with k_r=m^r and D_s=binom(d+s−1,s); choose L large and d sufficiently large (or d=m²m^{2L}) so a,β→0. One common finite weighted projective 2m^L-design supports all comparators and bases simultaneously.
Interface: All maps act on finite-dimensional full matrix algebras and are CPTP; T is half trace norm. The input family consists of rank-L mixed direct-sum states ρ_ψ=0_{H_0}⊕(1/L)⊕_{r=1}^L p_ψ^{⊗m^r}, p_ψ=|ψ⟩⟨ψ|, with a fixed finite design prior. The construction's input already contains a classically uncertain number of genuine unknown-state copies, up to K=m^L. The EB comparator is one common physical measure-and-prepare channel for all family states, with arbitrary finite outcomes. The commuting comparator must use one common basis. The cq comparator can choose a different X marginal but must be classical on H. The source's marginal error is exactly 1/L for its constructed channel; the optimal broadcast error is only bounded above by 1/L. Outputs need not be close to the product family and are highly correlated.
Source-reported proof spine: Let H_r=Sym^{k_r}(C^d), k_r=m^r. The explicit isometry partitions each symmetric k_r-copy block into m groups of k_{r−1}; the full-domain channel maps each sector down one level and sends H_0 to a fixed product output. Only the top and bottom blocks differ in each marginal, giving exact half-trace error 1/L. A fixed decoder extracts one qudit; composing it with any EB map and applying the pure-state estimation bound (k+1)/(k+d) yields the prior-average EB lower bound. For commuting families, the support projections Q_ψ=Lρ_ψ obey a second-moment bound summed over an arbitrary common orthonormal basis; the finite exact 2K design preserves the needed moments. A measurement of X and Q_{ψ_x}, followed by data processing and Cauchy–Schwarz, handles arbitrary changes to the comparator's X marginal. Explicit parameter choices make the bounds approach one while the marginal error tends to zero.
Costs: K=m^L genuine copies occur in the highest sector, dim H=Σ_{r=0}^L D_{k_r}, and the Carathéodory finite prior may require up to D_{2K}² points. The explicit algebraic cubature also has (ceil((2K+1)/2)(2K+1))^{d−1} points; the paper does not establish an efficient construction at large parameters. No cost is supplied for preparing the input from one unknown qudit; such preparation is not part of the contract. The channel is an explicit mathematical CPTP map on a very large space, not a demonstrated resource-bounded physical implementation. Global cloning error approaches one; for L≥2 the source also gives ‖Φ−Φ²‖_diamond=2. Small marginal trace distance therefore does not imply global product fidelity or near-idempotence.
Failure: This refutes only dimension-independent, statewise trace-distance stability without dimension/resource restrictions. It does not refute exact no-broadcasting, bounded-Holevo-capacity conclusions, small-Holevo-loss conclusions, or the pure-family theorem N534. The constructed states are mixed (choose L≥2), and dimension, copy number and Holevo capacity diverge. The exact capacity/loss boundary is routed separately in N553. No NPT bound-entanglement result, FEI solution, efficient one-qudit acquisition, practical experiment, or historic-scale breakthrough is claimed.
Closest comparator: Exact no-broadcasting and finite pure-state estimation/design results are cited as predecessors; the pure-state estimation inequality is reproved in the source. The source reports a targeted but non-exhaustive prior-art search, not historical priority. N534 assumes pure inputs and is not contradicted by this mixed, unbounded-resource family.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the direct-sum CPTP map, the one fixed finite-prior EB bound, the basis-uniform commuting bound and the changed-X-marginal cq argument. Check all norm conventions, finite-design moment order, quantifiers and resource dependencies; then assess priority against the exact prior literature.

title: The mixed-state broadcasting reservoir has diverging Holevo capacity and loss
text:

status=source_derived_unreviewed; Exact formulas and analytic bounds are reported in the source manuscript, with author-internal finite software receipts preserved. Claim: For the finite design prior and shift broadcaster in N552, with K=m^L and D_s=binom(d+s−1,s), the source derives exact Holevo capacity C=(1/L)Σ_{r=1}^L log D_{m^r} and exact actual-prior loss δ=χ(F)−χ(ΦF)=(log D_K−log d)/L. Along the explicit sequence d=m²K² this δ diverges. Thus this construction does not satisfy N368’s bounded-capacity premise or N371’s small-Holevo-loss premise and does not resolve N371. For a reweighted level distribution p_1,…,p_L, the same shift channel has marginal error ½(p_1+p_L+Σ_{r=1}^{L−1}|p_{r+1}−p_r|)≥max_r p_r, so error at most b forces L≥1/b and H(p)≥log(1/b) for this construction. This last inequality is not a universal lower bound for arbitrary broadcasters.
Interface: The formulas use the same finite-dimensional direct-sum family and marginal channel as N552. C is the Holevo capacity supremum over finite priors on that finite family; δ is evaluated for the stated exact finite design prior. The reweighting bound applies only to the described level-shift broadcaster. It does not quantify a universal optimum over channels, input families or reweightings outside this construction.
Scope and resource accounting: The source computes the block-diagonal average state and the entropy of each rank-L family state to obtain C. The marginal shift removes the top copy sector, giving the exact difference δ. A dimension lower bound along d=m²K² shows divergence. For reweighted sectors, total variation between the initial and shifted level distributions gives the stated endpoint/variation expression, bounded below by the maximum weight; the support and Shannon-entropy consequences follow only for this shift mechanism.
Costs: The same K=m^L copy resource and rapidly growing symmetric-space dimension as N552 apply. The source gives exact information quantities but no resource-bounded preparation or physical acquisition. Diverging C and δ are precisely why the example cannot test bounded-capacity or small-loss stability.
Failure: Do not use this construction as a counterexample to N368 or N371: its capacity and actual-prior Holevo loss diverge. It establishes no matching lower bound for N368’s logarithmic rate and closes no N371 gate. The reweighting inequality concerns only this shift construction; it is not a general converse for approximate broadcasting.
Closest comparator: N368 is a bounded-Holevo-capacity result; N371 asks whether small actual-prior Holevo loss forces common EB reconstruction. These source claims have different hypotheses from the present trace-disturbance counterexample. The source explicitly states those gates remain open.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the block entropy and exact Holevo-loss identities, verify divergence along the stated parameter sequence, and keep the reweighted total-variation bound restricted to the shift channel. Confirm the N368 and N371 premises are not met; do not infer closure or invalidation.

title: Unitary bases modulo column permutations admit a dimension-free distortion-three Hilbert embedding
text:
N554-unitary-quotient-distortion-three-hilbert-embedding | Unitary bases modulo column permutations admit a dimension-free distortion-three Hilbert embedding
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The attached packet reports a complete written proof candidate and focused algebra check. The intake preserved and routed the source only; it did not independently reconstruct the proof, execute the supplied random numerical checks, or establish external correctness, formal verification, historical priority, or a 9-10/10 breakthrough.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For each integer d>=1, let Q_d identify U and U P for P in Sym(d), with q_d([U],[V])=min_P ||U-VP||_F/sqrt(d). Define Delta_copy e_i=e_i tensor e_i and Phi_d([U])=(U tensor U)Delta_copy U*/sqrt(d), viewed in the complex Hilbert space Hom(C^d,C^d tensor C^d) with Frobenius norm. The source proves q_d([U],[V]) <= ||Phi_d([U])-Phi_d([V])||_F <= 3 q_d([U],[V]). Thus this quotient metric has a Hilbert embedding with distortion at most 3 uniformly in d. For a finite irreducible reversible Markov kernel with spectral gap gamma, this yields the stated squared-distance Poincare bound with factor 9/gamma; a separate conductance bound controls unsquared distances with factor 3/h.
Interface: The quotient is by the right action U~UP of permutation matrices only; it is not a quotient by monomial matrices or phases. q_d is normalized Frobenius distance after optimal column matching, not its square. Delta_copy is the copying map and is local notation. The Poincare consequences assume a finite irreducible reversible kernel and its stated spectral-gap or conductance convention.
Proof spine: The copying map is invariant under simultaneous permutation of its basis labels. For the lower distortion bound, expand the mixed tensor difference; |U_ij|^2 is doubly stochastic, so Birkhoff averaging bounds its assignment score by the nearest permutation trace score. For the upper bound, telescope the three unitary factors and bound each term by ||U-P||_F. Apply the ordinary Hilbert-valued Poincare inequality to Phi for the squared-distance consequence; use scalar level sets and Gaussian projections for the unsquared version.
Costs: The displayed map has d^3 coordinates and can be evaluated directly; the proof requires neither Haar integration nor a nearest-permutation algorithm. No cost or algorithmic guarantee for the subsequent repair/stability applications follows from this embedding alone.
Failure: The theorem uses exact orthonormal bases and permutation matching; it does not extend as stated to arbitrary matrices modulo column permutations. The copying-comultiplication encoding is established prior art. A dimension-free quantitative estimate does not by itself supply an efficient permutation repair or establish the broader Aldous-Lyons application.
Closest comparator: Coecke-Pavlovic-Vicary establish the copying-comultiplication basis encoding. The attached focused comparison says the checked Auddy-Yuan real odeco perturbation interface does not directly yield the normalized Frobenius estimate, while leaving priority unresolved. Chapman-Lubotzky Section 6.4 is the cited quotient-Poincare motivation.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the global lower and upper distortion bounds with the stated quotient convention, then verify both graph Poincare consequences and complete a version-aware prior-art review of the quantitative estimate.

title: A mixed-copy energy gap gives a charged exact permutation action from a supplied finite-dimensional unitary representation
text:
N555-finite-source-unitary-permutation-rounding | A mixed-copy energy gap gives a charged exact permutation action from a supplied finite-dimensional unitary representation
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported complete proof candidate with a focused algebra, dimension-bookkeeping and primary-interface check; this intake did not independently reconstruct it. External correctness and historical priority remain unresolved. No 9-10/10 breakthrough is claimed.

Claim: Let G be a finite group, S a generating list sampled with weights mu, rho:G->U(d) an exact representation, and P_s prescribed permutation matrices. Put delta^2=E_s ||rho(s)-P_s||_F^2/d. On Hom(C^d,C^d tensor C^d), define R(g)A=(rho(g) tensor rho(g))A rho(g)* and let Pi project onto the invariant subspace. If E_s||R(s)A-A||_F^2 >= kappa||A-Pi A||_F^2 for every A, with kappa>0, then an exact action h:G->Sym(N) exists with d<=N<=(1+197316 delta^2/kappa)d and E_s d_h(P_s,h(s)) <= (1+330354/kappa)delta^2. Here d_h charges every added label: it is one minus the fraction of the N labels agreeing with the original d-label input.
Interface: An exact finite-dimensional representation rho and a uniform mixed-copy energy gap are supplied hypotheses. The original permutation matrices are compared with the representation in normalized Frobenius square. d_h counts added labels in the denominator N; no compact-group or Haar-selection step is used.
Proof spine: The three-factor estimate from N554 bounds the copying vector defect by 9d delta^2. The gap controls its distance from invariant vectors; exact invariance yields an approximate map from the finite group to permutations. The multiplicative defect is at most 18 eta^2. Apply the finite-source Becker-Chapman theorem and track both degree growth and generator error, retaining the added-sheet charge.
Costs: This is an existence theorem, not an efficient repair algorithm. Enumerating the finite group may be much more expensive than reading its presentation. It requires an exact representation and a gap; approximate permutation generators alone do not furnish that representation.
Failure: No efficient algorithm or polynomial presentation-time guarantee follows. The conditional rounding theorem does not itself produce rho or prove the energy gap for an arbitrary group. Compact/Haar extensions are unnecessary and are not part of the stated proof.
Closest comparator: The attached source invokes Becker-Chapman Theorem 1.2 only in its finite-source case. N554 supplies the quantitative three-factor quotient estimate used in the argument.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the invariant-vector defect, constants, finite-source approximate-action repair and charged-degree bookkeeping; verify that every use of the supplied exact representation and energy gap is explicit.

Claim: Let C be a binary linear code of length L, dimension k and relative distance Delta_C>0, and G=F_2^L/C^perp with its L coordinate generators. Suppose the specified finite presentation and relation distribution have a unitary stability modulus f in the source precise sense: relation defect epsilon yields an exact representation rho:G->U(D), rank-r partial isometry w:C^d->C^D and eta=f(epsilon), with average_i ||U_i-w*rho(s_i)w||_F^2/d<=eta and both normalized rank deficits <=eta. For epsilon<=1/2, the attached derivation gives flexible permutation stability with F(epsilon)=min{1,2,000,000 f(2epsilon)/Delta_C}; where the second entry is below one, an exact action on N>=d labels has N<=(1+2,000,000f(2epsilon)/Delta_C)d and average generator error at most 2,000,000f(2epsilon)/Delta_C in the charged metric. For the CVY v2 Reed-Muller/Hadamard application, the reported modulus retains its q^(-c) floor and its separate presentation-dependent linear alternative.
Interface: The finite code presentation, coordinate generator distribution and relation sampling distribution are fixed as in the cited CVY Theorem 4.1. The unitary input guarantee includes both partial-isometry rank deficits; their dimension changes are charged before applying N555 with the character gap kappa=4Delta_C. For larger error the trivial action is the stated fallback. Delta_C denotes code relative distance, not N554 copying map.
Proof spine: Convert normalized Hamming relation error to the unitary Frobenius convention, use the code minimum distance to give every nontrivial character energy at least 4Delta_C, and apply the N555 mixed-copy rounding theorem. Embed the finite-dimensional partial-isometry corner in a common coordinate space, extend missing coordinates trivially, and charge all added labels. Substitute the source CVY parameters and preserve the additive q^(-c) floor.
Costs: This is a stability/existence transfer, not a polynomial-time decoder. The stated presentation is quasi-polynomial in k for the concrete sequence; the packet does not meet the sharper polynomial-in-k presentation target. No uniform floor-free poly(log k) epsilon^b guarantee for every positive epsilon is established.
Failure: Do not erase the additive q^(-c) term, the separate presentation-dependent linear alternative, or the charged added-label convention. This does not establish arbitrary-code permutation testability, a non-sofic group, or the random-complex first-stage repair. It is conditional on the precise external CVY and Becker-Chapman theorem interfaces.

The source notes the permutation presentation problem was described as open in the cited July 2026 CVY version; current priority is not established here.

text:

status=source_derived_unreviewed; The source reports exact derivations and a portable exact-arithmetic replay receipt. These examples delimit assumptions and refute a shortcut; they do not establish the main amplifier theorem or a historic-scale discovery.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: The campaign reports four scoped counterexample boundaries: (i) without multiplier-invariance of the source test space, an abstract four-comparison interpolation implication fails (the reported comparison is 296650/101277 versus 248/75), while the physical application uses the invariant test space; (ii) reversing the creation-port thermal orientation is necessary, with the correct scalar comparison 103/72<=105/62 and incorrect all-down comparison 133/72>105/62; (iii) independence of the two amplifier inputs cannot be dropped, even for separable classical coherent-state correlations with amplitudes sqrt(G-1)z and -sqrt(G)conjugate(z) that cancel the retained displacement, leaving output tau_(G-1) while the purported bound exceeds it by 2G(G-1)Var(z); and (iv) for rho=diag(15,74,11)/100 and phase-space dilation parameter t=3/2, an exact rational photon-law and entropy enclosure, using the one-mode convention \mathcal{N}(rho)=g^(-1)(S(rho)), gives \mathcal{N}(D_(3/2)rho)<(3/2)(\mathcal{N}(rho)+1/2)-1/2, violating the stronger universal physical-endpoint dilation entropy inequality by more than 0.0322153811310172 nats. The dilation counterexample does not refute the physical amplifier EPnI.
Interface: Each falsifier is local to the stated abstraction or assumption. The multiplier example refutes a bare lemma without the required invariant test-space hypothesis, not the corrected physical application. The creation-port example fixes scalar data and compares orientations. The independence example uses correlated inputs, outside N557 assumptions. The dilation example is a positive endpoint state construction, not a claim that intermediate dilation maps are physical channels.
Proof spine: The source supplies explicit exact scalar witnesses for missing multiplier invariance and port orientation, a coherent-state correlation construction that cancels the retained displacement, and a three-level rational input whose phase-space-dilated photon probabilities are q_m=16(198m^2+324m+1)/(3125*5^m). The report cites rational logarithm enclosures and a geometric-polynomial tail bound for the strict entropy comparison. Portable receipts are preserved but were not rerun here.
Costs: The counterexamples are explicit analytic/rational constructions with finite exact checks. Their ingestion cost was static file and archive verification only. The large campaign worker count is provenance, not proof or novelty evidence.

Conversely, compactness attains a finite-horizon norm-one maximizer; equality forces each active conditional direction to be deterministic. Identity and positive gate weights give nested active direction sets, and a repeated finite set yields a gate-invariant orbit.

Claim: For compactly supported probability measures mu,nu in R^d, define Phi_(r,eta)(mu)=D(mu*gamma_r||gamma_r)-D(mu*gamma_r||eta*gamma_r), for every r>0 and every finitely supported probability eta. The source proves nu<=cx mu if and only if Phi_(r,eta)(nu)<=Phi_(r,eta)(mu) for all such probes. The raw scalar profile D(mu*gamma_r||gamma_r) alone is incomplete; a reflected two-point pair has identical scalar profiles but incomparable convex order.
Interface: All measures are compactly supported; the probes range over all positive Gaussian scales and all finite eta. The theorem characterizes an infinite family of real-valued probes and supplies no oracle, finite query bound or efficient decision algorithm.
Proof spine: Forward direction follows because Gaussian addition preserves convex order and the probe’s log-likelihood is convex. For the converse, small-scale finite log-sum-exp probes approximate any finite maximum of affine functions uniformly on the compact supports; supporting affine approximations recover every finite convex test function.
Costs: The probe family is infinite and may require precision and many affine pieces. For supplied finite supports, standard martingale-coupling linear feasibility already decides convex order; the result is a complete reformulation, not an efficient new capability.
Failure: One scalar E_r profile is not enough; reflection preserves it while the two call functions cross. Replacing the whole probe family by a restricted small family requires separate approximation/cost guarantees.
Closest comparator: Gaussian mixtures, convex duality and finite martingale-coupling tests have established precedents; the source describes this as a useful reorganization and does not claim a new primitive.
Open verification: Independently check the log-sum-exp limit and supporting-affine approximation, then determine whether any restricted probe family yields a useful finite computational interface.

The upper horizon is independent of coefficient heights and has tower height growing with dimension.

The geometric statement is over an algebraically closed field as in the source. For the stated rational-input computational consequence, coefficients and initial point are rational and characteristic zero; polynomials are explicitly encoded.

Claim: Let C be a nonzero closed convex semialgebraic cone of completely positive maps on M_d, invariant under arbitrary CP pre- and postcomposition. The source candidate proves: if every member of C has some entanglement-breaking power, then there is N(C) such that every length-N(C) word of independently chosen members of C is entanglement breaking. Under these hypotheses pointwise eventual EB, a common equal-map EB exponent and a common arbitrary-word EB length are equivalent. The source applies this to PPT maps and to the cone CP ∩ 2-CoPos (maps that are both CP and 2-copositive), whose factors can include maps that are not PPT.
Interface: Finite-dimensional maps on M_d; every factor lies in the stated mapping cone and the full closed/convex/semialgebraic/CP-invariance assumptions are required. Words are serial compositions with factors allowed to vary by position; factors may be non-TP.
Proof spine: CP input/output filters isolate a transported cross coefficient in a two-dimensional triangular map. A nonzero coefficient would preserve qubit NPT at every power, contradicting the pointwise hypothesis; normalized boundary and positive-anchor inductions then yield a uniform arbitrary-word length.
Costs: The conclusion is finite existence of N(C), with dimension-only applications for PPT and CP plus 2-copositive cones. No practical numeric exponent or efficient decomposition is supplied.
Failure: The cone hypotheses cannot be dropped for an arbitrary compact set/class. This is serial composition, not tensor powers. Source says the later cone and unrestricted-word arguments were not covered by earlier focused reviews; targeted dependency/algebra checks are source-reported only.
Closest comparator: The source credits established mapping-cone and k-EB composition results and compares restricted mixed-map results. Its novelty search is explicitly targeted, not exhaustive.

Claim: For d≥2 and a length-n serial word T of maps on M_d that are both completely positive and 2-copositive (CP ∩ 2-CoPos), n≥d−1, the source gives entanglement-breaking CP maps E,F with E=q_nT+F, E*(I)=T*(I), F*(I)=(1−q_n)T*(I), where q_n=[1+4√2 d²(1−1/(8d))^floor(n/(d−1))]^−(d−1). For every reference and positive joint input X, ||(id⊗(T−E))(X)||_1≤2(1−q_n) tr[(id⊗T)(X)]. For trace-preserving words, the source gives a sufficient O(d² log(d/η)) length for diamond error at most η.
Interface: Every counted serial factor must lie in CP ∩ 2-CoPos (both CP and 2-copositive); factors may vary and need not be trace preserving. The output effect is matched exactly. The conditioned-output guarantee is via the trace-relative bound for positive joint inputs, avoiding an inverse success-probability penalty.
Proof spine: A Gaussian concurrence gap supplies an explicit contraction; depolarizing repair constructs an EB component, and effect matching controls the successful output trace under postselection.
Costs: Explicit q_n above; for trace-preserving words the stated sufficient length is (d−1) ceil[8d log(8√2(d−1)d²/η)] for η∈(0,2). This is conservative and does not include an efficient measure-and-prepare decomposition cost.
Failure: An averaged PPT map does not imply each branch is CP/2-copositive. No arbitrary network or tensor-power impossibility follows. Earlier exactness barriers show approximate EB replacement alone does not settle exact EB for unrestricted nonunital words.
Closest comparator: The source credits Gaussian concurrence, Bell-flag/2-EB iteration and filtered prior results, while keeping exact arbitrary-word membership and approximation distinct.

title: Dual-kernel lifting yields exact uniform samples under a certified collective-rank bound
text:
N580-dual-kernel-exact-joint-sampling | Dual-kernel lifting yields exact uniform samples under a certified collective-rank bound
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported exact sampler and conditioning proof candidate with exact finite checks and a native smoke record. Intake only preserved and hashed the packet; mathematical scripts were not run. The collective-rank promise and coordinate-specific acquisition boundary remain essential. External correctness and historical priority are UNKNOWN; status remains source_derived_unreviewed.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Let q be a prime power, A_1,…,A_m∈F_q^{p×n}, c_i∈F_q^n, and let g:F_q^p→F_q^m be efficiently evaluable. Suppose a certified integer R satisfies rank(Σ_i λ_i A_i)≥R for every nonzero λ∈F_q^m. For F(x) with rows xᵀA_i+c_iᵀ, the source derives an exact rejection sampler whose output conditioned on success is uniform over every pair in S_g={(x,y):F(x)y=g(x)}, including singular fibers. For R≥m+1, its expected number of trials is at most (1+α)/(1−α/(q−1))<3, where α=(q^m−1)q^(−R). In the pure bilinear fixed-target case c_i=0 and g(x)=b, R≥m suffices for fewer than four expected trials. For x=x_0+Pu of codimension a and a graph restriction Dy=h(x) with k independent rows, the source proves a transformed rank bound R−a−k; the <3 guarantee persists when R−a−k≥m+1.
Interface: Finite field F_q; matrices A_i and offsets c_i are supplied; g is evaluated as a supplied circuit/algorithm. The exact output domain is all satisfying joint pairs, sampled uniformly, not a chosen affine chart or only full-rank fibers. A valid collective-rank lower bound R must be certified. The stated closure covers affine restriction of x and a full-row-rank affine graph constraint on y with efficiently evaluable h; arbitrary added polynomial constraints are outside the interface.
Proof spine: For each dual λ and affine-kernel point x, the proposal/kernel factors give each admissible pair (x,y) the same one-trial probability q^(−p)/(1+α); counting the dual annihilator of F(x) yields the identical mass q^(m−p−n)/(1+α) for every solution pair. A projective union bound controls row-deficient x and supplies the expected-trial bounds. Under the stated conditioning, substitution through a right inverse and a basis for ker D transforms A_i to PᵀA_iQ and loses at most a+k rank.
Costs: Per trial: polynomially many finite-field operations in (m,p,n), one evaluation of g, exact linear-system solves, and O((m+p+n)log q) expected unbiased bits; the certified regimes give fewer than three or four expected trials. For square n×n matrices, the source gives a structured Moore-interpolation certificate R=n−s using O(n³+mn²) extension-field operations after a verified F_{q^n} representation. Field construction/search and verification are charged; the certificate is coordinate-dependent, and finding a favorable hidden basis is not included.
Failure: A high collective-rank certificate is a strong promise; individual A_i ranks do not suffice, and general minimum-combination-rank acquisition is not solved. The Moore certificate can weaken under an unknown basis scramble. Uncharged nonlinear identification can make a conditioned system empty (the alternating-matrix y=x example); rank loss and added constraints must be charged. Outside the certified regimes rejection may fail to terminate on an empty solution set, so this is not a general decision procedure or generic constraint solver.
Closest comparator: The source identifies Moore interpolation, linearized-polynomial/rank-metric bounds, and the pivot-chart triangular argument as established ingredients; it cites exact sampling for a single quadratic equation. The specific multi-constraint dual-kernel law and charged nonlinear conditioning are a targeted, unresolved prior-art question; absence from this search is not novelty evidence.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the equal-mass law including singular fibers, the projective deficiency bound, exact random-bit allocation, the R−a−k conditioning charge, and the square-map Moore certificate. Check empty-set behavior, hidden-basis degradation, all cost terms, and the exact multi-constraint prior-art boundary before reuse.

title: Affine-mixture rejection envelopes can incur exponential overhead even for an easy product target
text:
N581-affine-mixture-envelope-obstruction | Affine-mixture rejection envelopes can incur exponential overhead even for an easy product target
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-derived representation-specific rejection-envelope obstruction and exact finite records; intake did not rerun code or independently verify the proof. The target has a simple exact product sampler. No general hardness or historic-scale breakthrough is claimed; status remains source_derived_unreviewed.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For π(λ)=2^(−wt(λ))/(3/2)^m on F_2^m, equivalently independent Bernoulli(1/3) bits, let Q be any mixture of at most K uniform laws on affine subspaces and assume π(λ)≤ρQ(λ) pointwise. For integers 0≤D<m and t with positive numerator, the source derives ρ≥[Pr(Bin(m,1/3)≤t)−K(2/3)^(m−D)]/Pr(Bin(D+1,1/2)≤t). For m divisible by 8 it gives the weakened bound ρ≥[1−exp(−m/288)−K(2/3)^(m/8)]exp(m/112) for a stated choice of D,t, when the bracket is positive; hence polynomial K entails exponential overhead in that regime. Separately, the simpler rank-bound affine-cover construction obeys C/Z≥(4/3)^m/K. The target itself is exactly sampled by independent bits, so this is an affine-mixture representation barrier, not intrinsic sampling hardness.
Interface: Target distribution π on F_2^m; proposal Q is a mixture of at most K uniform distributions on affine subspaces. The lower bound concerns pointwise domination π≤ρQ, the condition used for rejection sampling. The affine-cover inequality applies to the separately stated uniform-rank-cover construction.
Proof spine: For an affine subspace of dimension at most D, its target mass is bounded by (2/3)^(m−D). For higher-dimensional pieces, information-set coordinates are unbiased under their uniform law, which bounds their mass on the low-Hamming-weight tail by a Bin(D+1,1/2) probability. Remove the union of low-dimensional components from {wt≤t}, compare remaining target mass to proposal mass, and derive the displayed ratio.
Costs: No sampler cost lower bound follows: π is sampled exactly with m independent Bernoulli(1/3) bits. The source supplies an exact finite formula and reports enumeration of every affine subspace through m=6 plus exact rational examples at m=100,250,500; intake did not rerun that checker.
Failure: Applies only to mixtures of uniform affine subspace laws under pointwise domination and to the specified envelope construction. It does not rule out multiplicative factorizations, product sampling, dual-kernel sampling, or other compact representations; the example is deliberately easy to sample.
Closest comparator: The source distinguishes product sampling, affine stratification and weighted/code-like models. It makes no claim that these models or exact sampling are novel; the result is a scoped obstruction to this proposal representation.
Open verification: Reconstruct the low/high dimensional mass bounds and the finite domination formula, verify constants and rounding in the m divisible by eight corollary, and preserve the product-sampler escape when interpreting the asymptotic rejection lower bound.

title: Binary single-coordinate rank ascent can stall despite arbitrarily high collective rank
text:
N582-binary-coordinate-rank-ascent-trap | Binary single-coordinate rank ascent can stall despite arbitrarily high collective rank
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported exact counterexample family to one local rank-ascent heuristic. Finite code checks were not rerun at intake; external correctness and priority remain UNKNOWN. This is not a general hardness claim; status remains source_derived_unreviewed.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For every integer d≥2, the source constructs two matrices A_1,A_2 over F_2 with 2d+1 input coordinates and d columns such that rank(A_1)=rank(A_2)=rank(A_1+A_2)=d. At x_0=e_0 the 2×d matrix F(x_0) has rank 1; changing any one binary coordinate yields rank at most 1 (the e_0 flip yields zero), while the two-coordinate move x=e_0+e_1+e_2 yields rank 2. Thus a single-coordinate rank-ascent rule can stall despite minimum nonzero-combination rank d. The source reports exact script checks for d=2,3,5,8.
Interface: Finite field F_2; a two-output linear matrix map F:F_2^(2d+1)→F_2^(2×d), for each d≥2. The obstruction is only to procedures whose next move changes one input coordinate at a time while seeking a larger rank.
Proof spine: Use the explicit coordinate generators F(e_0)=E, F(e_j)=E+e_2e_jᵀ, and F(eʹ_j)=E+(e_1+e_2)e_jᵀ, with E=e_1e_1ᵀ, j=1,…,d. Direct row inspection gives rank d for each nonzero A-combination; evaluating at e_0 and each Hamming-neighbor gives rank at most one, whereas the displayed two-coordinate move has rank two.
Costs: The witness dimension is 2d+1 by d with two constraint matrices; the source includes exact finite checks for d=2,3,5,8. No algorithm benchmark or asymptotic runtime comparison is supplied.
Failure: This falsifies only single-coordinate rank-ascent for the stated family. A two-coordinate escape is explicit. It is not a lower bound against multi-coordinate or global algorithms, a hardness result, or a failure of dual-kernel sampling.
Closest comparator: The source screens a separate pivot-chart construction against the established LLD triangular argument and does not claim it as novel. This counterexample addresses a local coordinate-update heuristic, not that established chart theorem or all rank-acquisition methods.
Open verification: Check the symbolic ranks for all d≥2 and the listed finite witnesses; make sure downstream use concludes only that single-coordinate ascent may stall, without inferring general rank-certification hardness.

title: An exponential-moment seed class has an exact environmental-kernel obstruction to rare mixtures
text:
N583-thermal-attenuator-environmental-kernel-rare-mixture-obstruction | An exponential-moment seed class has an exact environmental-kernel obstruction to rare mixtures
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported internal analytic reconstruction with scoped diagnostics. This intake checked preservation only and did not run source scripts or independently audit the proof. Heavy-tail, varying-mixture and collective-code cases remain UNKNOWN; no capacity threshold or historic-scale breakthrough is claimed.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For the single-mode thermal attenuator Phi_{eta,nu}, 0<eta<1 and nu>0, set G=1+(1-eta)nu and assume eta>G-1. Let R=(eta-(G-1))/(G-1)>0. For a normalized pure seed psi=sum_{j>=0} psi_j|j> satisfying sum_{j>=0}(j+1)R^j|psi_j|^2<infinity, the source constructs a nonzero normalizable vector g_* in the kernel of the full two-mode Stinespring-environment coefficient map. For every fixed distinct normalized pure finite-energy competitor phi, define q_phi=||T_phi g_*||^2/||g_*||^2>0, with T_phi the coefficient map for its complementary output. Then rho_p=(1-p)|psi><psi|+p|phi><phi| obeys limsup_{p down to 0} I_c(rho_p,Phi_{eta,nu})/[p log(1/p)] <= -q_phi < 0 (natural logarithms), hence has negative coherent information for all sufficiently small p. The source reports this sign without a finite receiver-relative-entropy assumption.
Interface: One use of a single-mode thermal attenuator with the full complementary output, including the thermal-environment purifier. The seed is pure, finite-energy and obeys the stated exponential-moment condition; the competitor is a fixed, distinct pure finite-energy state. The mixture weight tends to zero while both states remain fixed. This does not cover competitors depending on p or general entangled block-code inputs.
Proof spine: An explicit entangled Bargmann multiplier gives a normalizable vector in the seed complement kernel; its norm is an exact weighted photon-moment expression. Contracting the same vector with a competitor produces a Wronskian f h′-f′ h, nonzero exactly when the pure states differ, so an environmental measurement leaks probability q_phi>0 only under the rare component. A binary-label conditional-entropy continuity argument gives the asymptotic negative p log(1/p) term without a finite receiver-relative-entropy assumption.
Costs: No algorithmic or physical acquisition cost is claimed. The restriction is a weighted exponential photon-number moment depending on eta and nu; the sign conclusion is for each fixed seed/competitor pair and all sufficiently small mixture weights, with no uniform threshold in p supplied.
Failure: This excludes only the stated rare binary mixtures around seeds satisfying the moment condition. Sufficiently heavy tails outside the condition, varying seed/competitor limits, faithful complementary outputs outside this class, and general collective codes remain unresolved. It does not prove zero capacity or rule out a positive rate from another family.
Closest comparator: This is a single-letter rare-mixture obstruction for the thermal attenuator. It does not alter the cited primary paper reported positive witness at eta=0.7841 or establish the capacity threshold. The proof and diagnostics are source-reported internal work, not external validation.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the normalizable Bargmann kernel and exact norm criterion, verify the Wronskian leakage and binary-label continuity argument with the full complementary channel, then map precisely which seed tails and mixture limits remain outside the result.

title: Near antidegradability, high qubit entanglement fidelity requires a large energy-limited block
text:
N584-antidegradable-boundary-finite-block-energy-resource-lower-bound | Near antidegradability, high qubit entanglement fidelity requires a large energy-limited block
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported internal resource lower bound, not a capacity converse. The 1392 evaluation is source-reported; intake performed no research-code or numerical replay. External correctness and priority remain UNKNOWN.

Claim: For m uses of the single-mode thermal attenuator Phi_{eta,1}, any deterministic qubit encoder/decoder with total mean input photon number E obeys F_e <= 3/4 + |arccos(sqrt(eta))-pi/6| sqrt(3E+m). If E<=10m, eta=0.751 and target entanglement fidelity F_e>=0.99, the source reports the necessary lower bound m>=1392 channel uses. More generally, for E<=mN and F_e>=1-epsilon with epsilon<1/4, m >= (1/4-epsilon)^2/(|arccos(sqrt(eta))-pi/6|^2(3N+1)).
Interface: The channel is the memoryless thermal attenuator with bath mean photon number nu=1. The result applies to arbitrary deterministic qubit codes over m channel uses, with total average input energy E and entanglement fidelity F_e; it does not assume a maximum photon cutoff or a specific code family. The 1392 example additionally assumes average energy at most 10 photons per use and target fidelity 0.99.
Proof spine: At eta0=3/4 the channel is antidegradable, giving the qubit symmetric-extension fidelity ceiling 3/4 for every deterministic code. An angle-continuity estimate for the Stinespring beam-splitter dilation bounds the change in decoded entanglement fidelity by |theta-pi/6| sqrt(3E+m), yielding the displayed inequality and the necessary blocklength bound.
Costs: The resource variables are channel uses m and total mean input photons E; no decoder runtime, preparation procedure, maximum per-use energy, or sufficient construction is provided. The numerical threshold 1392 is a source-reported evaluation of the exact necessary bound.
Failure: This is not a quantum-capacity converse: it permits reliability with growing blocklength/energy and does not rule out positive coherent information or positive asymptotic capacity above eta=3/4. It applies to the stated deterministic qubit entanglement-fidelity task at nu=1, not arbitrary fidelity thresholds or assisted capacities.
Closest comparator: The primary source reports a positive finite-energy coherent-information witness at eta=0.7841 and antidegradability through eta=0.75; the exact threshold remains open. This finite-block resource lower bound does not extend that capacity bracket.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the antidegradable symmetric-extension bound and angle-continuity estimate for arbitrary deterministic encoders/decoders; audit the energy convention and reproduce the 1392 rounding from the exact formula without treating it as a capacity converse.

title: An index-two self-dual lattice repetition family reduces an ideal code to an explicit integral gate
text:

status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-derived ideal-code candidate with a conditional sufficient criterion. Claim: Let Lambda_0 be a full-rank symplectically self-dual k-mode lattice of volume (2pi)^k and chi:Lambda_0->Z_2 a nontrivial homomorphism. Choose t with exp(i t^T Omega lambda)=(-1)^chi(lambda), so 2t belongs to Lambda_0. The index-two lattice Lambda_n={(lambda_1,...,lambda_n) in Lambda_0^n: sum_j chi(lambda_j)=0 mod 2} is a valid commuting lattice encoding one qubit. For additive Gaussian noise with density f_v=N(0,v I_{2k}) per block and a fundamental cell C_0, define g_lat(s)=sum_{lambda in Lambda_0} f_v(s+lambda), f_chi(s)=sum_{lambda in Lambda_0}(-1)^chi(lambda)f_v(s+lambda), r(s)=f_chi(s)/g_lat(s), and g_t(s)=g_lat(s+t). Set rho(v)=integral_{C_0} f_chi(s)^2/g_lat(s) ds and beta(v)=integral_{C_0} sqrt(g_lat(s)g_t(s)) ds. For a uniform bit T with conditional iid syndrome densities g_lat or g_t, let H_shift(n)=H(T|Y_1,...,Y_n); let H_parity(n)=E_{S_j iid g_lat} h_2((1+product_j r(S_j))/2), with binary entropy in bits. The source-defined ideal analog stabilizer decoder obeys I_c(n)=1-H_parity(n)-H_shift(n) and I_c(n)>=rho(v)^n/(2 ln 2)-beta(v)^n, so rho(v)>beta(v) is sufficient for positive ideal coherent information at finite n. At bath occupation nu=1, sender preamplification maps v=2(1-eta); however, no lattice meeting the condition near v=1/2 is supplied.
Interface: The result concerns an ideal infinite-energy lattice-code family and analog syndrome decoding for a Gaussian additive-noise channel. The transfer to the thermal attenuator uses sender preamplification with v=2(1-eta) at nu=1. A physical finite-energy code additionally requires a charged envelope, Gram orthonormalization, syndrome instrument, finite precision and cutoff-error bound; these are not established by the integral criterion.
Proof spine: A nontrivial character of the self-dual base lattice defines a half-shift t. The parity-kernel sublattice has index two and its dual yields four logical cosets, giving a pure ideal qubit repetition family. Decomposing the decoded logical error into shift and parity bits gives I_c=1-H_parity-H_shift exactly. The binary entropy series lower-bounds 1-H_parity by rho^n/(2 ln 2), while a Bhattacharyya bound gives H_shift<=beta^n.
Costs: A block of n repetitions over a k-mode base uses kn physical modes per logical qubit. For the stated additive-channel simulation the source counts a sender preamplifier and a thermal-channel use per physical mode. No finite-energy preparation, decoder precision, outer coding or runtime bound is included.
Failure: The sufficient gate rho(v)>beta(v) is not met by the reported square, rectangular and tested hexagonal lattice seeds near v=1/2; the reported image-sum values are floating-point diagnostics, not a certified global search. No actual thermal-attenuator positive coherent-information witness near eta=0.75, finite-energy transfer, or complete decoder is proved. Failure of these examples is not impossibility for other lattices or codes.
Closest comparator: This is an ideal conditional construction route, distinct from the published finite-Fock positive witness at eta=0.7841. It neither improves the checked capacity frontier nor establishes an operational or physical code. The exact threshold remains UNKNOWN.
Open verification: Reconstruct the exact syndrome identity and entropy bounds; then find a rigorously certified self-dual lattice with rho(v)>beta(v) for v<1/2, or delimit the gate, and separately establish a finite-energy encoder/decoder transfer for the actual thermal channel.

Claim: Let g(x)=(x+1)ln(x+1)-x ln x and N(X|R)=g^{-1}(S(X|R)) when the conditional entropy is nonnegative. Prepare R,A by a two-mode squeeze of parameter 1/4 applied to tau_{1/2} tensor tau_{1/2}; take an independent vacuum B and apply a one-mode quantum-limited amplifier of gain G=6/5 to A,B. The source reports outward interval bounds N(A|R)>0.3895 and N(C|R)<0.6607, whereas the proposed conditional extension would require N(C|R)>=(6/5)N(A|R)+1/5>0.6674. Both conditional entropies are positive. Thus this finite-energy product-with-vacuum example refutes that reference-conditioned strengthening. The A and B input marginals remain independent and the unconditioned candidate inequality is saturated by the thermal marginals.
Interface: One mode in each amplifier port; ancillary input B is vacuum and independent of the reference-correlated A. The reference R is correlated with A by a two-mode squeezed thermal state. Vacuum covariance is 1/2 and entropies use natural logarithms. Only the proposed replacement S(X)->S(X|R) followed by g^{-1} is refuted; the independent-input unconditional theorem has no shared-reference premise.
Proof spine: The RA covariance has blocks aI,aI,cZ with a=cosh(1/2), c=sinh(1/2). Under gain 6/5, the output covariance blocks determine two symplectic eigenvalues. The source encloses S(A|R) and S(C|R) with outward intervals, then uses monotonicity of g to establish inverse bounds separated by more than 0.0067. The retained receipt reports an interval check; intake did not run the supplied mpmath code.

It does not contradict the unconditioned independent-input amplifier candidate N557, which is saturated here at the marginals; nor does it refute the weaker conditional entropy power inequality. It gives no thermal-channel capacity bound.

title: Universal reversible-relaxation convexity forces a chi-square divergence profile
text:
N587-dynamic-data-processing-rigidity | Universal reversible-relaxation convexity forces a chi-square divergence profile
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The note reports an internally complete finite-state argument. Intake only preserved and routed the source; it did not independently verify the mathematics or rerun checks. Claim: Let {D_n}_{n>=1} be finite-valued nonnegative functionals on strictly positive finite probability simplices, normalized by D_n(q,q)=0. Assume data processing under rectangular stochastic maps whose input and output distributions have full support, and for each fixed q assume continuity in p on the open simplex and C^2 regularity away from p=q. The source states that universal convexity of t↦D_n(p exp(tL),q) for every finite alphabet, full-support p,q and irreducible q-reversible continuous-time Markov generator L is equivalent to one alphabet-independent Ψ in C([0,infinity))∩C^2((0,infinity)) with D_n(p,q)=Ψ(χ²(p||q)), Ψ(0)=0, Ψ'(s)>=0 and Ψ'(s)+sΨ''(s)>=0. No tensor-additivity or trace-form premise is needed. As separate corollaries, tensor additivity forces D_n=c log(1+χ²), c>=0 (the order-two Rényi divergence); within that additive class, requiring D'''(t)<=0 along every finite reversible relaxation forces D=0. Under the same data-processing and regularity assumptions, convexity along every irreducible finite stationary generator, including nonreversible ones, forces D=0 without tensor additivity.
Interface: Finite alphabets, full-support row distributions p,q and rectangular stochastic maps with full-support outputs. A generator has nonnegative off-diagonal entries, zero row sums and acts by p_t=p exp(tL); q is stationary, and q_i L_ij=q_j L_ji in the reversible theorem. For each fixed q, regularity is in p only: continuity on the open simplex and C^2 away from p=q. The source does not assume differentiability at equality or regularity in q. Here n indexes alphabet size; the additive conclusion is named “order-two Rényi divergence” and is not denoted D_2.
Proof spine: Sections 2–3 derive exact refinement invariance, transverse Hessian scaling and a rare-clone curvature identity; taking the clone mass to zero forces gradient chord slopes to agree. Section 4 makes the gradient affine in likelihood ratio and establishes global constancy on chi-square level sets, including rational and irrational references. Section 5 identifies exactly the scalar convexity conditions. Section 6 solves the tensor-additive functional equation and the third-derivative obstruction. Section 7 uses nonreversible cycle generators to force the zero functional.
Costs: No algorithmic or physical runtime claim. The source reports exact computations supporting the curvature witness and scalar examples; the cited checker was not supplied and was not rerun at intake.
Failure: The main classification is finite-state and depends on data processing plus the stated p-regularity. It does not classify arbitrary divergences without these assumptions. Section 8 of the attached note separately states a regularity-free additive result on bounded Polish-space experiments, but points to a companion proof file not supplied or located; this ancillary statement is not included in the registered theorem. External correctness and historical priority remain UNKNOWN.
Closest comparator: The main result gives a broader scalar Ψ family than its tensor-additive logarithmic member. N588 is a separate complete-monotonicity classification: its positive entire-series profiles fit the scalar conditions here, but its local smoothness and independent-augmentation assumptions differ, and it derives rather than assumes data processing. This relation is only a scoped comparison, not a proof dependency.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the refinement/Hessian scaling and rare-clone limit, then audit the global level-set/reference argument, scalar sufficiency, additive functional equation and nonreversible cycle step with every assumption retained. Keep the missing Section 8 companion proof and the unsupplied Section 9 checker outside the established theorem.

title: Complete monotonicity under reversible Markov dynamics classifies positive entire chi-square profiles
text:
N588-finite-reversible-complete-monotonicity-classification | Complete monotonicity under reversible Markov dynamics classifies positive entire chi-square profiles
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The source reports an internally completed argument under its stated assumptions, while explicitly withholding originality and landmark claims. Intake did not independently audit the proof or run the illustrative symbolic check. External correctness, formal certification and historical priority remain UNKNOWN; no historic-scale breakthrough is established; status remains source_derived_unreviewed.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For every finite alphabet, let D_n be finite-valued and nonnegative on strictly positive probability distributions, with D_n(q,q)=0. Assume continuity in p throughout each open simplex, C-infinity regularity near each full-support q, and invariance under independent uninformative augmentation in both tensor orders: D_nm(p⊗r,q⊗r)=D_n(p,q) and D_mn(r⊗p,r⊗q)=D_n(p,q), without presuming relabeling invariance or full tensor additivity. If for every full-support p,q and every irreducible q-reversible continuous-time Markov generator L, t↦D_n(p exp(tL),q) is completely monotone for t>0, then and only then there is one alphabet- and q-independent power series Ψ(z)=Σ_{k>=1} a_k z^k, a_k>=0, with infinite radius of convergence, such that D_n(p,q)=Ψ(χ²(p||q)). Data processing follows from the classification and is not a premise. For s=χ²(p||q)>0 and every integer N>=1, the source gives D_{n^N}(p^⊗N,q^⊗N)>=((1+s)^N-1)/s · D_n(p,q), sharply attained by D=cχ². Thus no nonzero tensor-additive member, or member growing only O(N) under independent replication, lies in the class.
Interface: Finite-state distributions only. Each fixed q has continuity throughout the open simplex and C-infinity regularity in a neighborhood of q; no analyticity, nondegenerate Hessian or differentiability in q is assumed. Independent augmentation identities are explicitly required in both tensor orders; full tensor additivity is not assumed. Complete monotonicity means (-1)^k d^k/dt^k D_n(p exp(tL),q)>=0 for every integer k>=0 and t>0, for every irreducible q-reversible generator. The result does not cover nonreversible generators or a no-smoothness setting.
Proof spine: The proof represents each relaxation as a positive Laplace transform, then uses asymptotic spectral extraction and valid near-reset reversible generators to realize arbitrary q-orthonormal eigenbases. Positivity forces each smooth Taylor jet to be radial. A positive-measure argument recovers the global function without assuming analyticity. Independent augmentation identifies one alphabet-independent series and forces nonnegative coefficients; conversely, each monomial chi-square power is completely monotone along reversible relaxation, and the stated data processing and replication consequences follow.
Costs: No algorithmic, physical or runtime improvement is claimed. The source contains one illustrative exact third-derivative example, but its symbolic-check script was not supplied or rerun. No benchmark or empirical dynamics are involved.
Failure: Scope is finite-state and reversible, with C-infinity regularity near equilibrium and independent uninformative augmentation. It does not classify nonsmooth functionals, nonreversible relaxation, empirical or quantum dynamics, or Polish-space divergences. The exact example calculation is source-reported only; no formal proof-assistant verification or external correctness review is supplied.
Closest comparator: Compared with N587, this is a narrower profile class (nonnegative entire power series) with stronger complete-monotonicity and augmentation hypotheses; it does not assume data processing. Every profile classified here satisfies the scalar conditions of N587, but neither result is a proof dependency of the other. Do not transfer N587’s nonreversible zero conclusion to this theorem.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the Bernstein/Laplace spectral extraction, the admissible generators realizing arbitrary eigenbases, radiality of all Taylor jets, the global recovery argument without analyticity, and the augmentation step that identifies nonnegative coefficients. Check exact quantifiers and assumptions. Verify the attached note’s stated Bernstein citation edition/theorem number; the cited example checker was not supplied.

title: A verified singular-value envelope gives exact Gaussian equality-conditioned samples
text:
N589-residual-conditioned-gaussian-fiber-student-envelope | A verified singular-value envelope gives exact Gaussian equality-conditioned samples
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The 2026-10-10 packet reports internally derived sampler theorems, exact arithmetic checks, and a fixed-input finite-bit prototype. This intake checked source/archive hashes, JSON syntax, and repository routing only; it did not execute scientific scripts, replay numerical draws, independently reconstruct the proofs, or obtain external/formal verification. Physical acquisition and historical priority remain unresolved. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Let independent X~N(0,I_p), Y~N(0,I_n), F(x)_{i,:}=x^T A_i+c_i^T, H(x,y)=F(x)y-g(x), S(x)=F(x)F(x)^T, E_g(x)=g(x)^T S(x)^(-1)g(x), and W_g=E[det(S(X))^(-1/2) exp(-E_g(X)/2)]. The target is the Gaussian residual-disintegration/delta-conditioning law, whose x density is proportional to phi_p(x)det(S(x))^(-1/2)exp(-E_g(x)/2), followed by the Gaussian conditional Y|F(x)Y=g(x). If an explicit integer R>m and s>0 satisfy sigma_R(A_lambda)>=s||lambda|| for every lambda, then v(lambda)<=h(lambda)=(1+s^2||lambda||^2)^(-R/2). Propose lambda=Z/(s sqrt(V)), Z~N(0,I_m), V~chi-square_(R-m), accept by v/h, sample X|lambda from N(mu_lambda,K_lambda^(-1)) using the completed-square Gaussian formulas, then accept by exp(-E_g(X)/2) and draw the conditional Y. In ideal arithmetic each trial succeeds with probability W_g/C and has expected trial count C/W_g, where C=2^(-m/2)s^(-m)Gamma((R-m)/2)/Gamma(R/2).
Interface: This is the residual/delta-conditioned measure, not intrinsic Hausdorff surface measure; on regular fibers it includes the coarea Jacobian. Full-row-rank fibers are assumed almost everywhere with finite positive W_g. The singular-value lower bound and target-energy evaluation are supplied and verified inputs, not hidden oracles. For a verified uniform E_g<=beta, Jensen gives expected trials <=exp(beta/2) C sqrt(det T), T_ij=tr(A_iA_j^T)+c_i^T c_j. The zero-target theorem has the simplest interface; affine and nonlinear targets incur separate explicit correction costs.
Proof spine: The positive inverse-determinant Gaussian lift represents det(S)^(-1/2) as a Gaussian integral. Completing the square yields a positive dual density v(lambda) and a conditional Gaussian for X. The R-th singular-value condition bounds det(I+A_lambda A_lambda^T) below by (1+s^2||lambda||^2)^R, whose Student-t envelope has an explicit normalizer and exact sampler. Multiplying by the two acceptance factors recovers the stated x marginal; Gaussian projection supplies the correct fiber conditional. Tonelli and the finite envelope integral control normalization.
Costs: Exactness is stated in an ideal-real model with exact Gaussian, chi-square and uniform variates. Each trial uses finite-dimensional matrix factorizations and linear solves; expected trials are exactly C/W_g and can be large. R=Omega(m^2), aggregate near-isotropy, and a bounded target energy give a sufficient constant expected-trial regime with polynomial certificate/per-trial arithmetic. The useful orthonormal subspace U and elliptic Q are not automatically found. No uniform finite-bit, generic nonlinear, or condition-independent polynomial-time implementation follows.
Failure: Rank alone and an arbitrarily loose valid envelope do not bound useful acceptance. The scalar product-zero example has a nonnormalizable positive auxiliary envelope even when a different target construction may exist. Fourier duality is oscillatory for a nonzero target. Arbitrary nonlinear target composition can encode rare-event conditioning, so no generic acceptance bound follows. Projection of Y with an unconditioned X prior misses the determinant weight. Surface-area and delta-conditioned laws differ. These are scoped failures, not complexity lower bounds.
Closest comparator: Gaussian auxiliary-field identities, coarea/manifold conditioning, Gaussian conditional laws, Wishart sampling and MCMC determinant-cancellation precede this construction. Ellam et al. (2017) is cited as a close Gaussian auxiliary-variable/MCMC comparator. The exact combined independent-envelope formulation has unresolved historical priority; intake did not perform an independent literature search.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the residual-disintegration identity and both rejection stages; audit the R-th singular-value certificate, normalizers, singular-fiber limit and target-energy cost. Then check prior art for the exact combined theorem without conflating delta conditioning with surface-area sampling.

title: Collective stable rank yields an exact Gaussian dual envelope and a scoped finite-output W1 theorem
text:
N590-collective-stable-rank-exact-sampling-and-finite-output-wasserstein | Collective stable rank yields an exact Gaussian dual envelope and a scoped finite-output W1 theorem
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The 2026-10-10 packet reports internally derived sampler theorems, exact arithmetic checks, and a fixed-input finite-bit prototype. This intake checked source/archive hashes, JSON syntax, and repository routing only; it did not execute scientific scripts, replay numerical draws, independently reconstruct the proofs, or obtain external/formal verification.
