Claim: Let rational linearly independent p-by-n matrices A_i have Frobenius Gram H_ij=tr(A_i A_j^T), s(lambda)=lambda^T H lambda=||A_lambda||_F^2. If integer r>m satisfies the collective stable-rank bound ||A_lambda||_op^2<=s(lambda)/r for every lambda, then the homogeneous positive dual v(lambda)=det(I+A_lambda A_lambda^T)^(-1/2) obeys exp(-s/2)<=v(lambda)<=(1+s/r)^(-r/2). Either rational certificate M_p=sum_ij(H^(-1))_ij A_iA_j^T<=I_p/r or M_n=sum_ij(H^(-1))_ij A_i^T A_j<=I_n/r suffices. An exact ideal sampler proposes lambda=sqrt(r)H^(-1/2)Z/sqrt(V), V~chi-square_(r-m), accepts by v/h_r, then samples the conditional Gaussian X and projects Y onto ker F(X); its success is at least a_(r,m)=(2/r)^(m/2)Gamma(r/2)/Gamma((r-m)/2). Separately, the source states that for rational homogeneous g=c=0 inputs, a native M_p certificate and r>=4(m+1)^2 yield a finite-random-bit algorithm with W1 joint-law error<=epsilon and residual norm<=epsilon, using time/bits polynomial in input bit length, dimensions and log(1/epsilon). This finite-output theorem is not exact finite-bit equality conditioning and is not TV approximation to a continuous law.
Interface: The exact sampler assumes independent standard Gaussian prior coordinates, rational A_i, full-rank input family and a native collective stable-rank certificate. The finite-output theorem is narrower: homogeneous zero target, rational inputs, M_p certificate, r>=4(m+1)^2, rational 0<epsilon<1, independent uniform random bits, and W1 plus a residual guarantee. The theorem and the accompanying implementation are distinct evidence: the source prototype handles two 128x128 int64-numerator matrices with denominator 4096 and recomputes a native certificate r=62>=36 (m=2); arbitrary dimensions and rational encodings are not implemented.
Proof spine: The rational Gram matrix converts the span to conceptual Frobenius-orthonormal coordinates. PSD certificates bound both matrix-side operators and imply ||A_lambda||_op^2<=s/r. Concavity of log(1+u) yields r log(1+s/r)<=log det(I+A_lambda A_lambda^T)<=s; hence the Student-t envelope. Integrating the lower Gaussian bound yields the exact acceptance lower bound. The source’s finite-output proof separately charges the trial cap, normal tails, small singular values, arithmetic/coupling errors and output residual to obtain W1 control; it is a written analytic candidate, not certified by the finite examples.
Costs: The PSD sufficient verifier and per-trial matrix work are polynomial in dimensions and rational bit lengths; it is not a complete recognizer. Expected exact trials are at most 1/a_(r,m); r=Omega(m^2) suffices for a dimension-independent bound, while subspace restriction consumes up to a+b units of r. Finite-output polynomial bit/time is claimed only under the stated homogeneous theorem and independent-uniform-bit model. The included implementation is fixed-input-format prototype evidence; its three saved single draws and timings are not benchmarks and do not prove the law or uniform performance.
Failure: No arbitrary nonlinear-target or generic affine finite-bit theorem follows. A finite output cannot have TV distance below one from a non-atomic continuous target; the source correctly uses W1 and a residual bound. The stronger theorem’s one-input prototype does not establish distributional accuracy or generic matrix support. Receipt checks reuse producer code and were not rerun here. Large-rank physics use remains unestablished; the source does not claim practical speed or novelty.
Closest comparator: This extends the source’s earlier minimum-singular-value envelope in a scoped homogeneous interface; it also relates to classical Gaussian augmentation, Wishart/Student sampling and determinant-cancellation methods. The exact collective-stable-rank acquisition and finite-output combination require broader priority review; no novelty claim is established.
Open verification: Independently derive the spectral envelope and gamma-ratio acceptance bound; audit the complete finite-output W1 proof, especially small-singular-value and coupling error allocations. Separately inspect the exact rational native certificate and replay the fixed-input implementation only under an explicitly scoped software-verification task. Determine prior art without treating one sample as a distributional result.

title: The harmonic Gauss-law dual has an exact Weyl density and a sharp real-exponent integrability threshold
text:
N591-weyl-gauss-law-dual-integrability-threshold | The harmonic Gauss-law dual has an exact Weyl density and a sharp real-exponent integrability threshold
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The 2026-10-10 packet reports internally derived sampler theorems, exact arithmetic checks, and a fixed-input finite-bit prototype. This intake checked source/archive hashes, JSON syntax, and repository routing only; it did not execute scientific scripts, replay numerical draws, independently reconstruct the proofs, or obtain external/formal verification. Physical acquisition and historical priority remain unresolved. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For D harmonic traceless-Hermitian k-by-k coordinate/momentum pairs, m=k^2-1 and G=-i sum_a[X_a,P_a], the positive dual on traceless Hermitian Lambda is v_D(Lambda)=det_R(I+L_Lambda L_Lambda*)^(-D/2). If the eigenvalues mu_a sum to zero, Weyl reduction gives v_D=product_{a<b}[1+(mu_a-mu_b)^2]^(-D), and the normalized eigenvalue density is proportional to product_{a<b}[(mu_a-mu_b)^2/(1+(mu_a-mu_b)^2)^D] on the trace-zero hyperplane. The source proves that the normalizing integral of this real-D family is finite iff D>1+1/k. In particular D=2 is normalizable for every finite k>=2, despite the generic stable-rank condition r>m failing at sufficiently large k. The gap density has a positive half-Cauchy product envelope and so an ideal-arithmetic rejection sampler exists, but no favorable acceptance scaling in k is established. The physical target is the classical high-temperature, zero-coupling harmonic Spin Matrix Theory phase-space ensemble with a common positive oscillator frequency; it is not interacting BFSS/BMN dynamics.
Interface: Here D is the number of independent harmonic matrix pairs in the physical model and is a positive integer. The integrability theorem separately extends the eigenvalue density to real D>0. k is gauge SU(k) size, independent of D. The law is residual/delta-conditioned, not intrinsic orbit-volume or Hausdorff surface measure; no additional spatial angular-momentum constraints are included. The commutator representation has structural stable rank r=Dk when explicitly supplied or accompanied by a checkable representation witness; the generic Casimir certificate alone returns only r<=D. At D=9, fixed SU(3)/SU(4) constants are source-reported, but the large-k D=9 regime is not efficient under these bounds.
Proof spine: Diagonalize Lambda. Each unordered eigenvalue pair contributes two real commutator singular directions of magnitude |mu_a-mu_b|, yielding the determinant product. Weyl’s change of variables contributes the Vandermonde square; ordered gaps give a positive density. For D=2, bounding nonadjacent factors by one and retaining adjacent Cauchy factors proves finite normalization at each k. For real D, the source proves necessity by a large-radius cone and sufficiency by ordered-gap sectors, assigning each pair to its largest intervening gap and integrating the resulting logarithmic variables; the threshold is D>1+1/k.
Costs: The gap dimension is k-1, followed by an independent Haar eigenbasis. The D=2 half-Cauchy rejection proposal establishes existence in ideal arithmetic only; its acceptance as k grows is not bounded favorably. The generic stable-rank envelope gives explicit fixed-rank constants for D=9 and SU(3)/SU(4), but r=Dk eventually fails r>m at fixed D. The finite-output theorem as originally stated requires r>=4(m+1)^2 and does not literally cover these D=9 examples; the source gives a checked fixed-(D,k) argument for r>2m with constants, but no implemented multiprecision physical sampler or practical timing claim.
Failure: Finite normalization is not efficient acquisition. The D=2 squared inverse-determinant L2 control used by the source’s finite-output argument diverges logarithmically near the origin for every k, so that precision proof cannot be extended merely by sharpening stable-rank constants. No replacement Lp or small-ball argument is proved. At fixed physical D=9, large gauge rank is not efficient under these bounds. The result is not a new physical law, quantum singlet sampler, interacting BFSS/BMN solution, or established historical novelty.
Closest comparator: The source identifies the target with Harmark–Orselli (2014) classical zero-coupling Spin Matrix Theory and distinguishes it from interacting classical matrix dynamics and Gaussian quantum thermal-circle methods. It also cites Cauchy-determinant and difference-eigenvalue-model antecedents; these citations and the physical convention were not independently checked during intake. No direct speed comparison or historical novelty evidence is claimed.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the commutator singular-value and Weyl Jacobian reduction, then audit both directions of the real-D integrability threshold including the trace-zero induced measure. Recheck the D=2 near-origin L2 divergence and the mapping to the cited Spin Matrix Theory ensemble. Determine whether a charged large-k eigenvalue proposal or replacement precision estimate exists; no polynomial sampler is assumed.

title: Maximum-rate stratification gives a finite-bit approximation to rare product-chain hitting times
text:
N592-rarity-uniform-product-chain-first-passage-approximation | Maximum-rate stratification gives a finite-bit approximation to rare product-chain hitting times
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source reports a complete internal proof and finite-bit specification. Intake performed static preservation and routing checks only; external correctness, formal verification, and historical priority remain UNKNOWN. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Let n independent two-state continuous-time Markov chains have rational stationary target probabilities p_i in (0,1), rational relaxation rates lambda_i>0, target-to-other rates (1-p_i)lambda_i and other-to-target rates p_i lambda_i, and the stationary product initial law. Let H be the first time all components occupy their designated joint target, with H=0 if initially there. For rational epsilon,delta in (0,1/2), the source specifies a randomized Turing algorithm outputting a nonnegative rational Hhat and proves an internal coupling claim P(|Hhat-H|>epsilon H)<=delta. Its asserted expected bit complexity is polynomial in total input bit length, n, epsilon^-1 and log(delta^-1), with no polynomial dependence on inverse target probability q^-1=(product_i p_i)^-1 or on rate ratios. It also derives sup_t |P(Hhat<=t)-P(H<=t)| <= delta-log(1-epsilon)/e. These are source-reported proof claims, not independently reconstructed by intake.
Interface: The target is one joint state and the initial law is the stationary product distribution. Only one approximate hitting time is returned. The source does not provide a trajectory, arbitrary-start hitting law, arbitrary target-set law, relative rare-tail error, exact continuous sampling, or total variation for the unquantized continuous law. Total variation is stated only for a requested finite binning with a separately charged boundary-error term.
Proof spine: The classical stationary renewal transform gives a geometric sum of exponential increments. The construction stratifies the activated Bernoulli rate sum by its maximum active rate, realizes the law as a Cox/Poisson mixture, and replaces only sufficiently large stratum sums by sample means. The finite-bit specification uses bounded dyadic uniforms, slack at the branch threshold, capped finite Poisson tables, explicit coupling budgets, and charged rational bit lengths; it avoids a Poisson oracle whose mean scales like q^-1.
Costs: The ideal-real construction reports O(n^3 epsilon^-2 log(4n/delta)) elementary increment work. The finite-bit theorem reports expected bit complexity polynomial in input bit length, n, epsilon^-1 and log(delta^-1); rare target probability and extreme rate ratios affect arithmetic representation length, not a polynomial number of simulated transitions. The source Python programs are floating-point demonstrations and do not implement or certify the finite-bit specification.
Failure: Brown’s exact stationary hitting-time representation is established prior art, and non-enumerative product-chain approximations already exist. The source only identifies the maximum-rate-stratified compressed coupling and its encoded complexity as potentially distinct; priority is UNKNOWN. Its numerical checks are finite floating-point observations, not the theorem proof. No unquantized TV or relative rare-tail guarantee follows.
Closest comparator: Brown (1974 report/1975 publication), as stated by Fill–Lyzinski, supplies the exact stationary geometric-sum representation. Horvath–Paolieri–Vicario (2025) give a non-enumerative product-chain ODE approximation. The source also credits established exponential-mixture, mixed-Poisson, and large-jump mean-replacement methods. The claimed distinction is only the combined maximum-active-rate stratification and rarity/rate-uniform finite-bit coupling bound; no priority clearance is established. Source prior-art notes: updates/CK/package/distinct_capability_20261010/04_prior_art_notes.md.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the finite-bit coupling and all probability/bit-cost budgets, then compare the exact encoded contract with the cited first-passage and mixed-Poisson literature. Keep the floating-point prototype separate from the Turing algorithm theorem.

title: Chebyshev fast-forwarding has exponential signed-mass cost on regular-tree walks
text:
N593-chebyshev-signed-particle-fast-forwarding-obstruction | Chebyshev fast-forwarding has exponential signed-mass cost on regular-tree walks
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The exact tree calculation is source-reported and was not independently reconstructed by intake. It rules out one stated estimator mechanism only. External review and any general fast-forwarding conclusion remain unresolved.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For simple random walk P=A/d on the infinite d-regular tree, d>=3, the Chebyshev polynomial T_k(P) has signed endpoint mass satisfying sum_y |T_k(P)(x,y)| >= [2(d-1)/d]^(k-1), for k>=1. The same witness applies in a finite d-regular graph when the radius-k neighborhood of x is a tree. Consequently any single signed-particle estimator W delta_Y with E[W 1{Y=y}]=T_k(P)(x,y) has E|W| at least this large and E[W^2] at least its square. This is a source-reported exact obstruction to the proposed signed-particle representation.
Interface: Classical simple random walk on a d-regular tree, Chebyshev first-kind polynomial, and an unbiased one-particle signed representation of the polynomial endpoint measure. The result concerns this estimator form and this local tree witness, not arbitrary access to a finite transition matrix or global algorithms.
Proof spine: At distance k, lower powers vanish and P^k(x,y)=d^-k. The leading coefficient of T_k is 2^(k-1), and there are d(d-1)^(k-1) vertices at distance k. Summing the absolute mass over that sphere gives the exponential lower bound. Unbiasedness forces E|W| to dominate the l1 norm, and Jensen gives E[W^2]>=(E|W|)^2.
Costs: For d>=3 the base 2(d-1)/d exceeds one, so the l1 mass and second-moment requirement grow exponentially with k for this representation. A positive universal-cover/nonbacktracking representation is also given, but its expected reduced path length remains linear in t for d>=3; the d=2 diffusive case is standard.
Failure: This is not a general classical fast-forwarding lower bound, a lower bound for all signed decompositions using multiple particles, or an obstruction to explicit global-state access. The separate bounded-radius locality observation applies only to local-output procedures. The broader proposed capability was stopped at this mechanism gate.
Closest comparator: The source credits established Chebyshev/nonbacktracking representations, including Apers–Sarlette quantum fast-forwarding, Alon–Benjamini–Lubetzky–Sodin nonbacktracking walks, and Biswas–Pyne–Rubinfeld local random-walk access. These works use distinct access models; the present obstruction does not subsume them.
Open verification: Test a different positive or global-access mechanism against this signed-mass obstruction without inferring a general no-fast-forwarding theorem from it.

title: Weighted cubic closure characterizes exact one-port recovery and the canonical minimal realization
text:
N594-cubic-network-observability-criterion-and-canonical-minimal-model | Weighted cubic closure characterizes exact one-port recovery and the canonical minimal realization
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Complete internal derivations and a targeted internal audit are reported in the packet. No proof was independently reconstructed by intake. External correctness, formal verification, and historical priority remain UNKNOWN; no 8–10/10 breakthrough is established.

Claim: For a finite-dimensional system xdot=-Kx-diag(alpha)x^{circ3}+e_1 u, y=x_1, x(0)=0, with real symmetric positive-definite K and unknown positive alpha_i, let W be the smallest linear subspace containing e_1, K-invariant, and closed under T(v,w,z)=alpha componentwise-multiplied by v,w,z. Under the source’s exact zero-initial ordered-pulse endpoint-germ interface, known physical dimension N is globally identifiable up to hidden signed permutations fixing e_1 if and only if W=R^N. If W is proper, changing K by a positive perturbation on W-perp can preserve all input-output responses. Without a supplied N, the complete exact input-output germ determines a unique minimum-dimensional realization within the same positive heterogeneous cubic class, of dimension dim W. The source also parameterizes all larger equivalent realizations by weighted signed coordinate blocks, inactive coordinates, and arbitrary positive-definite dynamics on the orthogonal complement. These are source-reported internal theorem candidates.
Interface: The port, input/output scales, zero initial state, exact cubic constitutive law, symmetric SPD K, and positive nodewise cubic coefficients are part of the model. Observations are exact endpoint germs of ordered positive-duration pulses with amplitudes 0 and 1; exact mixed derivatives/IO word coefficients and exact Hankel/Gram rank decisions are assumed. The full-model result is modulo hidden signed permutations fixing e_1. The all-dimension minimality theorem is only within finite-dimensional symmetric-SPD positive-heterogeneous-cubic models.
Proof spine: Directional cubic derivatives yield positive atomic moment sequences whose support projections identify active coordinates without observing hidden states. Lie-bracket/observable identities construct K action and weighted triple products on paired directions; exact Gram closure recovers W and proves necessity/sufficiency. After rescaling by diag(sqrt(alpha_i)), every ternary-closed subspace is a span of disjoint signed block indicators. The quotient coefficient is alphabar_B=(sum_{i in B} 1/alpha_i)^-1, and K restricts to the canonical quotient while an arbitrary SPD operator remains on W-perp.
Costs: The source gives finite exact word-jet and adaptive positive-Hankel/Gram certificates, including when N is not supplied, but exact real derivatives, rank/equality tests and root decisions are ideal information. Conservative jet-depth bounds grow rapidly; no stable finite-noise estimator or useful physical acquisition cost follows. In general physical dimension and residual hidden dynamics are not identifiable.
Failure: A proper W leaves K on W-perp invisible; all equivalent realizations can differ in inactive coordinates, block refinements and residual SPD dynamics. Exact flatness and zero Gram residuals are not statistical tests. The source’s focused internal audit found no blocking algebraic gap under its exact class, but this intake did not reconstruct the proof; external correctness, formal verification and priority remain UNKNOWN.
Closest comparator: Nonlinear input-output identifiability, Volterra methods and signed-permutation gauges have established predecessors, including Albertini–Sontag (1993) and Vanelli–Hendrickx, arXiv:2412.08472v4. The source distinguishes known-topology or local identifiability from its exact dense/sparse one-port closure criterion and cross-dimensional minimal quotient; this is not priority clearance.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the positive-moment support recovery, paired K/T closure, cross-dimensional stopping certificate, and exhaustive weighted signed-block classification. Keep exact-word-germ identifiability distinct from finite-noise or physically acquired recovery, then assess the cited nonlinear-identification prior art.

title: A homogeneous cubic law reveals physical node count from the exact one-port quotient
text:
N595-homogeneous-m-matrix-cubic-network-node-census | A homogeneous cubic law reveals physical node count from the exact one-port quotient
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source reports a complete internal census derivation. Intake did not independently reconstruct it. External correctness, formal verification, and priority remain UNKNOWN; this result does not establish practical noisy node counting.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Assume the exact model and input-output germ of N594. If every physical node has the same unknown alpha>0, K is symmetric positive definite with K_ij<=0 for i!=j, and its off-diagonal graph is connected, then each active synchrony block B has reduced cubic coefficient alphabar_B=alpha/|B|, no physical coordinates are inactive, and |B|=alpha/alphabar_B is an integer. The one-port coefficient identifies alpha, so the exact germ determines the physical node count N=sum_B alpha/alphabar_B, even though hidden internal connections/eigenvalues can remain unidentifiable. This is a source-reported exact-data consequence, not a noisy census procedure.
Interface: Homogeneous positive cubic coefficient at every physical node, irreducible symmetric SPD M-matrix coupling (off-diagonals nonpositive and connected), same zero-initial single-port input/output and exact endpoint-germ interface as N594. Unknown alpha is allowed because it is identified at the port. No finite-noise observation contract is provided.
Proof spine: The canonical quotient of N594 has reduced block coefficient alpha/|B|. Irreducible SPD M-matrix positivity gives K^-1 e_1 strictly positive; K-invariance places this vector in W, excluding inactive coordinates and mixed-sign blocks. Thus all blocks are ordinary synchronized node blocks and their multiplicities are recovered as alpha/alphabar_B.
Costs: The count follows from the exact adaptive quotient/finite-jet certificate of N594 and exact identification of reduced cubic coefficients. This does not identify hidden within-block stiffness or transverse residual dynamics, and exact integer/rank decisions do not provide finite-noise sample costs.
Failure: The common-alpha and connected SPD M-matrix hypotheses are material. Signed off-diagonal couplings can leave inactive coordinates; heterogeneous alpha can produce the same harmonic coefficient sum for different block sizes. Weak coupling makes the exact census arbitrarily ill-conditioned. The formula is not a general node-count method.
Closest comparator: Local network-size estimation can return minimal realization order while merging synchronized nodes; Tang et al., New Journal of Physics 22 (2020), 093031, is cited in the source. Brovia et al. (2026), DOI 10.1063/5.0318179, is a close modern predecessor. The proposed distinction is using the homogeneous cubic coefficient to lift a one-port minimal quotient to physical multiplicities; priority remains UNKNOWN.
Open verification: Reconstruct the inverse-positivity and signed-block argument, check both necessity counterexamples (signed couplings and heterogeneous coefficients), and search prior work on inferring multiplicities from a nonlinear minimal quotient.

title: A cubic response contraction can recover physical coordinates beyond the ambient tensor nullspace
text:
N596-one-port-cubic-response-physical-coordinate-reconstruction | A cubic response contraction can recover physical coordinates beyond the ambient tensor nullspace
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The exact contraction and generic recovery are source-reported internal derivations. No proof was independently reconstructed by intake. The campaign reports no practical advantage or external validation; historical priority remains UNKNOWN.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For the first-order model xdot=-Kx-diag(alpha)x^{circ3}+e_1u, y=x_1, with real symmetric SPD K, positive nodewise alpha_i and known dimension, the source derives an exact H1/H3 contraction. On a generic subclass with simple K eigenvalues, nonzero port modal overlaps, and nonzero pairwise-distinct hidden weights beta_i=alpha_i K_{i1}^2, the contraction B(s,t)=sum_{i>1} beta_i q_i(s)q_i(t), q(s)=(sI+K)^-1e_1, forms a symmetric matrix in the H1 modal basis whose eigenvectors recover the physical coordinates up to hidden signed permutation. The argument targets the needed contraction and does not reconstruct the full ambient quartic tensor. This remains an internally derived source candidate with an unverified acquisition interface.
Interface: Exact linear response H1 and cubic Volterra response H3 for the known first-order constitutive model, zero initial state and a single driven/measured coordinate. The original coefficient is recovered using a high-opposite-frequency limit or a finite-R extrapolation; H1 supplies modal poles and port weights. This is an exact kernel identity, not an assumption that hidden states or the full H3 tensor are directly measured at no cost.
Proof spine: The high-opposite-frequency pair separates the port contribution from hidden-node terms in H3. After subtracting the port term, the coefficient is a bilinear sum over hidden resolvent coordinates weighted by beta_i. In the H1 modal basis this is U^T diag(0,beta_2,...,beta_n)U; distinct eigenvalues of that matrix expose the physical mode rows, after which K and the nodewise nonlinear coefficients follow.
Costs: The source describes finite low-frequency evaluations after the asymptotic identity, but the first-order high-frequency route is noise-sensitive and the inverse can be exponentially ill-conditioned. No end-to-end acquisition, stable finite-noise bound, or advantage over nonlinear identification is established. The O(n^3) bounded-frequency query count belongs to a separate second-order oscillator model recorded in N597, not this first-order card.
Failure: Zero direct port coupling, repeated hidden beta values, repeated K eigenvalues or zero modal overlap defeat this particular reconstruction step but are not impossibility theorems for other kernels. High-frequency cancellation can suppress the hidden signal severely. The source’s focused prior-art review identifies parallel Wiener–Hammerstein/Volterra branch separation as a strong structural overlap; the exact physical-coordinate recovery distinction and priority remain unresolved.
Closest comparator: The source compares the cubic branch sum with parallel Wiener–Hammerstein identification and cites established Volterra/tensor methods, nonlinear frequency-response identification, and Vanelli–Hendrickx arXiv:2412.08472v4. These precedents prevent claims of novelty for branch separation or nonlinear network identifiability in general.
Open verification: Independently derive the H1/H3 contraction and the physical-coordinate recovery under every nondegeneracy condition; reconcile it with the source’s acquisition audit and compare with parallel Wiener–Hammerstein physical-parameter recovery.

Therefore intake retains the algebraic query construction and the conditional resource claim as source evidence, while the robust uniform stability/acquisition theorem remains unresolved.
Interface: Known dimension, identity mass, known scalar damping gamma>0, symmetric SPD K, positive nodewise cubic coefficients, one real input/output port. The source’s sufficient promise uses bounded eigenvalues m<=lambda_i<=M, a known eigenvalue gap delta, modal overlaps bounded below by a_min, hidden beta separation b (including separation from zero), and gamma<=Delta0/(400n) for Delta0=min(delta/(2sqrt(M)),sqrt(m)); independent sub-Gaussian readout noise is used in its sampling calculation. H3 values are obtained by phase-cycled finite real waveforms, not supplied free by the physical device.
Proof spine: At each low-frequency pair, the third-order response is a rational function of the opposite-frequency parameter with 4n known poles. Interpolation from bounded imaginary frequencies recovers the desired high-order residue coefficient; 4n samples per each of n^2 low-frequency pairs give 4n^3 H3 kernel queries. The resulting symmetric modal matrix can be diagonalized to recover physical coordinates under distinct hidden weights. Phase cycling extracts a cubic kernel estimate from 64 real waveform runs per replicate, with a finite-amplitude remainder and settling/reset budget stated in s41.

The s41 source additionally claims polynomial dependence on n, spectral range/gaps, damping, overlaps, beta separation, target error and failure probability, with 64 phase-cycled runs per kernel replicate and H1 calibration. The campaign’s operational forecast gives no advantage over a matched physical-likelihood baseline; no physical acquisition is reported.

Hald’s Jacobi reconstruction, nonlinear frequency-response methods, and Vanelli–Hendrickx network identifiability are also credited for their narrower interfaces. Historical priority remains UNKNOWN.

With independent Gaussian scalar readout noise of scale sigma, the source derives KL(P_K,P_Kprime)<=N C^2 epsilon^8/(2 sigma^2), hence N=Omega(sigma^2 epsilon^-8/C^2) samples for fixed-success discrimination; continuous white-noise observation charges total time in the same way. This rules out a uniform robust finite-noise recovery bound over the unrestricted generic SPD family under that interface, but does not refute exact identifiability. Separately, the source reports an n=8 conditional forecast with 145.7 million scalar samples and 32.9% K RMS error, versus a 2.59% local-oracle likelihood benchmark; these are not theorem bounds or executed global estimators.

The continuous-time white-noise analogue charges observation time. The finite n=8 forecast assumes supplied H1, common alpha and a specified perturbative acquisition protocol; reset/calibration and residual nonlinear costs remain unresolved.

The Gaussian KL chain rule then makes the n-sample information O(N epsilon^8/sigma^2), and a two-point testing argument yields the sample lower bound. This acquisition obstruction is independent of a particular estimator within the stated observation model.

A separate source forecast for n=8, gamma=.03, common known alpha reports 1.457e8 scalar samples and 0.32901 relative K RMS error; its local likelihood comparator reports 0.02587. It does not rule out stronger input/output interfaces, instance-dependent costs, or uniformly conditioned subclasses. The phase-family calculation concerns a complex-valued unit-modulus function and the corresponding Fourier probability/degree statistics; those are not the same theorem domain.

Thus h_2(epsilon)/epsilon diverges, but the construction leaves the Boolean codomain and cannot refute Boolean FEI. The proposed Boolean coordinate inequality remains an unproved sufficient route.

text:
N602-finite-bit-rare-clock-implementation-replay-certificate | An exact-arithmetic finite-bit implementation records compressed rare-clock acquisitions
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The exact-arithmetic code, mathematical certificate, audit, fixtures and 17-test result are source-reported. The input-bit assumption, external correctness, formal verification, historical novelty and broader practical capability remain unresolved. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.

Claim: For four independent two-state continuous-time Markov chains with stationary product initial law, dyadic target probabilities p=(1/8,1/16,1/32,1/16), relaxation rates (1,2,4,8), and one joint target, the source provides a Python-standard-library implementation that returns a nonnegative rational approximation to the stationary first-hitting time using integer and exact-rational arithmetic. Under its stated independent-unbiased-input-bits assumption, the source certificate gives the requested instance epsilon=1/4, delta=1/20 and conservative failure bound 59429/5242880 < 0.011336. For a deterministic recorded tape, the source reports an exact rational same-tape enclosure with relative discrepancy upper bound 0.001652145 for every extension of its accepted finite uniform cells. A separate q=2^-200 fixture reports all four strata compressed using 29,401 exponential cells; one OS-backed acquisition and its exact prefix replay are also recorded. The packet reports 17 passing implementation tests and an internal code-and-mathematics audit. This is an implementation supplement to N592, not a second general theorem.
Interface: The implementation gate accepts dyadic target probabilities strictly between zero and one, positive rational relaxation rates, rational epsilon and delta, and an independent stationary product initial law for one joint target. Component i has target-to-other rate (1-p_i)lambda_i and other-to-target rate p_i lambda_i. The moderate replay uses exactly n=4, p=(1/8,1/16,1/32,1/16), lambda=(1,2,4,8), q=1/65536, epsilon=1/4 and delta=1/20. The theorem-level rational-input contract remains the broader source-reported N592 construction. Randomized guarantees assume independent unbiased bit streams; the recorded SHA256 fixtures are deterministic, and the single OS entropy acquisition does not certify physical independence.
Proof spine: The implementation preserves the maximum-activated-rate strata and Brown/Cox representation used by N592. It encloses finite dyadic-cell exponential values by rational intervals using an atanh-series logarithm, makes branch decisions with explicit slack, samples small-stratum counts through bounded exponential-arrival cells, and compresses large strata with a fixed sample mean. The certificate separately accounts for cell rejection, branch ambiguity, count caps, large-stratum concentration, finite arithmetic and output error. The code and certificate are source-provided; intake did not independently reconstruct them.
Costs: For the specified moderate preflight, the source bounds expected exponential calls by 142,884. A deterministic SHA fixture records 15,849 exponential cells and 1,619,385 input bits; the same-tape reference uses 55,468 marks. The q=2^-200 fixture records 29,401 cells and 5,313,694 bits (about 0.91 seconds on the source environment). The single OS-backed acquisition records 14,769 cells and 1,514,177 bits. These are source-reported bounds and finite measurements, not uniform wall-clock guarantees or a statistical accuracy study.
Failure: The probability bound is conditional on mutually independent unbiased input bits; finite deterministic fixtures and one OS-backed acquisition do not validate that source assumption. The exact same-tape discrepancy is specific to the recorded finite-cell extension and is not a relative rare-tail or statistical failure-rate guarantee. The implementation only admits dyadic target probabilities, even though the broader N592 theorem candidate states a rational-input result. The audit and 17-test receipt are internal source reports, not a machine-checked proof or an independent intake reproduction. There is no exact path sampler, arbitrary-start result, arbitrary target-set result, continuous-law total-variation claim, external validation, or historical-priority determination.
Closest comparator: The packet credits Brown’s stationary first-hitting-time representation as exact prior work and cites a non-enumerative product-chain ODE approximation by Horváth, Paolieri and Vicario. The source presents its proposed distinction as a finite-bit rarity/rate-uniform guarantee and a concrete exact-arithmetic realization; this intake does not establish priority or a historic-scale capability.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the N592 coupling and probability/bit-cost proof, inspect and replay the exact integer/rational implementation including the recorded SHA and OS-prefix paths, and compare its accepted dyadic input/output contract with the broader theorem statement. Keep the N592 gate open until correctness, source assumptions, and prior-art scope are independently addressed.

title: Polar repair cost is governed by leakage, not deletion rank
text:
N603-polar-repair-and-concentrated-compression-error | Polar repair cost is governed by leakage, not deletion rank
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The attached LaTeX report is preserved exactly. Its mathematical arguments and diagnostics are source-reported; intake performed source-integrity and repository-routing checks only. No proof was independently reconstructed, no source script or replay was executed, cited literature was not independently checked, and external/formal correctness and historical priority remain UNKNOWN. This campaign did not establish flexible normalized Hilbert–Schmidt stability or a historic-scale breakthrough.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Use the source convention ||X||_{2,n}^2=Tr(X*X)/n even on a corner of C^n. For an orthogonal projection P, Q=I-P, U in U(n), A=QUQ restricted to Q C^n, and T=QU*PUQ restricted to Q C^n, the report gives inf_{V in U(Q C^n)} ||A-V||_{2,n}^2 = Tr((I_Q-sqrt(I_Q-T))^2)/n, between Tr(T^2)/(4n) and Tr(T^2)/n. With B=PUQ, T=B*B, so the cost is controlled by Tr((B*B)^2)/n, not rank alone. It also gives, for every integer q>=2, n=q^4 and a swap of two q^2-dimensional spaces for which an error of normalized size epsilon=q^-2 is killed by deleting an epsilon fraction, while the compressed unitary needs repair distance q^-1=sqrt(epsilon).
Interface: P is an orthogonal projection of rank k, Q=I-P, and the compressed operator acts on Q C^n. Every normalized Hilbert-Schmidt norm in this result uses denominator n, not n-k. The example is a finite-dimensional matrix construction.
Proof spine: A*A=I_Q-T. If s_j are singular values of A and t_j are eigenvalues of T, the closest-unitary Frobenius distance is sum_j(1-s_j)^2 with s_j=sqrt(1-t_j). The scalar bound t/2<=1-sqrt(1-t)<=t gives the two trace bounds. In the example, QUQ has q^2 zero singular values and the rest equal to one.
Costs: No computational, acquisition, or runtime claim is supplied; this is an exact finite-matrix argument as reported by the source.
Failure: This refutes a norm-only compression lemma and shows deletion rank is not a sufficient repair-cost statistic. It does not refute flexible stability for any particular group, establish a group-specific obstruction, or prove that all compression methods fail.
Closest comparator: The pasted record itself is the only proof source. The formula is a local matrix interface; no broader group-stability consequence follows without an additional theorem.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the nearest-unitary formula under the original-dimension normalization, check both inequalities and the q^4 example, and state precisely which proposed norm-only compression implication is invalid.

Thus the conjugation operator induced on the full Hilbert ultraproduct of (M_n,||.||_{2,n}) does not satisfy s^2=1. Claim: Let U_s in U(n), supplied skew-adjoint corrections b_s satisfy max_s||b_s||_{2,n}<=C epsilon, and w be a relator word of length L. Define F_b(t)=w((e^{t b_s}U_s)_s), D=F_b(0)-I, and L_U(b)=F_b\prime(0). Assume E=D+L_U(b) satisfies ||E||_{2,n}<=eta. For tau,sigma>0 the report claims an exact decomposition F_b(1)-I=R_diffuse+R_debt with ||R_diffuse||_{2,n}<=eta+(L^2/2)tau C epsilon, rank(R_debt)/n<=2L|S|C^2 epsilon^2/tau^2+eta^2/sigma^2, and ||R_debt||_op<=2+sigma+(L^2/2)tau^2. Each corrected generator remains unitary and moves by at most C epsilon in normalized Hilbert-Schmidt norm.
Interface: Corrections b_s are supplied, skew-adjoint, and small in normalized Hilbert-Schmidt norm; the linearized residual E is also supplied through the assumption ||E||<=eta. The word length L, number of generators |S|, and cutoffs tau,sigma are explicit. This is not an algorithm for finding b_s.
Proof spine: The source splits b_s=l_s+h_s by spectral cutoff tau, bounds rank(h_s)/n by C^2 epsilon^2/tau^2, Taylor-expands the low-frequency path, telescopes high-frequency and inverse-letter changes into a rank-bounded term, and splits E by singular-value threshold sigma. The diffuse and debt terms are defined by that construction.
Costs: No end-to-end runtime or method for acquiring b_s is provided. For tau=epsilon^alpha the diffuse nonlinear term is O(epsilon^(1+alpha)) and rank debt O(epsilon^(2-2alpha))n, but the bounded debt may have Hilbert-Schmidt size O(epsilon^(1-alpha)), larger than epsilon.
Failure: Existence of suitable corrections, admissibility of the linear residual, and a compatible o(n)-enlargement that removes the debt are unproved. The source explicitly says this is not a superlinear total-error bound and supplies no flexible-stability conclusion.
Closest comparator: This is a conditional matrix update, not a proof of the flexible group-stability target. N607 separately records why generic low-rank debt cannot be completed for all approximants.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the spectral truncation and Taylor estimates, especially inverse letters, the 2L|S| rank factor, operator-norm debt, and the singular-value split. Then identify a justified source of corrections and a compatible completion theorem before using it for group stability.

Padding by I_m bounds top-left, cross, and lower-right block errors; an eight-letter telescoping estimate then gives the stated lower bound.

title: Rank-absorbing stratification gives exact local stationary samples at fixed depth
text:
N610-rank-absorbing-stratified-exact-local-stationary-sampling | Rank-absorbing stratification gives exact local stationary samples at fixed depth
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The attached note supplies a theorem proof candidate and source-reported numerical checks. This intake preserved and routed the originals and checked hashes only; no sampler or verifier was run, no proof was independently reconstructed, formal/external correctness and priority remain UNKNOWN, and no historic-scale breakthrough is established.

Claim: The source states an exact sampler for the joint stationary law of any fixed finite batch of raw coordinates at specified times in a finite-depth, finite-field network whose same-level update is affine, whose deterministic forcing depends only on strictly lower levels, whose parent count is at most k, and whose site-time category has Haar-reset probability s>0. If m coordinates are requested, c is the fixed depth, h=kc^2, and Q is the number of distinct update categories exposed, its bound is E[Q] <= (m/s) sum_{j=0}^{c-1}(1+h/s)^j. The category oracle is shared across levels so reset/gate correlations are preserved. The source also gives an exponential backward-depth tail for fixed c,m,k,s. These are source-reported theorem claims, not independently reconstructed here.
Interface: States lie in F_q^c. At a site-time one shared category chooses independent uniform Haar values for all coordinates with probability s, a locally known residual reset with probability r, or a gate with probability 1-s-r. At level ell the gate is linear in level-ell parents plus a deterministic function of strictly lower-level inputs; same-level nonlinear feedback is excluded. Parent acquisition, forcing descriptions and their evaluation are charged. Rational s,r support ideal exact random-bit draws; the reference implementation covers prime q, while the note states a mathematical finite-field generalization.
Proof spine: Process same-level dependencies in descending time while tracking coefficient vectors and the span V generated by independent Haar contributions. If a coefficient lies in V, an independent uniform vector U_V absorbs any unknown contribution in V in distribution (U_V+vZ has law U_V); this is distributional masking, not pathwise coalescence. Otherwise expose the category, propagate affine coefficients, retain lower-layer forcing terms without expanding them, and recurse on lower levels using the same memoized category field. A layer induction yields exact joint laws; negative-binomial domination gives the displayed expected-query bound.
Costs: At most cQ site-layer visits and kcQ parent incidences are reported. For fixed c the source states expected arithmetic/bit cost polynomial in m,k,1/s,log q and the acquired forcing-description/evaluation costs; its exponent and constants may grow sharply with c. The source reports a failed costly million-site run at k=5,s=.09 and a completed source-reported run at k=3,s=.20. These demonstrations were not rerun by intake.
Failure: No same-level nonlinear feedback, unbounded parent access, arbitrary nonlinear cellular automaton, full-state efficient sampling, or general full-chain O(log N) mixing theorem is established. Fixed-depth is essential to the recursive bound; low reset probability and larger depth can be practically prohibitive. Exactness assumes ideal independent randomness and does not follow from the source's pseudorandom statistical checks.
Closest comparator: The source cites coupling from the past, perfect sampling for probabilistic cellular automata, algebraic decomposition of nonlinear cellular automata, and noisy-CA ergodicity results as overlapping prior art. The exact novelty of this rank-absorbing layered construction is explicitly unverified; citations were not independently checked.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the adaptive memoized-category and cross-level conditional-independence arguments, verify the negative-binomial and exponential-tail bounds including forcing acquisition costs, and perform a full prior-art review before treating this as a theorem or novelty claim.

Claim: As a corollary of the stratified sampler, the source claims that a countable network with uniformly bounded parent incidence and the same finite-depth, strictly lower-level nonlinear forcing has a unique stationary probability measure on (F_q^c)^Lambda. Every finite-dimensional local marginal converges to stationarity uniformly over the initial configuration, with a source-stated exponential-in-time bound C exp(-gamma T); a finite list of stationary coordinates is sampleable with finite expected local oracle work. Constants may depend on the fixed observable batch and model parameters.
Interface: This is a local/fixed-observable result for countable sites, finite state alphabet, positive Haar-reset probability, uniformly bounded indegree and fixed finite level count. For multiple requested observation times, their prescribed separation must be accounted for separately; the simple terminal-time local mixing bound is not a global joint mixing guarantee.
Proof spine: Compactness of the countable product and the Feller property yield existence. The finite-depth rank/masking certificate closes before a random ancestry horizon with exponential tail and makes a target cylinder's law independent of all initial values on that event. The remaining total-variation discrepancy is bounded by the tail event; hence invariant measures agree on every finite cylinder and are equal.
Costs: The source reuses the fixed-batch oracle-work bound in N610. It gives no efficient algorithm for the entire infinite configuration and no system-size-independent cost for arbitrary global observables.
Failure: Uniqueness and convergence are restricted to the stratified model. The source explicitly distinguishes this from general positive-noise nonlinear cellular automata, where counterexamples to universal uniqueness are known. It does not imply O(log N) convergence of the full q^(Nc)-state finite network in total variation.
Closest comparator: The source cites existing ergodicity results for noisy algebraic cellular automata and known positive-noise obstructions. Its corollary's independent novelty is not established.
Open verification: Independently verify the compact-product Feller construction, the uniform-in-initial-configuration cylinder coupling/masking argument, and the parameter dependence of C and gamma; compare the exact class and conclusion against cited noisy-CA results.

Claim: Under the report's fixed-observer-plane and constant-shear model, w_x=v_x-beta z and w_y=v_y, the source derives d/dt[g(y)L+beta z H(y)]=-W_g+g(y)tau, with L=xv_y-yv_x, tau=dot L, G'=g and H=yg-G. For a stationary ensemble with integrable terms and no boundary contribution, E[W_g]=E[g tau], so a central acceleration predicts zero. A directional choice g=-e_x e_y |y| gives the stated observable. The report also constructs an exactly Newtonian circular-orbit selection rule s(phi)=(1+epsilon sin(2phi))/2 whose selected mean is 2epsilon/(3pi), equal to 0.02122066 at epsilon=.1 despite zero physical torque.
Interface: The cancellation is exact only for the stated shear observation model, fixed beta and stationary unselected ensemble. The report's application to actual astrometry is not an instrument-level theorem; finite-angle geometry, time-varying observer geometry, systemic-motion estimates, sample selection, ordinary Galactic tides, encounters and companions require control.
Proof spine: Differentiate g(y)L and beta z H(y); use xw_y-yw_x=L+beta yz and H'=yg' to cancel the unknown-depth term. Integrate the derivative over a stationary ensemble. For the counterexample, weight uniform phase on a Newtonian circular orbit by the stated inclusion probability and integrate explicitly.
Costs: The source reports calculations on a public 36-pair archive and primary numerical tables for 32 HARPS pairs, with eight overlaps and 60 distinct pairs overall; a 33-pair clean-sample intersection was used. Reported means have descriptive standard errors only and cohorts are heterogeneous. No selection-calibrated likelihood or decisive torque evidence was obtained; intake did not reacquire inputs or recalculate these values.
Failure: The selection counterexample proves that a nonzero statistic need not identify a noncentral force. The observed statistics do not establish or exclude the external-field mechanism, and source data are not a homogeneous, selection-calibrated sample. The identity eliminates a leading hidden-depth term only under its observation assumptions.
Closest comparator: The source identifies angular-momentum conservation, projected-angular-momentum methods and external-field anisotropy as prior context. Those literature comparisons were not independently checked; no new force or historical priority is claimed.
Open verification: Reconstruct the identity and its observation model, then acquire a selection-complete astrometric sample with covariance and multiplicity controls and separate the predicted torque from tides, encounters, companions and projection systematics.

Claim: For the report's exact midpoint-geometry and fixed-adopted-distance observation model, r^2=R^2+z^2 and v(z)=w+zb. Minimizing eta(z)=sqrt(R^2+z^2)|w+zb|^2/(2 G_N M) over admissible depth reduces interior extrema to 3Bz^3+4dz^2+(V+2BR^2)z+2dR^2=0, where B=|b|^2, d=w dot b, V=|w|^2; evaluating real roots and endpoints gives the minimum. At the source's adopted central inputs, four pairs in its harmonized 33-pair cohort have eta_min>1 (IDs 3,33,42,59; range 1.1468–1.3994), so no choice of line-of-sight depth alone makes those fixed inputs a bound isolated Newtonian two-body pair.
Interface: The inequality is conditional on the adopted central astrometry, radial velocities, component masses, exact perspective reconstruction and isolated two-body Newtonian model. It is a feasibility envelope over unknown depth, not a probabilistic orbit fit or a gravity test.
Proof spine: Differentiate eta(z), factor the positive denominator, and reduce its interior critical points to the displayed cubic. Compare all real critical points in the physically admissible domain with its limiting endpoints. The source reports agreement of this cubic method and numerical minimization on 100 constructed cases; intake did not rerun that check.
Costs: The source reports four central-input violations in the harmonized archive/primary intersection; in the separate primary 32-pair table only HD189739/HD189760 (archive ID 59) violates the envelope, matching a pair already flagged in the primary study. Error propagation over measurement covariance, unresolved multiplicity and stellar-model uncertainty is not a calibrated confidence procedure.
Failure: A violation does not falsify Newtonian gravity: the pair can be unbound or perturbed, or masses, velocities or astrometry can be wrong; an unseen companion can alter the model. The result reproduces a known observational issue and is not a new anomaly.
Closest comparator: The source relates the calculation to published wide-binary data and an already identified problematic pair. Source citations were not independently checked; no gravity-law conclusion is claimed.
Open verification: Independently derive the perspective vectors and cubic, then propagate the actual astrometric/radial-velocity/mass covariance and multiplicity uncertainty before interpreting any pair-level infeasibility.

title: Closed-pool racemization and a source-mixture invariant constrain Bennu glutamate histories
text:
N614-bennu-glutamate-isotope-racemization-and-source-mixture-invariants | Closed-pool racemization and a source-mixture invariant constrain Bennu glutamate histories
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The pasted thread contains source-reported mathematical derivations, analyses of published numerical data, and explicit failed scientific explanations. Claim: For a closed glutamate pool with symmetric isotope-independent racemization, each isotope-class handedness imbalance m_j contracts by the same factor e^(-2K), and positivity implies 2K <= -ln(max(|e_14|,|e_15|)). The report converts the three published central values to e_14=0.0527903 and e_15=0.0175575, giving at most 4.24 handedness-halving times under this model. For a racemic background plus one L-biased source followed by isotope-independent racemization, the source's heavy-nitrogen fraction is q_excess=(q_L-d q_D)/(1-d), with d=D/L; the central measurements imply delta15N_excess about -590.5 per mil. A fit with a typical-range source remains compatible with individual quoted spreads after modest shifts, so the central-value inference is not a calibrated exclusion.
Interface: Mix isotope delta values only after conversion to heavy-atom fractions q=R/(1+R), R=R_AIR(1+delta/1000). The racemization inequality assumes a closed pool without later formation, exchange, selective destruction or protected compartments. The one-source invariant assumes the stated background/source mixture and isotope-independent racemization. The printed measurement uncertainties use different definitions and raw replicate covariance was unavailable.
Proof spine: Write n_j=L_j+D_j and m_j=L_j-D_j. The closed symmetric racemization equations conserve n_j and solve m_j(t)=m_j(0)e^(-2K); requiring |m_j(0)|<=n_j(0) yields the positivity bound. In the source mixture, isotope-heavy fractions mix linearly in q, and solving the L/D-weighted mass balance for the excess source gives q_excess.
Costs: The source reports a typical-source compatibility fit with D/L=0.8124, D delta15N=275.82 per mil, L delta15N=220.29 per mil and source delta15N=-20 per mil, each within one quoted spread under its separate definition. It also describes an illustrative D/L standard-error interpretation. No joint likelihood was reconstructed from raw scans.
Failure: The -590.5 per mil source value is model-dependent and unstable as D/L approaches one; the uncertainty fit prevents treating it as a required exotic reservoir. The closed-pool racemization bound is not an age estimate and does not apply to open histories. This does not establish contamination, overturn the source paper, or identify a chemical history.
Closest comparator: The source notes precedents for static isotope-of-excess calculations and preserves published measurement controls; those source comparisons were not independently checked. No novel chemical mechanism is claimed.
Open verification: Independently verify the isotope-probability conversion and mixture algebra, then obtain replicate-level isotope scans/covariances and test source histories under explicit open-pool and racemization assumptions.

Claim: For the source's restricted zero-field model—an initially singlet electron pair, one nitrogen nucleus, isotropic H=a I dot S_1, and separate singlet/triplet product rates k_S,k_T—the reduced populated sector gives Y_S=k_S(k_T+w)/(k_S k_T+w(k_S+k_T)), with w=2v^2 A/(A^2+a^2/4), v=a sqrt(I(I+1))/2 and A=(k_S+k_T)/2. Under its additional rule that singlet events return glutamate with randomized handedness while triplet events destroy it, matching the published central isotope/chirality values requires initial enantiomeric excess e_0>=0.3829; a source numerical best constant-parameter survival is about 2.46e-6. This restricted model does not generate chirality from an initially racemic pool.
Interface: The Hamiltonian, initial singlet state, single nuclear coupling, zero field, reaction rates, returned-molecule handedness rule and destruction channel are imposed assumptions. Other nuclear couplings, exchange, relaxation, additional reactions, open-system reservoirs and the actual Bennu reaction path are not specified by evidence.
Proof spine: Reduce by conserved total angular momentum to the stated 2x2 sector; integrate its density-matrix reaction equations to obtain Y_S; clear positive denominators to express the isotope ratio inequality as a nonnegative-coefficient polynomial. The report says full density-matrix calculations agreed in five parameter cases, but neither algebra nor numerics were rechecked during intake.
Costs: The source reports parameter-mixture searches over more than 31,000 yield settings and an approximate survival optimum; this was not a certified global optimization. The small survival figure depends on the assumed returned-molecule chirality rule and is not a universal impossibility bound.

Separate published abundance and bulk-nitrogen measurements concern different aliquots, so the source's inventory comparison is a warning under a restrictive model, not an empirical refutation. The calculation is not evidence the reaction occurs in Bennu.

title: Beta-alanine isotope-pair data admit an exact correlation inversion and a sharp source-range bound
text:
N616-beta-alanine-isotope-pair-correlation-and-source-range-obstruction | Beta-alanine isotope-pair data admit an exact correlation inversion and a sharp source-range bound
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The pasted thread contains source-reported mathematical derivations, analyses of published numerical data, and explicit failed scientific explanations. This intake preserved the full text and extracted scoped results only; no calculations or literature claims were independently reproduced, raw-data gaps remain, and external correctness, formal verification, historical priority, and any foundational natural law remain unestablished.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For the two native backbone carbon indicators, let p=E(X_1+X_2)/2, c=P(X_1=X_2=1), r=P_1/(2P_0) and t=P_2/P_0. The source gives the exact inversion p=(r+t)/(1+2r+t), c=t/(1+2r+t); thus the singly substituted ratio alone does not identify mean heavy-carbon abundance. Under a source-mixture model where molecules form independently within reservoirs with heavy-carbon fraction P, c-p^2=Var(P). If every source lies in [a,b], Var(P)<=(p-a)(b-p), a sharp endpoint bound. The report's equal-marginal correlated benchmark predicts P_2/P_0 23.71 times its independent-backbone alternative for Bennu and 6.18 times for Murchison; these are conditional native-isotope predictions, not observed peaks. For the stated Bennu organic-material interval, the source reports a maximum covariance 134.28 times below its benchmark requirement, excluding that bounded source class under the chosen interface.
Interface: All probability equations refer to corrected native carbon probabilities. The source uses the displayed VPDB-ratio-to-probability interface, but applying that correction to this pair model is unverified. A derivatization reagent adds carbon, so native double-substitution ratios require the stated generating-polynomial deconvolution. Two 13C substitutions and one 18O substitution are separated by only 0.00246468 Da; calibrated line shapes, standards and integration are needed.
Proof spine: Express P0=1-2p+c, P1=2(p-c), P2=c and solve the ratio definitions for p,c. In a reservoir mixture c=E[P^2], p=E[P], so covariance equals Var(P); the pointwise inequality (P-a)(b-P)>=0 gives the sharp interval bound. Independent-position unequal marginals alone move r in the opposite direction. The source reports additional LP and generated-distribution checks, not replayed by intake.
Costs: The source reports Bennu and Murchison benchmark quantities and says the bounded Bennu source interval permits covariance at most 1.40165e-5 while the candidate needs 1.88210e-3. Raw isotope spectra were not acquired; fragment/reagent contributions and mass-line overlap prevent interpreting a nominal mass-plus-two count as the native carbon-pair signal.
Failure: The equal-marginal correlation distribution is one feasible construction, not a unique source history. The interval bound applies only to the cited organic-material source class, not every historical carbon-bearing phase; extreme reservoirs remain possible but unconnected to the amino acid. The central mechanism of mixing-induced isotope clumping is acknowledged as known prior art. No β-alanine origin or chirality mechanism is established.
Closest comparator: The source identifies prior work on mixing-induced doubly substituted species and apparent site-specific isotope effects. It explicitly demotes the general mechanism as prior art; the quantitative application and instrument caveats are source-reported, not a novelty claim.
Open verification: Acquire replicate-level raw mass spectra and calibration standards; verify native/reagent isotope deconvolution and line shapes; test the predicted doubly substituted abundance with a calibrated likelihood; only then compare bounded and extreme source histories.

title: A reset-language-preserving extension separates reset threshold from pair-distance MST
text:
N617-reset-language-extension-separates-reset-threshold-from-pair-mst | A reset-language-preserving extension separates reset threshold from pair-distance MST
status=source_derived_unreviewed; CQ preserves the exact independent-investigations directory and indexes only scoped claims and failures. Source-reported proofs, finite checks, extracted figure measurements, selective raw-data provenance and literature boundaries were not independently reproduced; no supplied research script was executed. External correctness, formal certification, historical priority, physical acquisition and claimed scientific interpretation remain UNKNOWN. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Let A be a complete synchronizing deterministic finite automaton on m>=2 states with at least two letters a,b. The source constructs B by adjoining m-1 proxy states p_i and retaining every original transition, with p_i a=q_i a and p_i b=q_{i+1}b; every further letter maps p_i into the original image Qc. Every nonempty word has exactly the same image from B as from A, so their nonempty reset languages and reset thresholds agree. The pair-specific unit merges form a spanning path, forcing the pair-distance MST weight K(B)=|Q_B|-1=2m-2. Applied to the classical m-state Cerny family, |Q_B|=2m-1 and rt(B)=(m-1)^2=(|Q_B|-1)^2/4, so rt(B)/K(B)=(|Q_B|-1)/4 and no universal constant C gives rt<=C K (even with a fixed additive constant).
Interface: Complete deterministic automata; at least two alphabet letters; the core automaton is synchronizing. Pair distance is the shortest word merging a specified pair; K is the minimum spanning-tree weight using these distances. The construction is not strongly connected: the original states form a closed subautomaton.
Proof spine: For every letter c, the new states map into Qc while original states still have image Qc; induction on a nonempty word gives Q_B w=Q_A w. The pairs {q_i,p_i} merge under a and {p_i,q_{i+1}} under b, giving a unit-weight spanning path. Since every edge weight is at least one, this attains the |Q_B|-1 MST lower bound. The classical Cerny threshold then yields the unbounded ratio.
Costs: The extension is written with O(m times alphabet-size) transition assignments. Pair distances are polynomial-time computable by reverse search on unordered pairs. This does not provide a short-reset algorithm or improve general reset-word upper bounds; exact subset BFS appears only as a finite check in the source.
Failure: This refutes the specific proposal that a fixed multiplicative rescaling of pair-distance MST universally pays for a single common reset word. It does not refute the Cerny conjecture, all polynomial-size potentials, or the same claim restricted to strongly connected automata. Historical priority is UNKNOWN.
Closest comparator: The construction uses the classical Cerny family and the source cites established reset-threshold literature. The exact extension formulation was not independently checked against prior art during intake; no novelty or priority claim is made.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the reset-language equality and MST calculation, audit the precise extension against automata literature, and separately test whether an analogous obstruction can satisfy strong connectivity without changing the claimed scope.

title: A 160-vertex triangle-free regular digraph refutes a stationary joint neighborhood repair
text:
N618-stationary-joint-neighborhood-repair-counterexample | A 160-vertex triangle-free regular digraph refutes a stationary joint neighborhood repair
status=source_derived_unreviewed; CQ preserves the exact independent-investigations directory and indexes only scoped claims and failures. Source-reported proofs, finite checks, extracted figure measurements, selective raw-data provenance and literature boundaries were not independently reproduced; no supplied research script was executed. External correctness, formal certification, historical priority, physical acquisition and claimed scientific interpretation remain UNKNOWN. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: The source gives an explicit strongly connected, oriented, triangle-free 52-outregular 0/1 digraph on n=160 vertices. For the stationary distribution pi of its uniform-outneighbor walk, with s(v) the number of exact two-step outneighbors excluding v and its first outneighbors, it reports E_pi[d^-(v)+s(v)] = 104 - 2493/485524 < 2r=104. Thus the proposed universal stationary joint inequality is false even under equal row degree, strong connectivity and directed-triangle exclusion. The same construction family at n=64,r=20 separately gives E_pi s=20-29/1186<r. Since 160>3*52, these examples do not contradict the directed triangle case of Caccetta–Häggkvist.
Interface: Finite oriented directed graphs with adjacency entries in {0,1}, equal outdegree r, strong connectivity, and no directed 3-cycles. pi is the unique stationary distribution of the uniform-outneighbor Markov chain. s(v) counts vertices reachable in exactly two steps but not at distance zero or one.
Proof spine: The source builds a 16-vertex row-4 block H and substitutes it into a triangle-free regular outer digraph F_q, adding complete inter-block arcs. It derives the stationary law from R sigma=q*1+H^T sigma and gives exact rational group masses. At q=3, n=160,r=52; direct rational evaluation yields the displayed deficit. The source reports a second exact implementation and full adjacency/stationary certificates.
Costs: The witness is finite and explicit; the report states that two exact-rational implementations verify adjacency, stationary coordinates, connectivity, triangle exclusion and neighborhood counts. This intake checked file hashes and routes only and did not run either implementation.
Failure: The counterexample falsifies only the proposed stationary second-neighborhood inequality and the specific indegree-paid joint repair. It is not a counterexample to Caccetta–Häggkvist, does not establish an impossibility theorem for stationary methods, and does not create a new CH barrier. The valid reverse-step entropy lemma is separate from the failed charging step.
Closest comparator: The report cites established Caccetta–Häggkvist background and related average second-neighborhood conjectures. The exact witness priority was not established; the cited literature was not independently audited during intake.
Open verification: Reconstruct the block substitution and stationary equations independently from the full adjacency certificate, verify the rational expectations, and preserve the strict distinction between this false intermediate inequality and the still-open Caccetta–Häggkvist question.

Claim: The broad claim E_pi |N_2(v)| >= E_pi d^+(v), for the stationary law of the uniform-outneighbor walk on every strongly connected oriented graph, is false. One four-vertex witness has arcs 0->1,0->3,1->2,2->0,3->1,3->2, stationary law (4,3,4,2)/13, outdegrees (2,1,1,2), and exact second-neighborhood sizes (1,1,2,1), giving expectations 19/13 and 17/13. A separate strongly connected triangle-free eight-vertex cyclic-block graph with variable outdegree has E_pi d^+=17/7 but E_pi |N_2|=2. These examples obstruct broad stationary-weighted extensions; neither refutes the existential Seymour conjecture, the minimum-outdegree formulation, or a row-regular triangle-free statement.
Interface: Finite strongly connected oriented digraphs; pi is stationary for the uniform-outneighbor transition. In the first witness outdegree is variable and directed triangles exist. The second witness is triangle-free but variable-degree, with exact second neighborhoods defined to exclude the start and first outneighbors.
Proof spine: For the four-vertex graph, multiply the stated rational row vector by the transition matrix and enumerate exact two-step neighborhoods. For the triangle-free example, arrange four two-vertex blocks cyclically, put one internal arc in each block and all arcs to the next block; the exact stationary weights are 3/28 on each u_i and 4/28 on each v_i, while each exact second neighborhood has size two.
Costs: The examples have explicit adjacency lists and exact rational stationary laws. The package retains finite-discovery and exact-check scripts; they were not executed during intake.
Failure: These witnesses do not test or falsify the regular triangle-free averaging route covered separately by N618, do not refute Seymour’s existential conjecture, and do not imply a general obstruction to stationary methods. They are scoped counterexamples to the stated weighted inequalities only.
Closest comparator: The report makes no novelty claim. Its purpose is to prevent importing a broad stationary-weighted theorem without proof.
Open verification: Recompute both stationary distributions and exact second neighborhoods from the adjacency lists, then retain each failure only at its stated variable-degree scope.

title: Coded population marginals give exact sparse generator identities under a supplied tag model
text:
N620-coded-population-generator-tomography-contract | Coded population marginals give exact sparse generator identities under a supplied tag model
status=source_derived_unreviewed; CQ preserves the exact independent-investigations directory and indexes only scoped claims and failures. Source-reported proofs, finite checks, extracted figure measurements, selective raw-data provenance and literature boundaries were not independently reproduced; no supplied research script was executed. External correctness, formal certification, historical priority, physical acquisition and claimed scientific interpretation remain UNKNOWN. No historic-scale breakthrough is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: Under x'(t)=A x(t) with Metzler A, known positive initial population p, neutral inherited binary tags whose initial fractions W_ji are known, a sufficient declared-state model, and at most s off-diagonal incoming rates per state, the source derives f'_ji(0)=sum_{k!=i} lambda_ik(W_jk-W_ji), where f_ji=x_ji/x_0i and lambda_ik=A_ik p_k/p_i. With an (s+1)-disjunct code, lambda_ik is the minimum eligible derivative over rows W_ji=0,W_jk=1. Separately, for a time-homogeneous A and occupation-integrated tagged counts U_j=integral_0^T exp(-lambda t)x_j(t)dt, endpoint quantity H_j=exp(-lambda T)x_j(T)-x_j(0) satisfies (A-lambda I)U_j=H_j; the source derives a row equation Z_i a_i=D_i for the off-diagonal rates. If every at-most-2s-column submatrix of Z_i has full column rank, the s-sparse row is unique. The source reports exact rational finite examples, including recovery of 16,256 rates.
Interface: Requires known/observed initial abundances and tag fractions, tag neutrality and inheritance, all declared-state classification, calibrated measurements, and no tag-dependent dynamics. The finite-interval identity additionally requires one common time-independent A and occupation-integrated measurements, not just endpoints. Hidden heterogeneous subtypes can invalidate the mean model.
Proof spine: Apply the quotient rule to tagged and total population equations; the diagonal A_ii terms cancel. Nonnegative incoming rates plus disjunctness make the min decoder exact. For finite intervals, integrate the linear dynamics with exponential weight, integrate by parts, then subtract F_ji times the untagged coordinate equation so diagonal and lambda terms cancel. Uniqueness follows because the difference of two s-sparse solutions is a null vector on at most 2s columns.
Costs: The reported 128-state derivative example uses 49 tags and O(n^2 q^2) comparisons for the stated polynomial code. Finite-interval support enumeration is combinatorial in s; conditioning, population balance, discretization/assay error and independent replicate-population variation require separate accounting. Exact rational code tests are source-reported and were not rerun.
Failure: The derivation does not construct a physical state-dependent tag writer or establish neutral tags, lumpability, feasible destructive-cohort sampling, or acquisition advantage over ordinary barcoding/tracer tomography. Exact-real identifiability is not a finite-precision stability guarantee. No new coding theorem or transformative capability is claimed.
Closest comparator: The source explicitly places the construction alongside known prospective lineage barcoding, group testing, compressed sensing and tracer tomography and credits the polynomial disjunct-code construction to Kautz–Singleton. Those prior-art claims were not independently audited during intake.
Open verification: Independently derive both identities and verify the exact-rank assumptions; assess whether the required tag/occupation interface is physically available and compare charged resources with ordinary prospective barcoding and tracer methods.

Claim: For the source's ideal model of a random bounded measurable classical signal with a constant clock channel, fixed reciprocal real couplings, coherent ladder evolution and endpoint preparations/readouts, define for each finite channel word w of length r the signed endpoint contrast D_w(lambda)=i^r E[U_w[a;lambda]_{r0}-U_w[a;lambda]_{0r}]. The source reports an exact reciprocity identity and a completeness theorem: the signal law equals its time-reversed law if and only if D_w(lambda)=0 for every finite word w and every positive coupling lambda. The proof route extracts all antisymmetric expected ordered integrals from analytic leading coefficients and uses the clock-augmented integrated path and Stone–Weierstrass to separate bounded signal laws. This is an unbounded hierarchy, not a finite-resource decision procedure.
Interface: The signal is not altered or replayed; the ideal theorem assumes reproducible windows, a noninvasive signal, known bounded channels including a clock, real calibrated reciprocal coherent couplings, phase reference and endpoint readout. A time reversal of increments is defined in the source using the clock-augmented path; it is not ordinary signed path inversion.
Proof spine: Real symmetric instantaneous Hamiltonians imply the propagator under reversed input is the transpose of the forward propagator. Endpoint swapping makes the contrast exactly odd under reversal. Its first nonzero Dyson coefficient is the difference between expected ordered integrals for w and reverse(w). If all contrasts vanish for every positive lambda, analyticity gives equality of all expected iterated integrals; the clock coordinate removes reparameterization ambiguity, and the shuffle algebra plus Stone–Weierstrass yields equality of the bounded path laws.
Costs: For any fixed word, the report gives a bounded-outcome finite-shot concentration bound and a finite-coupling remainder. The complete theorem quantifies over all finite words and positive couplings; it supplies no uniform first distinguishing word length, polynomial-time search, uniform sample complexity, or practical signal-to-noise guarantee.
Failure: The only demonstrated finite-strength separation is from constant commuting integrators. Existing time-resolved and nonlinear correlation sensors can distinguish suitable signals. No physical platform, native signal-to-coupling transduction, calibrated advantage, or new sensor capability was demonstrated. The rotating example is identified as a spin-1 Rabi-class calculation.
Closest comparator: The source cites Chen iterated integrals, sparse path-signature results, Rabi dynamics, SENSIT time-reversal sensing and quantum computational sensing as close prior work; it explicitly withholds novelty. Intake did not independently verify that literature boundary.
Open verification: Reconstruct the completeness proof with the exact path-law topology and reversal convention; check the relation to sparse path characteristic functions and prior time-reversal sensing; require a physical target and matched native-sensor baseline before any capability claim.
