title: Tetragonal-domain averaging gives conditional Hall tensor invariants and a population-independent [111] slope
text:
N622-conditional-tetragonal-domain-hall-tensor-invariants | Tetragonal-domain averaging gives conditional Hall tensor invariants and a population-independent [111] slope
status=source_derived_unreviewed; CQ preserves the exact independent-investigations directory and indexes only scoped claims and failures. Claim: Under the source's weak-Hall, local-diffusive model with the same scalar zero-field longitudinal conductivity in every domain and fixed single-domain coefficients a,c, tetragonal symmetry gives K0=diag(a,a,c) and K(n)=aI+(c-a)nn^T. First-order arithmetic averaging is exact under those assumptions: for Q=E[nn^T], tr Q=1, K_eff=aI+(c-a)Q and b_hat·K_eff b_hat=a+(c-a)E[(n·b_hat)^2]. For the three ideal SrTiO3 tetragonal variants and B along [111], every squared projection is 1/3, so the model predicts S_[111]=(2a+c)/3 independent of domain populations. Orthogonal full-tensor slopes sum to tr K_eff=2a+c, invariant under pure orientation redistribution in this model. These are conditional deductions, not measured values of a,c or evidence for a microscopic mechanism.
Interface: Assumes weak Hall response, local diffusion, a common scalar zero-field longitudinal conductivity, fixed a,c across intervention, and arithmetic averaging at first order. Arbitrary inhomogeneous anisotropic composites are outside scope. B projection and contact-normal geometry must not be conflated.
Proof spine: The axial-vector transformation laws make K transform as an ordinary rank-two tensor. Tetragonal D4h symmetry fixes diag(a,a,c); the domain director gives the rank-one form. The uniform zero-field corrector under common scalar longitudinal conductivity makes the first-order effective Hall tensor the arithmetic mean, from which the [111] and trace identities follow.
Costs: The source digitizes plotted vector markers from a published figure and reports descriptive finite-field statistics. Its +/- perturbation range for extraction is a sensitivity interval, not a confidence interval or experimental error model. No suitable matched before/after [111] or full three-axis raw dataset was located in the bounded search.
Failure: The analysis neither statistically rejects the microscopic scattering explanation nor establishes a new natural mechanism. Contact gains, temperature mismatch, heat-flow changes, spatially varying longitudinal anisotropy, domain walls and other scattering changes remain possible. A raw Hall angle is not automatically the zero-field slope.
Closest comparator: The source identifies prior SrTiO3 domain-orientation work and known Hall-sign-inversion examples in inhomogeneous media. It makes no novelty claim; citations and figures were not independently reanalysed during intake.
Open verification: Acquire matched-temperature full-tensor Hall measurements in [111] and three orthogonal geometries with calibrated contact/longitudinal response; then test the invariants against spatially inhomogeneous transport and the source-reported uncertainty.

Claim: In the source's selected-trace analysis of 44 traces from 43 cells with a cell-identity-based discovery/validation split, the frozen primary OFF-window classifier labeled one resolved post-pulse onset among 16 validation pulse traces from 15 cells, alongside 15 immediate/unresolved traces. The identity of late events changed under the fixed 200-ms guard and threshold sensitivities; counts across the six fixed settings ranged from zero to two of 16. The report therefore does not identify a robust excess of delayed post-pulse activation over ordinary recovery. This is a source-reported negative analysis, not evidence that mechanical priming is absent.
Interface: The observable is first sustained autonomous rotation during the OFF interval, not stator attachment or occupancy. The report uses selected 4-kHz long-axis/PCA angles, cell-level discovery/validation separation, a fixed Savitzky–Golay derivative, thresholds, persistence rule and edge guards. The 44 traces cover 43 unique cells; one cell appears under both forcing directions within the validation grouping, but no cell crosses the discovery/validation split.
Proof spine: The candidate distinguishes instantaneous activation from a latent mechanically prepared state by comparing first sustained autonomous-motion onset during OFF intervals. Extraction rules were frozen before validation outcomes were parsed, with a documented pre-validation correction. The reported late-event identities are guard/threshold sensitive and ordinary unforced recovery is sparse, so the source closes the candidate as unidentified rather than claiming a mechanism.
Costs: The original multi-gigabyte source ZIP was not fully downloaded; selected entries were fetched by byte ranges and individually CRC/SHA checked in the source record. This intake did not reacquire data, rerun extraction, or fit a calibrated clustered-event model. Reported Poisson tails are explicitly descriptive, not calibrated tests.
Failure: The analysis does not rule out sub-100-ms priming, priming hidden inside the edge guard, mechanical pinning, or attachment masked by bearing/glass effects. It cannot observe molecular attachment. The selected records are too sparse and sensitivity-unstable to establish delayed priming; no causal or molecular claim follows.
Closest comparator: The source identifies Ito, Nakamura and Toyabe (2021) as the experimental source and notes prior hypotheses of rotation-enhanced assembly, gear activation and MotB stretching. The report also records bearing barriers as a rival. Literature and raw source archive were not independently reaudited by intake.

Costs: The reduction uses O(n) qubits, terms and coefficient bits, beta O(n), and log Z O(n^2). It is a conditional hardness statement, not a sampler or capability gain.
Failure: This rules out only the stated whole family unless a complexity collapse occurs. It is not an intrinsic sign-problem theorem or an unconditional impossibility for more restricted classes. Source code and rounding margins were not independently checked.
Closest comparator: The source invokes Alimonti–Kann cubic-MaxCut hardness and cites prior thermal/tensor-network methods; this intake did not recheck those applications.

Claim: Let n>=1 qubits start in |0^n> and a reference with H_R=sum_{r>=0} r|r><r| start in any finite-mean state rho of mean mu. Under an arbitrary joint unitary commuting with H_S+H_R, retain all outputs and compare the final joint state with |+^n><+^n| tensor the same original rho, uncorrelated. If D is their trace distance, then for every s>0, D >= exp(-s mu)[1-((1+exp(-s))/2)^n], and D >= n/[8e(mu+n)]. Thus for 0<epsilon<=1/(16e), D<=epsilon requires mu>=n/(16e epsilon). A supplied sine-profile reference and explicit conserving interactions attain D<=min(1, pi sqrt(n(n+1))/(2(L+1))) with mean energy n+(L-1)/2, giving optimal Theta(n/epsilon) scaling for this exact joint-return task.
Interface: All system outputs and the reference are retained; the target contains the same uncorrelated reference. U may be arbitrary subject to exact total-energy conservation. Trace distance is 1/2 trace norm. The upper construction assumes the coherent sine reference is supplied; it is not constructed from free inputs.
Proof spine: The invariant bounded effect exp[-s(H_S+H_R)] has expectations L_rho(s) and L_rho(s)((1+exp(-s))/2)^n on actual and target states. Jensen gives L_rho(s)>=exp(-s mu), yielding the all-protocol lower bound. For the upper bound, sector Hadamards yield 2^(-n/2) sum_x |x> T^|x| eta; telescoping shift error and W~Bin(n,1/2) give the uniform overlap bound.
Costs: Mean resource scaling is Theta(n/epsilon) in the stated small-error regime, with a supplied sine reference of mean n+(L-1)/2; no gate-synthesis or reference-preparation complexity is bounded.
Failure: The lower bound is for the entire joint output/reference comparison, not the reduced system channel or a channel diamond norm. The construction prepares no reference and charges no arbitrary-unitary synthesis; initial-reference precision contributes additional error. A fixed-pure-reference overlap optimum is also source-derived but does not imply efficient synthesis.
Closest comparator: The source cites Chiribella, Yang and Renner (2021), “Fundamental Energy Requirement of Reversible Quantum Operations,” https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevX.11.021014, plus finite sine-reference and catalytic-coherence antecedents. Citation and exact priority comparison were not rechecked in intake; no novelty is claimed.

Claim: Given T explicit trace-preserving instruments on C^d with Gaussian-rational Kraus matrices of at most B-bit numerators/denominators, a polynomial-bit algorithm decides whether every length-T history product has rank at most one without listing histories. For a repeated fixed instrument, eventual all-history collapse occurs iff it has occurred by D=binom(d,2) steps. Separately, the exact terminal channel after forgetting outcomes has a representation sum_{j<=d^4} c_j B_j X B_j*, where c_j are positive rationals and every B_j is an actual length-T branch product. If all products have rank at most one, this yields an exact measure-prepare form.
Interface: The instrument and Kraus matrices are supplied. Complexity is polynomial in dense Hilbert dimension d and input bit length, not in qubit count log2(d). Compression preserves only the terminal forgotten-outcome channel; it need not preserve histories, their probabilities, or intermediate intervention responses.
Proof spine: Lift each Kraus operator to the exterior square; the span of all branch images is propagated by V_t=sum_i (Lambda^2 K_i^(t))V_(t-1), and is zero iff every branch product has rank<=1. For a fixed instrument the descending subspace chain stabilizes within D steps. For compression, vectorize branch products into Hermitian Choi rank-one matrices in a d^4-dimensional real space and use exact rational conic elimination with positive weights.
Costs: The source gives polynomial bit complexity in dense dimension d, instrument length and input bit size, with O(sum_t r_t D^3) field operations for the span test and at most d^4 retained products.
Failure: This is not representation-independent entanglement-breaking recognition: the source gives an invertible-Pauli Kraus representation of a depolarizing entanglement-breaking channel that fails the test. d^4 is polynomial in d but exponential in qubits. No generic simulation improvement follows. Its exact combined novelty is unestablished.
Closest comparator: The source identifies exterior algebra, conic Caratheodory elimination and rank-one Kraus/measure-prepare equivalence as standard. It cites Horodecki, Shor and Ruskai (2003), https://arxiv.org/abs/quant-ph/0302031. No broad entanglement-breaking theorem is claimed.

Claim: For each k>=1, an explicit connected path instance on 2k qubits with 2k-1 gates and positive rational weights has exact partition function Z=26^k(1+epsilon)^(k-1), epsilon=1/(100k), computable in O(k) rational arithmetic, while the specified iid I/C/D loop-selector estimator satisfies E[Y^2]/Z^2 >= exp(-0.02)(189/169)^k.
Interface: The pair gates are F(4,4,1) and bridges F(1,epsilon,epsilon); one selector is drawn independently per gate with probabilities proportional to a,c,d and Y is the product normalizer times the exact selected-word trace. The claim is estimator- and family-specific.
Proof spine: Leaf partial traces give Z=2 product_e(2a_e+c_e+d_e). Condition on all bridges selecting I; pair-gate relative second moments multiply to (189/169)^k, while the bridge probability/normalization factor is bounded below by exp(-0.02). A parity check is required when evaluating selector loops.
Costs: The exact partition function takes O(k) rational arithmetic with polynomial bit lengths; one selector draw and exact path trace are polynomial in k. The second moment grows exponentially in k.
Failure: This refutes the usual variance-based FPRAS argument for this iid estimator on this connected family only. The family itself has an elementary exact algorithm. It proves no counting hardness, no lower bound for all estimators, and no general tensor-network variance barrier. Finite selector checks are source-reported and not rerun here.
Closest comparator: Related to N115 and the existing N190/N191/N193 EPR results, but it is an estimator-specific extension/obstruction and does not settle global EPR sampling.
Open verification: Independently check the leaf-trace identity, estimator normalization, bridge conditioning, and parity treatment; seek a conditional or global acquired estimator without overstating this negative witness.

title: Complex Lee–Yang operators have sharp spectral separation and varying products approach rank one
text:
N638-complex-lee-yang-spectral-finite-product-bounds | Complex Lee–Yang operators have sharp spectral separation and varying products approach rank one
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The 10 October source packet reports internally derived/reconstructed arguments and coordinator or adversarial checks for the stated scopes. Claim: Define LY(r), r>1, by zero-freeness of the flattened polynomial f_K(z,w)=sum_xy K_xy z^x w^y when all variables lie in the open polydisk of radius r. For every complex 2^n-by-2^n K in LY(r), the maximum-modulus eigenvalue is unique, nonzero and algebraically simple, and every other eigenvalue obeys |lambda/lambda_*|<=r^-2; its rank-one spectral projector factors into LY(r) vectors. Also, if K_1,...,K_T each lie in LY(r), M=K_T...K_1, e=|0^n>, and a=e^T M e !=0, then B=(Me)(e^T M)/a has rank one and ||M-B||_F <= 2(1+r^2)^(n/2)r^(-2T)||Me||_2 <= 2(1+r^2)^(n/2)r^(-2T)||M||_2.
Interface: All matrices may be complex, nonnormal, non-PSD and varying; they share the same supplied whole-layer LY(r) promise. Products and contractions use bilinear transposes without conjugation. The estimate is conditional on the global zero-free promise for every factor.
Proof spine: Import two zero-free contraction/limit facts; establish eigenvector comparison via holomorphic diameter contraction, then use generic perturbation or the product theorem to obtain spectral separation. For varying products, propagate polynomial ratios and apply Parseval to bound the Frobenius residual from the explicit rank-one B.
Costs: The explicit sufficient product length for relative operator-norm error epsilon is T >= [log(2/epsilon)+(n/2)log(1+r^2)]/[2log r], conditional on the shared whole-layer LY(r) promise; this is a theorem bound, not an implementation-cost guarantee.
Failure: A zero-free promise does not recognize itself from local input, compute M e or e^T M, normalize thermal quantities, or provide physical acquisition/nonunitary implementation. No polynomial-cost state-preparation, thermal-normalization or finite-temperature capability follows; exponential postselection examples are explicit. The theorem extends a source-cited PSD mechanism but originality is not claimed.
Closest comparator: Bravyi, Gosset, Liu and Wong, arXiv:2607.14401v1, is source-cited as prior PSD spectral separation/quantum ground-energy work; Rugh (2010), https://doi.org/10.4007/annals.2010.171.1707, is cited for projective contraction antecedents. Source-reported citations were not rechecked at intake.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the complex contraction facts, spectral perturbation, nonnormal case, bilinear projector, and varying-product estimate. Separate the theorem from the absent polynomial-cost recognition, preparation, and normalization algorithms.

title: The all-copy rank-two functional is locally nonnegative near a specified zero family for each fixed copy number
text:
N639-fixed-copy-ghz-rank-two-local-minimum | The all-copy rank-two functional is locally nonnegative near a specified zero family for each fixed copy number
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The 10 October source packet reports internally derived/reconstructed arguments and coordinator or adversarial checks for the stated scopes. This intake preserves and routes those records only; it did not independently reconstruct the proofs, run research scripts, or validate external correctness or historical priority. No historic-scale/foundational breakthrough, physical acquisition, or practical transformative capability is established.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For q_n(C)=sum_{S subseteq[n]}(-1/2)^|S| ||Tr_S C||_F^2 on complex matrices in M_(3^n), the universal target q_n(C)>=0 for all n and rank(C)<=2 remains unresolved. The source reports that for every fixed n>=1 there is a neighborhood within the rank-at-most-two variety of C0=|0^n><0^n|+(-1)^(n+1)|1^n><1^n| where q_n is nonnegative, with a smooth local zero manifold of real dimension 4*2^n-6+4n; all its points are critical and the Hessian is positive in normal directions. The radius is not uniform in n. An exact block lift shows that uniform local stability at all diag(R,R,0) rank-two zeros would encode the lower-copy global target; a separate high-rank witness defeats one proposed swap-sector concentration route but is not a rank-two counterexample.
Interface: The local theorem is fixed-n, complex rank exactly two near the specified C0 family (the local neighborhood is separated from rank<=1). The global question quantifies over every n and every complex rank<=2 C. The local radius has no uniform lower bound. q_n uses partial trace over the indexed qutrit sites and Frobenius norm.
Proof spine: Construct the explicit smooth zero manifold, prove stationarity, compute the full rank-two chart Hessian including its kernel and positive normal spectrum, then use a positive normal Hessian in adapted coordinates for higher-order local control. Separately derive q_(m+1)(C(t))=t^2 q_m(X) for the exact rank-two block lift and compute the high-rank swap-sector counterexample.
Costs: The argument is a fixed-n local analysis on a rank-two matrix variety of ambient dimension 3^n; its neighborhood radius and quantitative conditioning are not uniform or supplied as usable bounds.
Failure: This proves neither the global q_n inequality nor an NPT bound-entangled state. The exact lift is a barrier to an overbroad local-to-global argument; the swap-sector witness has high rank and is not a negative rank-two C. Two-copy positivity is cited prior art, not a result of this intake.
Closest comparator: The packet cites Song and Chen, https://arxiv.org/html/2607.23416v1 and https://arxiv.org/html/2607.24479v1 for two-copy work, plus Tran et al. 2017 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1704.03385), a 2024 paper (https://arxiv.org/html/2402.18037v1) and earlier local-minimum work (https://arxiv.org/abs/0711.2613). Citations and originality are not rechecked; no novelty claim is made.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the full fixed-n Hessian/normal-coordinate proof and exact lift. Keep G-ALL-COPY-NPT-UNDISTILLABILITY open until a proof or valid complex rank-two counterexample covers the universal target.

title: A fixed path-reweighting roulette fails on an explicit finite-state response system
text:
N641-stationary-path-roulette-response-obstruction | A fixed path-reweighting roulette fails on an explicit finite-state response system
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The source records report internal derivations, audits, and finite diagnostics at the stated scope. This intake preserved files and checked hashes/routes only; it did not execute research code, rerun analyses, or independently reconstruct proofs. External correctness and historical priority remain unresolved. No historic-scale foundational breakthrough is established. The negative result concerns one fixed stationary proposal and a specified common-prefix roulette construction, not chaotic response in general.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For a strictly positive column-stochastic finite-state transition matrix P with positive stationary vector h and a fixed strictly positive row-stochastic backward proposal Q, define K[j,i]=P[j,i]^2/Q[j,i]. The source proves ρ(K)≥1, with equality exactly at the Perron twist Q[j,i]=P[j,i]h_i/h_j. In a supplied two-state deterministic piecewise-affine response example, the proposed common-prefix single-term roulette has infinite absolute expectation (and second moment) for every independent full-support level law, while an exact transfer-operator solve gives the response directly. The source also reports four-state slow-mixing stress cases: for δ=10^-3 and absolute-bias target 10^-3, the exact finite-horizon bias requires n≥6212, while its fixed-proposal response-variance lower bound has log10 at least 486.666 and the stated independent-path count for standard deviation 10^-3 has log10 at least 492.666.
Interface: The proposal is fixed at the differentiation point; finite-horizon score estimators are distinguished from roulette estimators. The deterministic realization has a finite Markov partition and is not a claim about globally smooth expanding maps. The four-state family separates uniform inverse-branch contraction from mixing constants that degenerate as δ→0.
Proof spine: A Perron-vector/Cauchy–Schwarz argument gives the spectral radius and equality condition. The explicit map realizes the finite transition matrix exactly. Conditional increment bounds show divergence of the absolute roulette expectation; direct transfer equations provide the exact small-instance comparator.
Costs: The direct finite-state transfer calculation uses standard finite-dimensional linear algebra; the proposed path method samples O(n) transitions per path and has the reported unbounded/infinite roulette cost in this example. No scaling advantage is established. In the reported δ=10^-3 stress case, the variance/path-count lower bounds make this specific estimator impractical; the exact transfer solve remains available for the finite state model.
Failure: The generic eigenfunction-twist principle is prior work, as the source itself notes. The counterexample only defeats the stated fixed stationary proposal and common-prefix single-term roulette. It is not a lower bound for horizon-dependent/adaptive proposals, resampling, control variates, other couplings, all chaotic-response methods, or smooth systems.
Closest comparator: The source compares the Perron twist to Whiteley–Lee, “Twisted particle filters” (arXiv:1210.0220v4), and the single-term estimator identity to Rhee–Glynn/Vihola (arXiv:1512.01022). Generic twist and exact transfer methods are established; priority of this explicit example is unknown.
Open verification: Independently reconstruct the finite-state response and non-integrability calculation, and require any replacement estimator to be compared against an acquired transfer-operator baseline with all proposal, bias, variance, and acquisition costs charged.

title: Boolean coordinate restriction has a sharp entropy modulus, but a prescribed-coordinate ratio diverges
text:
N642-bool-fourier-local-entropy-modulus | Boolean coordinate restriction has a sharp entropy modulus, but a prescribed-coordinate ratio diverges
status=source_derived_unreviewed; The source records report internal derivations, audits, and finite diagnostics at the stated scope. This intake preserved files and checked hashes/routes only; it did not execute research code, rerun analyses, or independently reconstruct proofs. External correctness and historical priority remain unresolved. No historic-scale foundational breakthrough is established. The result does not refute FEI or the existential good-coordinate route.
Symbols and resource contracts LOCAL to this card.

Claim: For a Boolean f:{−1,1}^n→{−1,1}, let Δ_i(f)=H(f)−(H(f_i^+)+H(f_i^-))/2 and let I_i(f) be coordinate influence under the stated Fourier normalization. With h(t)=−t log_2 t−(1−t)log_2(1−t) and D(t)=h(t)+1−h(1/2+√(t(1−t))), the source proves 0≤Δ_i(f)≤D(I_i(f)) for every coordinate. For every even m≥2 it gives F_m and a distinguished z with p=2^-m, I_z(F_m)=p, Δ_z(F_m)=p log_2(1/p)+(3/ln 2)p−(19/(6 ln 2))p^2+O(p^3), and D(p)−Δ_z(F_m)=2p^2/ln 2+O(p^3), so Δ_z/I_z=m+3/ln 2+O(2^-m), while H(F_m)≤2I(F_m). Thus no universal bound Δ_i(f)≤C I_i(f) can hold for all Boolean functions and all prescribed coordinates.
Interface: All quantities use the source’s Boolean Fourier normalization. The theorem concerns a specified coordinate; the family need not have every coordinate bad.
Proof spine: Pair Fourier coefficients across coordinate i, express the restriction entropy loss as a weighted binary-entropy comparison, derive the modulus, and evaluate the explicit even-m family to second order. The report states the family remains globally FEI-bounded.
Costs: Finite-dimensional exact mathematical construction; no algorithmic or physical cost claim.
Failure: It does not refute the Fourier Entropy–Influence conjecture, does not show that every coordinate in F_m is bad, and does not disprove existence of some coordinate with Δ_i≤C I_i. It only rules out an all-coordinate linear decrement inequality. The equality statement is one-way: upper-bound equality is possible only at influences 0, 1/2, or 1; influence 1/2 alone is not sufficient.
Closest comparator: The source treats coordinate restriction as an existing FEI proof strategy. N601 is a complex-valued relaxation obstruction; N529 concerns a different absolute-product coordinate criterion. Neither is invalidated, and the existential Boolean selection problem remains open.
Open verification: Reconstruct the sharp modulus and equality cases, then independently resolve the existential coordinate-selection question or pursue another FEI route. Do not infer a Boolean FEI counterexample from the prescribed-coordinate family.

Claim: Let W=(W_ij) have the real Wishart law W_p(ν,Σ), with ν>p−1, Σ positive definite, and a block partition p=p_1+⋯+p_r. Under the source convention E exp(−tr(TW))=det(I+2ΣT)^(-ν/2) for T⪰0, the source reports that for all s_i≥0, E∏_{i=1}^r det(W_ii)^{s_i} ≥ ∏_{i=1}^r E det(W_ii)^{s_i}. It also proves the stronger one-block-versus-rest comparison. The statement covers arbitrary real ν in the stated range and arbitrary block count.

Proof spine: Condition on one principal block and represent the complement by an explicitly constructed noncentral Wishart law. Prove determinant-product expectation monotonicity in its mean through a rank-one differential identity and a rank-saving decomposition; use determinant-weighted association of ordered Wishart eigenvalues and Wishart regression to finish. The FKG/MTP2 association and boundary steps require independent reconstruction.
Costs: A finite-dimensional analytic inequality; no runtime or sampling improvement is asserted.
Failure: The source’s proof is not independently checked here. This theorem does not supply a sampling algorithm or a new primitive. Historical novelty is unresolved; the two-block case was already known.
Closest comparator: The statement is Conjecture 1.1 in Genest, Ouimet, and Richards, “On the Gaussian product inequality conjecture for disjoint principal minors of Wishart random matrices,” arXiv:2311.00202v3. The authors state that d=2 was proved earlier; see also their two-minor result arXiv:2409.14512. The source reports the all-partition proof; correctness and priority remain UNKNOWN.

Claim: In a homogeneous spatially flat GR model with separately conserved barotropic components p_i=p_i(ρ_i), ρ_i+p_i≥0, and 0≤c_{s,i}^2=dp_i/dρ_i≤1, allowing a separate constant vacuum term, set x=a^-3 and Y(x)=H^2(x). A source-reported BAO-only check found a sequence satisfying these radial shape restrictions within 0.781 marginal standard deviations of each of six radial measurements, with reported constrained-fit χ²=0.9542; it reports no compelling violation.
Interface: Assumes flat homogeneous GR, separate conservation, barotropic pressure response, the stated null-energy and causal sound-speed bounds, and the source’s DESI DR2 compressed radial-distance likelihood. Does not cover interacting fluids, all scalar-field models, modified gravity, or non-flat cosmology.
Proof spine: Use x=a^-3 and separate conservation to derive xρ′=ρ+p and xρ″=c_s^2ρ′. Sum densities in the flat Friedmann equation to get Y′≥0 and 0≤xY″≤Y′; transform to u=x² for concavity. The report evaluates the finite radial constraints in inverse-square distance coordinates without assuming Gaussian errors there.
Costs: The source reports 13 compressed DESI distances with covariance for its ΛCDM baseline and six radial distances for the shape test; the actual input files and code are absent from this intake, so those calculations are not reproducible from the preserved report alone.

text:

For a strongly connected loopless digraph G with adjacency B, N>=2 and spectral radius r>0, replace each vertex by the transitive tournament T_m and each original arc by all cross-block arcs. The source derives rho(B tensor J_m + I_N tensor T_m)=1/((1+1/r)^(1/m)-1), preservation of directed girth and delta-plus(G[T_m])=m delta-plus(G). For D_m=C4[T_m], rho(D_5)>20/3 although girth=4, and rho(D_m)/(4m)->1/(4 log 2)>1/3. These graphs have minimum outdegree density 1/4: they refute the proposed spectral implication, not Caccetta–Häggkvist. The substitution construction is acknowledged prior mathematics; originality of the calculation is unestablished.

Define beta(M)=max_{w>=0,1^T w=1} min_i (Mw)_i=min_{p in Delta} max_j (M^T p)_j. For nonempty finite blocks H_i, the source proves beta(G[H_1,...,H_n])=beta(A_G+diag(beta(A_Hi))). Acyclic blocks have beta=0, so acyclic substitution preserves beta even for unequal block sizes; beta(D_m)=1/4. This distinguishes distinct-neighbour mass from walk growth and supplies no universal one-third bound.

On Z/10, include increments +1,+3 everywhere and +2 where i mod 5 is in {0,1,3}. The source gives girth four, det A=5, w=(3,1,2,2,1,3,1,2,2,1)/18 and p=(2,2,1,3,1,2,2,1,3,1)/18, with Aw=A^T p=(5/18)1. Positivity plus invertibility gives unique optimizers p!=w. This excludes identifying the two optimal measures; it does not exclude every weighted or stationary method.

The remaining assertion is beta(A+I/3)<=1/3 for every finite triangle-free oriented adjacency A, equivalently for every w in Delta some i obeys (Aw)_i<=(1-w_i)/3. The response derives equivalence to the directed-triangle Caccetta–Häggkvist target, using lexicographic powers of C4, continuity and rational independent-clone blowups. The assertion itself is unproved. Computing or naming beta has not removed the original obstruction.

The proposed sharp criterion is gamma_H(p)>1: all counts are finite and |t(H,U)-t(H,W)|<=C ||U-W||_square^((gamma-1)/(m-1+gamma-1)) for cut-norm differences <=1. text:
N705-bounded-coupling-local-thermal-faithfulness-and-finite-band | Bath-uniform local thermal faithfulness and finite-band bounds are proposed under bounded coupling
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported mathematical arguments only. Intake checked byte preservation and repository structure; no independent proof reconstruction, scientific-code replay, citation verification, formal proof, quantum circuit execution, or experimental validation was performed. External correctness and historical priority remain UNKNOWN.

For finite H_S tensor H_B, d=dim(H_S), H=I_S tensor K+V with Hermitian K,V and ||V||op<=v, all subsystem-only terms and subsystem-bath coupling belong in V. At beta>0 let rho=exp(-beta H)/Z and X=x tensor I_B for any possibly non-Hermitian x. No bath dimension, bath energy scale, geometry, gap, commutation or mixing restriction is assumed. The claimed local KMS bound is K_rho(X)=Tr(sqrt(rho)X^dagger sqrt(rho)X)>=4 exp(-4 beta v)||x||op^2/(9d)>=4 exp(-4 beta v)Tr_S(x^dagger x)/(9d^2). This is a quadratic form, not ordinary uncentered variance or a transport coefficient. When v=0 it is exactly Tr_S(x^dagger x)/d.

More generally, lambda>sqrt(3) gives (1-3/lambda^2)^2 exp[-(lambda+1)beta v]||x||op^2/d. The singular-profile extension for lambda>0 replaces the numerator by sum_a(s_a(x)-3||x||op/lambda^2)_+^2. For Hermitian A,B with ||A-B||<=v, low/high spectral projections separated by g obey ||QP0||<=v/g, using a Sylvester integral. If X commutes with P0, compression error is <=3||QP0||^2||X||. Applied to I tensor K versus H, each low bath level supplies a copy of x; retained singular values after widening by lambda v are thermally integrated and divided by the scalar min-max bound Z<=d exp(beta v)Z_B. No false operator-order monotonicity of exp or efficient spectral-projector access is assumed.

The finite-band form K_{rho,Omega}(X)=sum_{|E_i-E_j|<=Omega}sqrt(p_i p_j)|X_ij|^2 obeys K_{rho,7v}(X)>=exp(-5 beta v)||x||op^2/(72d). Width-v bath windows enlarged by 3v on each side and a bounded overlap count supply this absolute floor. It is not a constant fraction of all KMS weight, excludes no zero-frequency contribution, and gives no nonzero-frequency absorption, conductivity, rapid mixing or finite-resolution measurement algorithm.

For Hermitian A centered at its thermal mean, BKM covariance dominates KMS. Static susceptibility is at least (4beta/(9d))exp(-4beta v) Var_tauS(A). For traceless local basis F_a with tauS(F_a F_b)=delta_ab, fixed bath K and fixed coupling V0, and ||V0+sum h_a F_a tensor I||<=v throughout a convex parameter region, Hessian(log Z)>=beta^2 kappa I, kappa=4exp(-4beta v)/(9d). Thus ||h-h'||_2<=(9d/(4beta))exp(4beta v)||m(h)-m(h')||_2. This is conditional local-field identifiability with fixed environment, not identification of an unknown bath/coupling. The explicit commuting h Z_S+b Z_B+J Z_S Z_B example gives indistinguishable local Gibbs states for different h when bath/coupling vary.

With q bounded observables ||F_a||<=L, supplied independent exact equilibrium copies, and a fit with stated residual, the note gives the sufficient count q+81q^2 L^2 d^2 exp(8beta v)log(2q/alpha)/(2beta^2 epsilon^2) for parameter error epsilon. It does not efficiently compute the expectation map, log Z or the fit. Copy preparation costs multiply this count by the actual T_eq; independence, preparation bias, measurement implementation and optimization remain charged. The theorem supplies no Gibbs sampler or equilibrium-time bound.

The low-temperature qubit H=hZ has susceptibility beta sech^2(beta h)~4beta exp(-2beta v), so universal polynomial-beta-v conditioning is impossible; exponent constants are not claimed optimal. For even d>=4, an explicit bath of dimension d-1, M=4log d, r=2/(sqrt(M^2+4)+M), local traceless Hermitian x=diag(1,-1,r^2,-r^2,...) and norm-one disjoint two-by-two perturbations gives beta=v=1, thermal mean zero, K<=3/d and tauS(x^2)>=1/[2(4log d+1)^4]. Their ratio tends to zero. This excludes a dimension-free KMS-to-tracial comparison in this general class, not a fixed-locality bounded-degree global covariance theorem or a dimension-free impossibility for BKM itself.

For k-qubit support with incident interaction norm sum <=gk, d=2^k,v<=gk yields ||X||tau <=(3/2)2^(k/2)exp(2beta gk)||X||rho,KMS. The source compares this linear-beta exponent with Chen--Anshu--Nguyen arXiv:2504.02706v1 Lemma III.6 and Bergamaschi arXiv:2610.01074v1 Lemma 3.6, which have beta log(beta) behavior in the specified inequalities. This is not exhaustive novelty clearance or a complete learning-algorithm speedup. The desired global BKM covariance bound Cov(sum u_a P_a,sum u_a P_a)>=c(beta,J,k,Delta)sum u_a^2 independent of size/term count remains open. Applying a local bound to the whole support makes d exponential and v extensive; positive termwise variances do not control off-diagonal cancellation. Learning-SYK arXiv:2610.02178v1 retains an explicit term-count denominator in the cited comparison.

status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported conditional models, circuit constructions, oracle proofs and producer diagnostics only. No transformative technological capability, physical experiment, atomistic simulation or net device advantage established. Input is a prepared donor population, weak coupling J to one resonant acceptor with exponential amplitude memory exp(-kappa s), and a differential Stark vector d=d0 u with one supplied nonzero norm d0 and arbitrary fixed u in S^2. For periodic primitive Theta'=E, f_u=exp(i d0 u.Theta), Fourier coefficients c_n(u), and Omega=2pi/T, the model gives Gamma(u)=2J^2 sum_n |c_n|^2 kappa/(kappa^2+n^2 Omega^2), Gamma0=2J^2/kappa and A=d0 E_rms. These are initial leakage rates, not demonstrated molecular lifetimes or chemical yields. For scalar finite-RMS modulation, Jensen gives Gamma>=2J^2 kappa/(kappa^2+A^2), attained by static detuning. Static orientation-averaged Gamma/Gamma0=atan(x)/x, x=A/kappa. Its frozen-ensemble mean lifetime is instead (1+x^2/3)/Gamma0, and its worst-orientation lifetime remains 1/Gamma0.

Representation change: take R=pi/d0, positive degree-2t Gauss–Legendre/azimuth cubature on S^2 with (t+1)(2t+1) nodes, a closed latitude/meridian path of length L<=2pi R(t+2), normalized traversal measure nu, and degree-t Legendre kernel K_t. Set delta=1/[2(t+1)^2], h_t(n)=integral K_t(n,x)dnu(x), and dwell weights a_k=w_k(1-delta h_t(n_k))>=w_k/2. The combined traversal/dwell occupation measure integrates spherical polynomials through degree t exactly. Travel consumes fraction delta at speed E_rms/sqrt(delta), so T=L/(E_rms sqrt(delta)); no instantaneous jumps or free traversal. Uniformly for every fixed u, |c0(u)|<=2 pi^(t+1)/(t+1)! and Gamma(u)/Gamma0<=4[pi^(t+1)/(t+1)!]^2+(kappa/Omega)^2. Peak/RMS=sqrt(2)(t+1), and Omega/A>=1/[pi sqrt(2)(t+1)(t+2)]. This is a source-reported conditional proof, unreviewed by intake.

Fejer filtering Theta to degree K keeps RMS and peak from increasing but adds carrier error: |c0,K(u)|<=2 pi^(t+1)/(t+1)!+A/[Omega(K+1)]<=2 pi^(t+1)/(t+1)!+A/B, B=K Omega. Hence Gamma_K/Gamma0<=(2 epsilon_t+A/B)^2+(kappa/Omega)^2. A bandwidth as large as A Omega/kappa may be needed for the illustrative quadratic regime. Smoothing does not preserve exact design moments for free. Existing Ehler–Grochenig t-design curves supply stronger existence length scaling; the underlying averaging principle and its existence claim are not new mathematical discoveries here.

Producer numerical benchmark: degree-2 Fejer-64 waveform at 100-fold orientation-averaged initial-rate suppression uses A_rms/kappa=91.764 and A_peak/kappa=368.127, versus static 156.440 for each, with B/kappa=445.465. Thus RMS is 1.70 times lower but peak is 2.35 times higher. It loses in RMS at 10-fold suppression. The 200-orientation, 32768-time-point computation, quadrature/aliasing bounds and peak-grid correction are preserved; it is not the orientation-uniform analytic theorem, an independent replay, interval-roundoff certification or a measured instrument advantage. The source's 3.42 s OS receipt times one NumPy diagnostic process, not the research inference budget.

Acquisition remains unclosed: same-species calibrated d0/kappa, weak transfer, one resonant Lorentzian bath, frozen orientation over cycles, common nonzero slope norm, linear Stark law over the full peak/bandwidth, preparation, competing channels, heating/ionization and damage. Source example Stark slopes and IVR rates come from different systems and cannot be combined as an achieved molecular operating point. No arbitrary multiple-channel norm coverage or bond-selective consequence is established. A separate retained finite-retention proofreading/latch model (HL6) supplies another negative boundary, not a validated manufacturing or geometric-control application. No transformative capability, originality or experimental validation was established.

Next decisive obligation: Independently review the model proof and known design-curve comparator. Acquire a same-species nonzero differential Stark-vector norm and Lorentzian decay parameter in the actual weak-transfer regime; then calibrate a three-axis finite-bandwidth field and compare initial leakage against equally prepared static and strongest admissible control under matched RMS, peak, bandwidth and delivery energy. Rotation, multiple channel norms, competing resonances, damage, preparation, lifetime and chemical yield remain separate gates.

title: Confined solid-iron export remains an admission hypothesis with explicit collection and energy costs
text:
N707-confined-solid-iron-export-and-collection-cost | Confined solid-iron export remains an admission hypothesis with explicit collection and energy costs
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported conditional models, circuit constructions, oracle proofs and producer diagnostics only. No transformative technological capability, physical experiment, atomistic simulation or net device advantage established. Candidate: reduce fine ore upstream with H2, admit Fe atoms from a continually renewed source into a confined transport path, retain gangue, and reconstruct/harvest solid Fe downstream. The preferred representation is an independently conducting CNT wall with a moving/regrowing solid Fe plug; the permanent 3 nm hot-Fe shell is an optimistic calculator model with unclosed dewetting/continuity premises. Existing prepared pure-Fe nanoscale transport and biased collection are credited antecedents, not a demonstrated raw-ore process or novelty certificate.

Stipulated molar model J=(2f/a) Ds Gamma_s/(RT) [Z*F E-partial_x mu], mu=mu0+gamma Vm curvature+Vm sigma_h+RT log activity. It assumes connected uniform mobility, an admitted Fe source and an open maintained product sink. For T=1163 K, a=L=30 nm, f=0.2, 0.3 nm mobile layer, 3 nm conducting shell, sigma=1e6 S/m and Z*=10, the imported clean-free-Fe law gives Ds=5.75274e-10 m^2/s. Target 10 kg/m^2/h gives E~1536 V/m, active v~46.09 microvolt, projected j~64.53 MA/m^2, optimistic active electricity ~0.297 MWh/t. Assumed contact RA=1e-12 ohm m^2 adds ~0.416 MWh/t. These are conditional arithmetic, not measured flux, a validated ore coefficient or atomistic simulation. A full Fe plug changes conducting area and can raise modeled electricity ~4.76-fold; CNT conductivity, shell Z* and hot-free-Fe diffusion cannot be mixed without a new contract.

Supply cannot be hidden: integral export<=integral fresh admission+initial Fe inventory. The modeled initial shell holds only 9.92 mg/m^2 and discharges in 3.57 ms without replenishment. A gangue cage admitting H2/H2O but disconnected from the metal path can fully metallize yet export no Fe; recovery<=accessible connected Fe fraction f_acc, so grade/metallization do not acquire f_acc>=0.94. EM work ~44.47 J/mol can be cancelled by ~6.27 MPa backstress; assumed curvature terms ~236–473 J/mol can exceed it. Coarsening, source-root stoppage, purity and product detachment are unclosed. Geometric exclusion of gangue fragments does not reject surface-mobile or dissolved impurities/carbon/scaffold species.

Electrical construction divides total online area A into N cells of area A/N, electrically in series but materially supplied/collected in parallel, with isolated batch cavities. I_terminal=jA/N, V_terminal=Nv and P_ideal=jAv: terminal current decreases, local current density and ideal power do not. Contact dissipation per active area obeys sum rho_c j^2/kappa_contact independent of N. A common conducting Fe product manifold shorts the circuit. For N_gap connections spanning H, conductivity<=sigma and allowed extra heat fraction eta, V_gap/A >= j H^2/(sigma eta v) (N_gap/N)^2. Product/feed storage requires H>=m tau(1/rho_Fe+1/C_Fe); the combined lower bound grows as batch time tau^2. At 10 kg/m^2/h, 100 micrometre product space fills in ~283 s. The illustrative 1 m^2, 300000-cell, 200 A/9 V layout requires ~80 L gap-spanning conductor for 10% extra heat, in addition to ports, barriers, insulation and material-access volumes. Duty D at fixed installed area increases contact/active ohmic heating by at least 1/D, or more area must be installed. These are scoped circuit/resource derivations, not a universal architecture impossibility.

On the source's illustrative 45% Fe grade and 94% export-recovery basis, one tonne exported Fe needs 2.364 t ore and leaves ~0.843 t gangue. At 97% metallization ~31.9 kg metallic and ~31.9 kg unreduced Fe remain. H2 floor ~54.15 kg/t exported Fe or ~55.87 kg at the stated metallization. Avoided 890-to-1600 C gangue heating/fusion is ~0.260 MWh/t, while whole-ore preheating is ~0.454 MWh/t before recuperation. The optimistic ~0.297 MWh/t active drive already matches/exceeds that avoided duty. Include all H2 production, heat/recovery, contacts/leads, feed renewal, scaffold/carbon, finishing, waste/lost Fe, and final product melting when matching a molten-output comparator. No net energy or economic advantage survives as an established claim.

Decisive gate: a <=1 cm^2 supported coupon with isotope-labelled oxide/quartz, all contacts metered, matched temperature/total-power bias-off/reversed/blocked/no-ore/pure-Fe controls. Require isotope-resolved feed-derived product >100 times all accessible preloaded inventory, repeated source replenishment/harvests, mass and scaffold/carbon balance, impurity assay, actual mobility/drive response, and simultaneous V/I/T/net-product measurements. Only after admission move to untreated real ore. The >=94% recovery/metallization, steel-usable chemistry, 10 kg/m^2/h and lower complete cost targets are exploratory and unmet. No device, physical experiment, durable ore transport or transformative capability was established.

Next decisive obligation: Review the stipulated transport/circuit laws and run a frozen <=1 cm^2 isotope-labelled oxide/quartz admission test with all contacts inside a measured V/I/temperature/power boundary. Require feed-derived Fe export beyond 100 times all accessible preloaded inventory, sustained replenishment and repeated harvests, full Fe/carbon/scaffold balance and impurity assay against matched bias-off, reversed, blocked, no-ore and pure-Fe controls. Only then assess untreated real ore, recovery, lifetime and full-process economics.

Finite reversible CTMC family with M=2^d and states {A,B,u_j,v_j}: q(A,u_j)=q(B,v_j)=1/M, q(u_j,A)=q(v_j,B)=1, q(u_j,v_j)=q(v_j,u_j)=theta_j>0. All topology, endpoints and pi_A=pi_B=1/4, pi_u=pi_v=1/(4M) are known. An adaptive unit-cost local query reveals theta_j (even the full unknown row); equilibrium samples and endpoint evaluation are free. Listing all M neighbors still costs M output entries. This is an unstructured local-rate oracle contract, not an atomistic force oracle.

Set f(theta)=theta/(1+2theta), S=sum_j f(theta_j). The source derives committors h_u=f, h_v=(1+theta)/(1+2theta), capacity S/(4M), reactive route weights f(theta_j)/S, mean first-passage time E_A tau_B=2M/S, and exact Laplace transform E_A exp(-s tau_B)=B(s)/[s(s+2)+B(s)] with B(s)=(1/M)sum_j theta_j/(s+1+2theta_j). These identities are source-reported proofs, not independently reconstructed by intake.

For epsilon=M^-2 compare all theta=epsilon with one unknown index J at theta_J=1. The means are T0=2(M^2+2) and TJ=6M(M^2+2)/(M^2+3M-1), a ratio asymptotic to M/3. The hidden route weight wJ=(M^2+2)/(M^2+3M-1)>=1-3/M. Coupled adaptive transcripts are identical until the hidden index is queried; TV<=q/M, also with expected distinct-query cost under model0. For M>=3, 25%-relative mean estimation with failure alpha requires q>=(1-2alpha)M. Route sampling at TV delta requires q>=M(wJ-delta)-1. Using P0(tau<=12M)<=12/M and PJ(tau<=12M)>=1/2, full first-passage-law sampling requires q/M>=1/2-12/M-2delta; M>=96 and delta=1/16 give q>=M/4. The exact premises, accuracy and query accounting matter.

The equal-interface baseline queries all M gates and computes S in O(M) arithmetic. The obstruction is exponential in succinct label dimension d but only linear in the explicitly listed graph size; it is not an impossibility against that baseline or against richer certified symbolic access. Known equilibrium, selected coordinates and finite fitted Walsh/locality checks do not certify the missing global rate information. Pairwise microscopic factors do not by themselves bound effective committor/rate elimination width. title: A hidden observation ladder proposes exponential passive versus polynomial controlled inference
text:
N709-hidden-observation-ladder-passive-active-separation | A hidden observation ladder proposes exponential passive versus polynomial controlled inference
status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported mathematical arguments only. Intake checked byte preservation and repository structure; no independent proof reconstruction, scientific-code replay, citation verification, formal proof, statistical sampling assay, or experimental validation was performed. External correctness and historical priority remain UNKNOWN.

Source-reported candidate theorem: for every integer r>=1, an explicit rational finite continuous-time Markov chain Q_r with 4r<=n<=16r, uniform stationary law and balanced binary observation Y_t=f(X_t) has an exponentially hard passive distinction from a stationary equilibrium binary chain of flip rate 1/2, but a polynomial-duration test under a specified conservative-field rate law. All statements use ordinary stationary time reversal with every microscopic state even under physical reversal. Independent correctness and historical priority remain UNKNOWN; no device or transformative technological capability is established.

The positive Walsh lift is Q_r=J-I+epsilon A, epsilon=1/(16r), A^3=0, rank(A)=2r and ||A||_(2->2)=1. With ell=2r-1 and distinct Walsh characters {1,f,c_1,...,c_ell,d_1,...,d_ell}, d_j=f c_j, set Af=d_1, A c_j=d_(j+1) for j<ell, A c_ell=f, and A zero on other characters. A1=A*1=0, ||A||_F^2=2r and ||A-A*||_F^2=4r. The explicit state-basis construction gives 7/(8n)<=q_ij<=9/(8n), exit rate <9/8, reverse-rate ratio <=9/7, total-variation mixing <=exp(-t/2), and all nonzero eigenvalues -1 with Jordan blocks of size at most three. An actual label-preserving state permutation R satisfies RQR=Q*, ensuring an exactly time-reversal-invariant observed path law. R is an auxiliary symmetry, not an alternative physical reversal convention. The source bounds sigma(Q_r) between 1/(144r) and 1/(112r).

Multiplication Dg=fg switches 1 with f and c_j with d_j. A scalar observation word containing A needs at least 2r A-insertions and 2r+1 observations. All joint distributions at <=2r times match the binary equilibrium reference, including C(t)=exp(-t). The first odd moment at t_0<...<t_(2r) is epsilon^(2r) exp[-(t_(2r)-t_0)] product_j(t_j-t_(j-1))>0. This observation-depth statement alone is not the full passive lower bound.

For full continuous records, Q_r=(J-I)/2+B with B=(J-I)/2+epsilon A a valid uniform-stationary generator. Give the observer the independent rate-1/2 reset times as extra information. On each segment the projection/Duhamel series has no contributions of orders 1,...,2r-1, and the state-basis row norm K<=2r bounds the remaining signed terms. The source obtains TV(P_Q^[0,T],P_eq^[0,T])<=(2/3)(1+T/2)16^(-r), covering exact jump times and unlimited processing. Equal-prior success >=2/3 therefore requires the fixed observation horizon T>=16^r-2. This is not a lower bound on expected sequential stopping time. For M independently acquired stationary windows of total length T the bound becomes (2/3)(M+T/2)16^(-r); stationary starts are not free resources. Scaling both generators by r gives sigma in [1/144,1/112], passive horizon >=(16^r-2)/r, controlled unit trial duration 1/r and exit rates O(r).

Essential active interface: q_ij^(h)=q_ij exp[h(f_j-f_i)/2], with diagonal row sums restored, initial zero-field stationarity and symmetric kinetic factors fixed. This law is not determined by passive observations or guaranteed by simply naming a field. The source derives chi_r(t)=1-exp(-t)-(epsilon^2/2)[1-(1+t)exp(-t)], versus chi_eq(t)=1-exp(-t). At t=1 the gap is c_* epsilon^2, c_*=(1-2/e)/2>1/8. Take h=epsilon/100 and finite difference D(h)=[m(h)-m(-h)]/(2h); a third-derivative bound <500 yields bias <=500h^2/6 and a finite-field gap >=13epsilon^2/120>epsilon^2/10. The equilibrium mean is tanh(h)[1-exp(-cosh(h))].

To acquire that distinction rather than assume a susceptibility oracle, estimate each endpoint mean to a=epsilon^3/8000 using N=ceil[(2/a^2)log(8/zeta)] samples per sign. Before every trial, switch the field off and wait L>=2log(8N/zeta); regeneration coupling charges dependent-trial error. The claimed total experiment duration is O(r^6 log(1/zeta)[1+log(r/zeta)]), including the waits, with inverse-polynomial absolute field/timing tolerances epsilon^3/10^8 and polynomially many precision bits. The constants are conservative and large. The archive contains no Monte Carlo implementation of this full sampling protocol. A bound of 2|h| on field-switch work per trial excludes actuator, sensor, calibration and model-construction costs and establishes no total energy advantage.

To exclude a dispensable hidden dissipative subsystem, the source constructs F_+=product_(j=1)^r Y_j and F_-=product_(j=1)^r Y_(-j) with conditional covariance -tau_r given Y_0=-1, tau_r=epsilon^(2r)exp(-2r). Finite reversible hidden deterministic-observation models have nonnegative conditional past/future covariance. For any finite stationary all-even exact hidden realization G, additive reversibilization G_rev=(G+G^dagger)/2 has the same stationary law and exit rates and KL(P_G^L||P_Grev^L)<=L sigma(G)/4. A bounded covariance witness and Pinsker imply sigma(G)>=epsilon^(4r)exp(-4r)/(16r)>0, uniformly over finite hidden dimension and rates. This floor is not sharp and does not estimate the actual dissipation to fixed relative error.

For a finite stationary generator and bounded f under the same rate-perturbation law, the note proposes |chi(t)-[C(0)-C(t)]|^2<=(M^2/2)sigma t Var(f), M=(max f-min f)/2. Balanced binary observations give sigma>=2|response defect|^2/t; the constructed t=1 response supplies an inverse-polynomial floor 2c_*^2 epsilon^4 for models matching both correlation and susceptibility. Promoting finite differences to this derivative certificate also requires a controlled Taylor remainder. This is neither a universal response oracle nor a universal hidden-system inference algorithm.

Resources and robustness: a dense explicit generator uses O(n^2 log(r+2)) bits and O(r n^2) character operations to construct; output and acquisition are charged, not polylogarithmic in r. The exporter uses signed 64-bit integer arrays with overflow guards and quadratic dense output. Reflection-paired ladder amplitudes in [1/2,1] preserve the stated separation up to constants; generic microscopic errors can create shorter observation loops. title: Finite-query noise bridges propose a paid finite-seed simulator for correlated-noise channels
text:

status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported mathematical arguments only. Source-reported computational candidate: for an n-qubit H_X(t)=H_0+sum_(a=1)^r X_a(t)A_a with arbitrary Hermitian noncommuting supplied operators, independent stationary classical OU and/or symmetric telegraph modes, and an input initially independent of the noise, implement the complete noise-averaged channel to diamond error epsilon. With p supplied instruments at prescribed times, adaptive choices based on retained outcomes are allowed, uniformly over controllers unable to inspect the private seed. This is a derived unreviewed construction, not a demonstrated quantum circuit, physical quantum-bath model or universal speedup.

OU modes have dX=-lambda X dt+sqrt(2lambda)dW and covariance exp(-lambda|t-s|), with lambda=0 a static Gaussian. Telegraph modes switch at lambda/2 and have the same covariance, but their joint laws differ. Physical amplitudes belong in A_a. Actual controlled, inverse and indexed implementations of H_0/alpha_0 and A_a/alpha_a, parameter acquisition, selection, coefficient loading and finite precision are charged in C_sel(b). Set S=sum alpha_a and action Acal=1+p+T(alpha_0+S). The proposed gate bound is O-tilde(Acal C_sel+Acal^2)+C_ctrl, hiding fixed polynomials in parameter bits and logarithms of r+2, 1+lambda_max T, 1+Acal and 1/epsilon, with no grid-size power. It does not promise preparation of a full density matrix or fine trajectory.

On M=2^m grid cells, stationary OU endpoints and conditional midpoints are generated by a binary bridge. For half-width h and a=exp(-lambda h), X_mid=a(X_left+X_right)/(1+a^2)+sqrt[(1-a^2)/(1+a^2)]Z_node. Opposite telegraph endpoints give an unbiased midpoint; equal endpoints x give -x with probability (1-a)^2/[2(1+a^2)]. A queried value visits at most m+2 innovations, consistently addressed by mode/tree node, with stable Gaussian recursion 2a/(1+a^2)<=1. This constructs joint laws, not merely covariance; classical virtual Brownian trees are credited prior work.

For coupled paths, diamond error <=2 integral sum alpha_a E|X_a-Y_a| dt, including instruments before conditioning. Let C_G=sum_G alpha_a sqrt(lambda_a), C_R=sum_R alpha_a lambda_a and Delta=T/M. Left-grid error <=2sqrt(2)T sqrt(Delta)C_G+2T Delta C_R. A sufficient grid has M>=C[1+T^3 C_G^2/epsilon^2+T^2 C_R/epsilon], plus M>=C Lambda T(1+p/epsilon) for segmentation/control rounding. The huge grid is represented by log M bits. Finite Gaussian quantiles use antisymmetric rounding, truncation and polynomial-bit inverse-CDF evaluation with mean-zero squared approximation error <=eta^2; unit l2 coefficient sums keep each grid-value error bounded by eta. Finite telegraph thresholds charge log(rM/epsilon) bits without visiting all nodes. A final deterministic Gaussian cap B=ceil(sqrt[2log(64(1+ST)/epsilon)]) gives Lambda=alpha_0+B sum_G alpha_a+sum_R alpha_a. All channel-error estimates are first proved under fully independent innovations.

For piecewise constant cells in a segment d, the ordered k-fold Dyson integral equals d^k/k! times the expectation of the sorted-cell product, including repeated cell indices; no noise differentiability is assumed. Established truncated-Dyson simulation, uniform binary time registers, reversible sorting and oblivious amplification yield q=O[(1+p+Lambda T)log((1+p+Lambda T)/epsilon)] Hamiltonian calls. Padded intervals do not advance the physical noise clock. Including bridge computation and uncomputation gives a fixed innovation-query bound Q=8q(m+2), chosen before the seed family, avoiding a random-budget circularity.

The established bounded-query replacement lemma, also proved in the report by degree-2Q output-density polynomials, says a Q-query quantum circuit has exactly the same averaged output channel under a 2Q-wise independent uniform innovation function as under a fully independent table. It retains references and measurement records, but does not approximate the complete path distribution. A degree-(2Q-1) polynomial over F_(2^b) supplies the function on D=O(r(M+1)) addresses. Uniform coefficient registers remain private; reversible Horner evaluation costs O(Q poly(b)) per call and O(Q^2 poly(b)) total, with O(Qb) seed/workspace. A deterministic quadratic field tower with trace-one elements pays finite-field construction. Scratch is uncomputed so it leaks no extra information outside the query model. Short-seed values need not be globally Gaussian or Markovian; exact circuit-output equality is applied only after the independent-law approximation proof.

Precision b=O[B_in+m+log((r+2)(q+1)(1+ST)/epsilon)] is rounded to a power of two with enlarged arithmetic/synthesis constants. The explicit gate cost is O[q C_sel(b)+Q^2 poly(b)]+C_ctrl, workspace n+O(q a_sel+Q poly(b))+W_ctrl. Coefficient reading, selector compilation and expanded circuit output are charged. For O(n) bounded-locality terms/modes a scan selector costs O(n poly(b)); at T=O(1/J), sigma=O(J), p=O(n), the proposed bound is O-tilde(n^2)+C_ctrl. No QRAM or fine-noise array is assumed. This is a many-body workload, not an exponential advantage inferred from a single-excitation state space.

The same seed persists through interventions, retaining outcome-conditioned future noise memory. With coherent input preparation/inverse cost C_in and bounded effect implementation cost C_F, additive-delta estimation costs O-tilde[(G(delta)+C_in+C_F)delta^-1 log(1/zeta)]; copies-only access instead incurs delta^-2 sampling. Bell preparation/readout for control entanglement fidelity costs O(n) plus the ideal control/inverse. Amplitude estimation acts on the already compiled accurate circuit, not an unlimited noise service. Tiny conditional outputs and full classical tomography remain separately charged.

Competent comparators are explicit: amplitude encodings of stochastic paths are not free coherent binary-value oracles; Gaussian pseudomodes may be preferable and do not automatically reproduce non-Gaussian telegraph laws. Telegraph noise has an exact r-qubit Markovian embedding with H_ext=H_0+sum A_a tensor Z_a and L_a=sqrt(lambda_a/2)X_a, with general normalized Lindblad time T(alpha_0+S+sum lambda_a/2). The candidate trades quadratic Hamiltonian action for removal of leading switching-rate cost in its uniform upper bound. Moderate rates or certified fast-noise averaging can favor specialized methods. No lower-bound separation or superiority over all specialized algorithms is proved.

Independent signs and (a,b,ab) have identical one/two-variable marginals but three commuting sign pulses give order-one channel discrepancy; resetting a static Gaussian each cell removes dephasing; a short-seed full table can be far from the independent law; and fixed integrated white-noise strength makes amplitudes grow as sqrt(lambda). These failures delimit the operation. Prescribed classical noise is not a finite-temperature quantum bath with backreaction/detailed balance. Parameter learning, hardware-oracle certification, full circuit execution and formal verification remain absent. The exact prompt/process/report and recovered citation targets are preserved without repairing the pasted source. Reported small diagnostics are not independent general-proof or priority evidence. text:

status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported mathematical arguments only. Source-reported global theorem candidate: distinct canonical-sign nonidentity Pauli strings P_a on n qubits, support size <=k and candidate incidence max_i #{a:i in supp P_a}<=Delta (including zero-coefficient candidates), H(h)=sum h_a P_a with max_i sum_(a:i in supp P_a)|h_a|<=g, beta>0 and an unrestricted full-rank Gibbs state rho_h. For every real u, A=sum u_aP_a and A_c=A-Tr(rho A)I, the manuscript proposes centered KMS norm squared >=c||u||_2^2 and therefore BKM covariance >=c||u||_2^2, c=exp[-C_(k,Delta)(1+beta g)^2]. C is finite/constructive, independent of n,m, signs, gaps and mixing, but potentially extremely conservative. No commutation, frustration exclusion, high temperature or correlation-decay assumption is made. This is an unreviewed derivation with unknown independent correctness/priority, not a validated new physical law or end-to-end learning advantage.

This directly follows up N705's recorded global cancellation obstruction. The earlier local spectral-multiplicity theorem is reproved in the new manuscript; the N705 unreviewed card is not assumed as a proof premise. A reciprocal continuation notice exposes the candidate follow-up while preserving N705's original source, claim status and historical unresolved gate. The newer proposed proof does not certify closure of that independent-review obligation and does not invalidate the earlier local theorem or its dimension counterexample.

With Hhat=H/g and b=beta g (the g=0 case handled directly), one-site Pauli commutators are supported on at most s=1+Delta(k-1) sites. The reconstructed local input gives kappa_b=4exp(-4bs)/(9*2^s), and Pauli orthogonality yields sum_(i,alpha)||[Q_(i,alpha),A]||_K^2>=8 kappa_b||u||_2^2. This gradient floor alone does not prevent global cancellation.

Gaussian-filtered B_(j,omega)=(2pi)^(-1/2)integral exp(-t^2/2-iomega t) exp(it Hhat)Q_j exp(-it Hhat)dt satisfy exp(zHhat)B_omega exp(-zHhat)=exp(zomega+z^2/2)B_(omega+z). The exact KMS adjoint of partial_omega(X)=[B_omega,X] is exp(-bomega/2+b^2/8)B_(-omega+b/2)Y-exp(bomega/2+b^2/8)Y B_(-omega-b/2). With w_b=exp[-(1+b)|omega|], G_j=integral w_b partial^sharp partial and G=sum_j G_j are exactly KMS self-adjoint, positive in that inner product and annihilate I. -G need not be completely positive, physical or rapidly mixing; those properties are not used to infer information.

On the bounded-degree candidate graph, Gaussian-filtered operators have radius-r approximants with arbitrarily fast fixed exponential spatial decay, at large size-independent prefactor. Short-imaginary-time nested-commutator bounds combine with spatial estimates to give joint shells <=C exp(-mu r)exp(-a|omega|), a=1/(8k). A Schur bound on K_(ia)=exp[-mu dist(i,S_a)] gives the coefficient-l2 residual sum_j||[R_(j,Omega),A]||_K^2<=T_const^2 exp(-2aOmega)||u||_2^2, without an n||u||_infinity^2 loss. Choosing Omega_b=O_(k,Delta)(1+b) yields D(A)=<A,GA>_K>=eta_b||u||_2^2 with eta_b=2kappa_b/L_(b,Omega_b)^2, L^2=(exp[(1+b)Omega]-1)/(pi(1+b)).

The decisive image lemma controls G on the bounded-incidence local interaction space. In <G_iP_a,G_jP_c>_K move the exact thermal adjoint first, giving <P_a,G_iG_jP_c>_K, then replace by disjoint local approximants whose product on P_c vanishes. Spatial errors and bounded graph volume make the transformed Gram rows summable; ordinary thermal covariance decay is not assumed. The proposed bound is ||GA||_K^2<=B_0 exp(b^2/4)||u||_2^2. Cauchy--Schwarz with GI=0 gives ||A_c||_K^2>=eta_b^2||u||_2^2/[B_0 exp(b^2/4)] and BKM dominates KMS by logarithmic/geometric means. The manuscript supplies explicit tail/image estimates, disconnected-component treatment and a sequential constant-construction recipe; intake has not independently verified them. The image lemma does not bound G on all operators.

Weighted-strength-only obstruction: for fixed beta,h,lambda>0, H_N=-h sum_(i=0)^N Z_i-(lambda/N)Z_0 sum_(j=1)^N Z_j, with all displayed couplings nonzero and incident strength <=h+lambda. Set t=tanh(beta h), A_N=N^-1 sum Z_0Z_j-tZ_0. Its coefficient norm squared is t^2+1/N, while commuting BKM variance <=1/N+(beta lambda)^2/N^2. The ratio tends to zero. This is a classical two-local counterexample with growing center incidence; it excludes weighted strength alone, not the bounded-candidate-incidence theorem.

On a convex coefficient domain satisfying the common strength bound, F=log Tr exp(-beta H) has Hessian >=beta^2 c I, ||h-h'||_2<=||m(h)-m(h')||_2/(beta c), and D(rho_h||rho_h')>=beta^2 c||h-h'||_2^2/2. The original local moments jointly identify coefficients with no additional system-size inverse-Lipschitz loss. Candidate overlap coloring chi<=k(Delta-1)+1 allows disjoint Pauli supports to be measured together with single-qubit basis measurements. Total l2 coefficient error <=epsilon is proposed with O[chi*m/(beta^2 c^2 epsilon^2)log(2m/p)] independent Gibbs copies; for RMS coefficient error m^(-1/2)||hhat-h||_2<=epsilon the m factor disappears. This is not a uniform per-coefficient infinity-norm guarantee.

Acquisition, computation and bit costs remain separate. Gibbs copies must actually be prepared independently and readout/model bias controlled. Dense F/gradient evaluation uses dimension 2^n, illustrative O(8^n+m4^n) arithmetic operations and O(4^n) memory, not a bit-complexity advantage. Inexact gradients need an error budget tied to beta^2 c epsilon. A polynomial count of ideal gradient calls for fixed physical parameters can still require exponentially expensive calls. No generic efficient preparation, complete reconstruction or superiority over current arbitrary-temperature algorithms is established.

The source compares only specified bounds: the 2021 Anshu--Arunachalam--Kuwahara--Soleimanifar geometric-lattice Hessian with 1/m loss, and Learning SYK Hamiltonians Appendix D/Theorem D.1 with 1/[m(1+log(2m))] loss for bounded incidence, not dense SYK. It credits prior commuting/high-temperature conditioning, arbitrary-temperature learning, KMS/Fourier technology and finite-range Lieb--Robinson arguments. Bergamaschi's stationarity entropy-production Fisher information is a different functional from equilibrium BKM covariance. Exact literature versions and applicability are preserved in the original bibliography, not independently cleared by intake.

One-qubit sech^2(beta h) suppression forbids temperature-independent or polynomial-beta universal floors; the quadratic exponent is not claimed optimal. The theorem neither bounds the largest covariance eigenvalue nor proves clustering or absence of phase transitions. A fixed-charge sector has exact null directions outside the unrestricted Gibbs interface. Growing degree, constrained systems and better coefficient geometry need new theorems. The original recovered ZIP, LaTeX, PDF, script and recorded six algebraic/quadrature, 24 covariance and seven analytic-star checks remain exact producer artifacts. status=source_derived_unreviewed; Source-reported mathematical arguments only. Candidate scope: H(h)=H_bg+sum_a h_a P_a, with distinct canonical nonidentity Pauli parameter strings, support<=k and candidate incidence<=Delta including zero coefficients. At the operating point the full H has support<=ell and per-site incident operator-norm strength<=g; the fixed background need not have bounded combinatorial degree. The state is an unrestricted full-rank Gibbs state at known beta>0. No commutation, lattice, high-temperature, clustering, gap or mixing hypothesis is imposed. The result concerns equilibrium Hamiltonian-parameter Fisher information, not unitary phase encoding or simultaneous multiparameter SLD attainability.

One fixed parameter-independent protocol measures independent uniformly random X/Y/Z bases on each independent Gibbs copy, retaining bases and outcomes. Detector sign errors must be independently calibrated across sites and copies, with visibility eta_i>=eta>0 and no parameter dependence; quantum outcomes need not be independent. The unbiased feature is Y_a=product_{i in S_a}(3 s_i/eta_i)1{basis_i=(P_a)_i}. Let C be BKM covariance, V=Cov(Y), F_loc the full recorded classical Fisher matrix and F_Q the SLD matrix. Proof spine: measurement covariance excess N=V-V_q is positive and exactly zero between disjoint supports, preserving long-range quantum correlations; overlap counting bounds its row sums. The established Brooks-Harris inequality bounds V_q-C by beta/12 times the thermal double commutator. Support/weighted-strength Schur counting gives W<=4g k(k+ell)Delta I. Gibbs response Cov(Y,score)=-beta C and a Schur complement transfer covariance to actual information. C(C+R)^(-1)C-(C-R)=R(C+R)^(-1)R>=0 needs no commutation. For u with ||u||_2^2=O(n), additional optimal quantum readout information is at most O(n). If u^T F_Q u/||u||^2 diverges with beta,g,k,ell,Delta,eta fixed, the local/optimal information ratio tends to one; enhanced scaling itself is not guaranteed. With f=u dot Y, v=Var(f), q=||u||^2, (v-nu q)_+<=u^T C u<=v. Thus beta^2(v-nu q)_+^2/v<=u^T F_loc u<=u^T F_Q u<=beta^2 v, lower endpoint zero if v=0. The same variance gives static-susceptibility bounds. The scalar sample mean is asymptotically competitive at enhanced response, with the displayed locally unbiased estimator requiring separately acquired reference mean and slope; finite-displacement bias is outside its variance formula.

Acquisition: |f|<=L_u=(3/eta)^k||u||_1. Paired independent samples Z=(f_1-f_2)^2/2 estimate v; M>=2 L_u^4 zeta^(-2) log(2/p) pairs suffice for additive variance error zeta at failure p. Independent maximally mixed Z-field qubits have fixed-readout loss proportional to n. Positive additive protection does not prevent a poorly conditioned direction from remaining poorly conditioned.

For an explicitly represented finite source-target DAG with independent exponential activity durations, strictly positive rational rates and a rational deadline T supplied exactly in binary, the manuscript proposes a randomized polynomial-bit algorithm for U=Pr(longest source-target duration >=T). For rational epsilon>0 and 0<delta<1 it would output a binary rational ell with Pr[|ell-ln U|<=epsilon]>=1-delta when U>0, in time/bit work polynomial in graph size, total input bits, 1/epsilon and log(1/delta). It outputs -infinity for U=0 and ell=0 for T<=0 when a path exists. Missing path means U=0 by convention; for T>0 zero-only paths do not contribute. It computes log U without materializing a potentially enormous probability denominator. This is a proof candidate, not validated software or an established algorithmic advance.

Mechanism: order relevant activities by (rate,index), partition paths by their minimum-rate anchor, and use a topological skip/select scan rather than scanning in rate order. At most 2n union components comprise anchored overruns A_i with all other class coordinates <T, and single-activity tails B_j={X_j>=T}. For anchor rate lambda, integrate X_i exactly: Pr(A_i)=exp(-lambda T) product_j C_j * p_i, C_j=lambda_j integral_0^T exp[-(lambda_j-lambda)x]dx. The remaining independent q_j densities on [0,T] are decreasing (uniform at equal rates). With S the sum of class non-anchor coordinates and L the longest class path excluding the anchor, R=S-min(L,T)>=0 and p_i=E_q exp(-lambda R)=Pr[omitted path cost<=E AND S<=T+E], E~Exp(lambda). For m non-anchor coordinates p_i>=rho=1/[4 max(1,m lambda T)^m]; rho has polynomial encoding length, not necessarily inverse-polynomial numerical size. m=0 is handled directly.

The crucial smoothing is Pr_q[D(ae,ab)]>=a^m Pr_q[D(e,b)] for 0<a<=1, where D is the downward event with omitted and total resource budgets. It uses decreasing continuous densities and simultaneous scaling BEFORE atomization. It is not a theorem for arbitrary finite-atomic two-budget laws or the original heterogeneous tail. Comparator discretization has step tau/lambda and polynomially many cells from log(1/(tau rho)). Atomization clamps below ell_grid=tau rho/(m d_max), uses g=1+tau/[10m(m+1)] exactly, and rounds both cumulative resources upward. Each resource is bounded by g^(m+1) times its exact value outside the charged small-coordinate event. Retain the first resource point >=2mT, plus zero and absorbing overflow rejection. Endpoint, anchor phase and zero-connector epsilon-elimination preserve path legality and one read per independent activity; no path enumeration or subset determinization is assumed.

Dyadic coordinate laws need polynomial ABSOLUTE precision depending on log(1/rho); use disjoint integer-interval binary decoders with a common denominator 2^b. An ordinary polynomial-size NFA at a polynomial unary word length counts accepted words ONCE, not nondeterministic accepting runs. The sole stated external algorithmic theorem is Arenas–Croquevielle–Jayaram–Riveros #NFA FPRAS (JACM 2021). Conditional generation may self-reduce prefix counts. Jitter accepted atoms under original truncated densities and comparator cells, then set X_i=(T-L)_+ +Z, Z~Exp(lambda), and draw outside-class coordinates from their original laws. A component-weighted union estimator averages 1/M(X) over true containing components, at most K<=2n; log-scale weights avoid huge denominators. Approximate counts, conditional laws, membership failures, concentration and final logarithms have separate budgets. The K symbol for comparator cells in Section 4 is distinct from the union-component K elsewhere.

Density/conditioning bounds and a union bound over at most 2^n path edge sets give u=zeta rho/[100 n 2^n D] of polynomial bit length for unambiguous membership outside charged exceptions. Coordinates, longest paths and shifted anchors use enclosing intervals; inverse CDF, exponent/log cutoffs, tails, near-equal rates and confidence amplification are charged. On its communicating killed domain, the source uses symmetry and the maximum principle to bound G(z,u)<=G(z,z)<=1/(2w), because the initial adjacent pair has direct killing rate 2w. These are different sides; generic Markov chains do not inherit the inversion step. Because A_e^2=2A_e, Duhamel sensitivity at time one has TV derivative <=integral_0^1 a_w(s)a_w(1-s)ds. Every vacuum multi-time word with at most k creation and k annihilation fields therefore agrees for all times and labelled linear combinations. An r-particle probe distinguishes them. A justified fixed total Q replaces full-Fock N=n by at most min(n,Q). Exact statement: For each m>=2 and R>0, one smooth radial strictly log-concave all-exponential scalar density positively regularizes every bounded self-adjoint m-tuple, on every Hilbert space, with ||sum u_j A_j||<=R|u|, and attains the largest eventual radial tail-envelope fixed offset b*=log[2/(R(m-1))]-1 in p(x)~C exp[-r/(2R)(log r+loglog r+b*)]. At that sharp offset the lower relative margin tends to zero in remote tails; the separate basic-endpoint epsilon sandwich must not be imported. Separately, for Mhat(t)=nuhat(t)exp(i t.sigma) for all three normalized Pauli observables, every radial positive scalar finite-variance law has covariance v I with v>=v*=23/9-2/[9(4K+2)], where K=integral_1^infinity h0, h0=1 on [0,2], and 2(s-1)h0'(s)+h0(s)+h0(s-2)=0 thereafter. Centering and rotations give tr Cov(nu)>=3v* for arbitrary scalar laws. Positive renewal attains v*; smooth spatial densities have the same infimum without attainment. Its multiplier obeys [3/(2080 sqrt2)]/(1+k^2)<=phi(k)<=2/(1+k^2), hence scalar convolution is H^s(R^3)->H^(s+2)(R^3) isomorphic. Separately, compact Banach-cone distributions admit precisely the proved open convex finite-MGF domains, and weighted-tempered (W) distributions admit the stated noncompact all-exponential criterion. As a separately identified classical boundary, an exact all-linear positive POVM representation with compact scalar noise exists for a bounded self-adjoint tuple on an arbitrary Hilbert space if and only if the operators commute pairwise. For each fixed valid exact representation, compact noise and compact outcome support are equivalent; commuting tuples may still have noncompact representations. This is an internally reconstructed short corollary of Uchiyama 1993 Theorem 7, with two direct internal proofs, not a historically new all-Hilbert-space theorem or foundational breakthrough.
Source-reported status: UNKNOWN: mixed incoming producer and internal research statuses remain in their exact cited originals; no aggregate producer status inferred.
Assumptions: Endpoint: finite m, R>0, bounded self-adjoint tuple with the exact norm-ball contract; 0<epsilon<1 and the proof-specified sufficient scale.; Domain theorem: compactly supported real Banach-valued distribution, closed proper cone with nonempty interior, T(1)=e interior, and open convex D containing zero with transform interior on D.; Noncompact theorem: the full weighted (W) distributional seminorm hypothesis and T(1)=e; do not substitute arbitrary temperedness or all-noise exclusion.; Sharp offset: m>=2 and the exact universal radial eventual-envelope contract, with finite multiplicative constant; no uniform relative epsilon margin at that offset.; Pauli optimum: all three normalized coordinates, exact full scalar-convolution identity, positive scalar law/POVM and finite variance. Attainer is singular like 1/r; smooth subclass nonattainment is separate.; Compact-noise characterization uses the full exact all-linear multiplier identity and normalized weak POVM. Bounded noise in one direction plus all positive exponential moments in a second direction forces the corresponding commutator to vanish; finite Fourier-grid accuracy does not supply those tilted moments.
